items.title: Contributing to PRESTUS
items.text:
Thank you for your interest in contributing to the open-source development of PRESTUS!

We welcome all types of contributions, including code submissions, documentation, tests, and feedback.

PRESTUS emerged from the need for tailored simulation solutions in the realm of transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) research. As TUS research advances, new equipment and experimental paradigm requirements continually arise, often outpacing the capabilities of existing simulation tools. PRESTUS was developed to address these challenges by providing a flexible set of functions for ultrasonic simulations. This adaptability allows researchers to efficiently prototype, test, and refine simulation workflows that are responsive to the unique and evolving demands of their studies.

Your contributions help maintain and usefully expand this evolving tool for the non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) community.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
• Fork the repository and clone it locally.
  • Install dependencies as described in README.md.
  • Please review open issues and discussions to avoid duplicating work and to align with ongoing development.

items.title: Coding Standards
items.text:
PRESTUS is a research tool, and we strive for transparency, reproducibility, and clarity—even if the workflows are evolving and at times built for specific use cases in scientific work. Please consider the following guiding principles:

  • Motivation: When proposing changes, open an issue or comment on an existing one to describe the scientific or technical motivation behind your contribution.
  • Documentation: Clearly document any new features, changes, or known limitations directly in the code and in your pull request description. If your contribution addresses messy or ambiguous data, describe your approach and any assumptions made.
  • Reproducibility: Strive to make your changes as reproducible as possible. If you use external data, scripts, or parameters, provide instructions or references so others can replicate your results.
  • Transparency: If your solution involves workarounds, non-standard methods, or "messy" scientific practices, explain these choices in your code comments and pull request. This helps future users and contributors understand the context and rationale.
  • Code Quality: Write clear, descriptive commit messages. Limit the impact of your updates to the target features/fixes, and minimize unintended effects on other workflows or users.
  • Backward Compatibility: Remain backward-compatible where possible. If not feasible, document the necessary changes and impacts in your code, issue, and pull request.
  • Data Handling: If your contribution involves new datasets or changes to data processing, include metadata and a description of data provenance, quality, and any preprocessing steps.

items.title: How to Submit Changes
items.text:
• Create a new branch for your feature or fix.
  • Ensure (to the best of your ability) that your features work as expected and the pipeline remains functional. Unit tests have not yet been implemented, so please verify your changes manually and describe your testing process.
  • Submit a pull request to the development branch with a clear description. Before this pull request can be accepted, it will need to be reviewed by another contributor.
  • [Optional] Attach a log or summary to the pull request, stating that the "pipeline has finished successfully" or describing any issues encountered.
  • [Optional] Add yourself to the contributor list in the readme (you will automatically be recognized by GitHub's contribution tracker). Follow these instructions.

items.title: Code of Conduct
items.text: Please read our Code of Conduct before contributing.

items.title: Contact
items.text: If you have questions, please open an issue.

items.title: Advanced Modelling
items.text:
A single PRESTUS run simulates one transducer setup at one intensity with one set of tissue properties. The modes on this page run several related simulations from one config, so that a result can be bracketed across tissue property bounds, compared across intensities, combined across transducers or carried from one sonication into the next.

On this page:

  • Advanced simulation modes: the four modes, each with its own page, and how they combine.
  • Iterating parameters: varying other settings across runs from a MATLAB script.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To bracket a safety estimate, compare intensities, model two transducers, or carry heat from one sonication into the next.
  • Before you start: A working single-run study config (Your first simulation).

items.title: Advanced Simulation Modes
items.text:
Each mode is documented on its own page:

Mode Description Uncertainty Run the default medium and four ITRUSST-bound variants (Temp-H/L, Trans-H/L) to bracket plausible heating and in-situ intensity Multi-Intensity Scale one acoustic simulation to multiple target ISPPAs in parallel Multi-Transducer Coherent or asynchronous multi-transducer simulations Sequential Chain simulations so that each run inherits the thermal state of the previous one

Modes can be combined: uncertainty + sequential, multi-intensity + uncertainty, async multi-transducer + multi-intensity sweep. Composition rules and affix conventions are described on each mode's page, with combined-affix examples in Sequential: Output affix handling.

items.title: Iterating Parameters
items.text:
A study config specifies a single setup: transducer, entry-target points and temporal sequence. To explore the effect of a parameter, for benchmarking or for choosing a stimulation sequence, work from one study config (Your first simulation) and overwrite values in a MATLAB script, setting parameters.<field> per iteration.

The exception is the intensity and depth setting of the transducer output, which depend on the transducer calibration. Where the built-in profiling does not provide sufficient flexibility, use calibration_transducer within an iterative MATLAB loop to find phase and amplitude settings that replicate the desired free-water output profile (Transducer Calibration).

items.title: How PRESTUS Works
items.text:
A PRESTUS result depends not only on your study config but also on the config layers merged beneath it, on where the run executed and on which cached stage outputs it reused. This page shows how a run is put together, so that you can trace a value or a result to the stage that produced it, and change the pipeline without breaking the conventions that keep results consistent.

On this page:

  • Overview and Entry Points: the path from config to outputs and the entry-point functions.
  • Configuration Layers: the four config layers, the steps after merging and which keys count as known.
  • Run Execution and Chained Jobs: local runs, cluster jobs and the chained pipelines that split a run into several jobs.
  • Pipeline Stages: what each stage reads, writes and caches, and the functions behind it.
  • Caches and Reuse: when a cache is reused, how its settings are checked, and starting from an earlier run's outputs.
  • Intensity Scaling: how results are scaled to the free-water target ISPPA, also with several transducers.
  • Acoustic and Thermal Backends: how the solver is selected and dispatched.
  • Logging and Provenance: output folders, logs, parameter snapshots and provenance records.
  • Checklist for Code Changes: what to update for a new key, function or stage, and the checks to run before committing.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When you debug a run or change the pipeline. For the stage switches see Modules; for every parameter see Parameters.
  • Before you start: Nothing; this is a reference page for contributors and advanced users.

items.title: Overview and Entry Points
items.text:
config YAML(s) ──► load_parameters ──► prestus_pipeline_start ──► prestus_pipeline ──► outputs
                    (merge, validate)    (where to run)             (stages 1-12)        CSV, NIfTI, HTML,
                                                                                         cache/, log/

Entry points:

Function Use prestus_pipeline_start(parameters) One subject: runs locally or submits an HPC job. prestus_study_start(config) Many subjects/conditions from a study manifest; one prestus_pipeline_start per row (Group analysis). prestus_group_report_start(config) Group maps and report from finished runs. prestus_nexus Desktop app that writes the study config and starts the above (Nexus). prestus_pipeline(parameters) The stages themselves (called by the above; call it directly only for debugging).

All MATLAB code is under functions/<subsystem>/; Functions lists every function by subsystem.

items.title: Configuration Layers
items.text:
The user-facing description is Configuring a study. load_parameters builds one parameters struct from up to four layers, each merged onto the previous one (mergestruct + restore_struct_arrays, so struct arrays such as transducer(2) keep their own fields):

Layer Source Notes 1. Toolbox defaults config/config_default.yaml Always loaded first. 2. Project defaults config_default.yaml next to the study config (or in the folder passed as second argument, or the current folder) Copied by prestus_config_init to pin defaults. Keys added to the toolbox since the copy was made fall back to layer 1, with the warning prestus:staleProjectDefault; prestus_config_upgrade refreshes the copy. Using the current folder's copy warns (prestus:cwdDefault). 3. Study config(s) the YAML file(s) or struct passed in YAML keys PRESTUS does not know warn (prestus:unknownConfigKey, with a suggestion for typos). 4. Overrides trailing {'dotted.key', value; ...} cell e.g. one row of a study manifest (apply_config_overrides). Post-merge steps

After merging, load_parameters migrates deprecated keys, derives transducer parameters (load_transducer_parameters, which also resolves transducer.serial against the equipment library), validates the timing protocol, sanitises io.output_affix into a BIDS _desc-<label> entity, and validates backends. Missing tool paths (hpc.ld_library_path, startup.simnibs_bin_path) prompt only in an interactive desktop session with simulation.interactive: 1; otherwise they warn, so batch and HPC runs never wait on a dialog.

Known keys

A key is known when the merged defaults contain it, or when it is listed under extra: or deprecated: in nexus/prestus_nexus/overlay.yaml: keys the code reads that config_default.yaml omits. That list is shared by MATLAB (config_known_extra_keys) and the Nexus, and the Nexus drift test checks that every entry is still read by functions/.

items.title: Run Execution and Chained Jobs
items.text:
prestus_pipeline_start resolves platform (auto detects SLURM or qsub via hpc_detect_system, and errors when neither is on the PATH):

  • matlab: runs in the current session.
  • slurm / qsub: saves parameters to a temporary .mat, writes a small .m launcher that adds the PRESTUS paths and calls prestus_pipeline, and submits it (hpc_submit_job; SLURM via sbatch --parsable). With hpc.wait_for_job it blocks until the job ends (hpc_wait_for_completion); otherwise it submits a dependent report job (hpc_job_report: run time, memory, energy).

Three chained pipelines split one run into several jobs that pass results through caches:

Mode Triggered by Function Stages Async multi-transducer simulation.transducer_coupling: async and >1 transducer async_transducer_pipeline shared preprocessing → one acoustic job per transducer → incoherent combination → thermal Multi-intensity transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 is a vector multi_isppa_pipeline one acoustic job with free-water baseline → one thermal job per intensity (field rescaled) → summary Uncertainty simulation.uncertainty: 1 uncertainty_pipeline shared preprocessing → one job per medium-property variant → uncertainty report

resolve_chained_overwrite maps io.overwrite_files onto these: always re-runs the output stages but resumes the intermediate ones from cache; force re-runs everything.

items.title: Pipeline Stages
items.text:
prestus_pipeline calls one function per stage and passes the stage outputs explicitly; no stage reads another stage's variables from a global. Positions are converted between coordinate systems at fixed points only: RAS mm → T1 voxels once in the placement stage (ras_to_grid), T1 voxels → grid voxels in the grid stage, and back for NIfTI export. See Coordinate systems before changing any transform.

Data passed between stages Variable Contents Produced by parameters Configuration plus derived values: grid.dims, transducer positions in grid voxels, io.dir_* output folders, state.* flags load_parameters, then updated by most stages planimg Planning image (T1) header and the transforms between T1 voxels and the simulation grid grid stage segmentation, medium_masks Tissue labels on the grid, and their mapping to medium_properties layers grid stage kwave_medium Sound speed, density, attenuation (and thermal properties in medium_plus) on the grid medium stage kgrid, source, sensor k-Wave grid, source and sensor source stage acoustic_provenance Free-water baseline ISPPA and its origin, calibration, FOV offsets baseline + acoustic stage sensor_data p_max_all, p_min_all, p_final (scaled to the target ISPPA) acoustic stage fov_state Full-grid copies when the acoustic run uses a cropped field of view FOV crop

parameters.state records what is available downstream: acoustics_available, heating_available, acoustic_dry_run (a backend wrote its inputs but did not simulate), and planned_trans_t1_vox / planned_focus_t1_vox (planned positions in T1 voxels, kept for the targeting analysis because the grid stage replaces trans_pos/focus_pos with grid indices).

Stage inputs and outputs # Stage Reads Writes / caches 1 Segmentation T1 (T2) m2m_sub-XXX/ (governed by io.overwrite_simnibs) 2 Placement placement.*, Localite/heuristic/MNI/PlanTUS inputs transducer(i).trans_pos/focus_pos in T1 voxels; placement report 3 Grid T1, segmentation, pseudo-CT cache/…_grid_cache…mat (io.save_grid_cache), …_planimg…mat sidecar 4 Medium masks, medium_properties, pseudo-CT cache/…_medium_cache…mat (io.save_medium_cache); property NIfTIs – FOV crop grid.acoustic_fov_* cropped medium and positions; fov_state 5 Source transducer geometry, drive cache/…_kwave_source…mat – Free-water baseline source, water properties acoustic_provenance.freefield_isppa_wcm2, freefield_source 6 Acoustic medium, source, sensor cache/…_results…mat (cache_acoustic) 7 Acoustic analysis sensor_data, masks …<affix>.csv, intensity/pressure/MI NIfTIs, …_targeting.csv 8 Thermal acoustic field, timing protocol cache/…_heating_res…mat 9 Thermal analysis heating results thermal columns in the CSV, temperature/CEM43 NIfTIs 10 Reports all outputs …_report…html 11 Post-hoc water same transducer a water run per transducer 12 Sequential options.sequential_configs follow-up run starting from this run's end temperature Stage functions # Stage Function(s) 1 Segmentation preproc_segmentation (SimNIBS charm) 2 Placement preproc_transducer_placement → position_transducer_* 3 Grid grid_stage → grid_tissue_setup, autopad_grid_for_transducers, grid_transducer_location, grid_axisymmetry 4 Medium medium_stage → medium_setup; nifti_medium – FOV crop acoustic_fov_crop 5 Source coherent_drive_calibration (coherent, >1 transducer); source_sensor_setup → source_create; checkStability – Free-water baseline acoustic_water_baseline → needs_water_baseline, water_baseline 6 Acoustic acoustic_stage → run_acoustic_backend (acoustic_wrapper / jwave_wrapper / babelbrain_wrapper); apply_isppa_scaling 7 Acoustic analysis acoustic_analysis; nifti_acoustic; targeting_analysis 8 Thermal thermal_stage → thermal_simulation (k-Wave kWaveDiffusion) or babelbrain_thermal_wrapper 9 Thermal analysis thermal_analysis; nifti_thermal 10 Reports generate_simulation_report (+ group, multi-intensity, uncertainty) 11 Post-hoc water prestus_pipeline_start with simulation.medium: water 12 Sequential sequential_pipeline

items.title: Caches and Reuse
items.text:
Every expensive stage writes a cache under cache/ named sub-XXX_<medium>_<stage>…<affix>.mat (the full list is under Output directory structure). Whether a cache is reused is decided by io.overwrite_files (confirm_overwriting): never reuses, always/force recompute, anything else asks in interactive sessions.

Caches are for re-runs of the same run. A separate run starts from an earlier run's stage outputs instead: the SimNIBS segmentation (path.seg), the pseudo-CT (pseudoCT.json), a placement run (placement_run.json, placement.reuse) and the T1w pressure map (path.acoustic_input, LOAD_ACOUSTIC_INPUT). See Starting from earlier stage outputs.

Cache signatures and sidecars

Because cache names do not encode the settings, a reused cache could silently ignore a changed setting. Grid, medium and acoustic caches therefore store the settings they depend on (cache_signature) and compare them on reuse (check_cache_signature, io.cache_signature_check); see Cache reuse checks. The acoustic cache also checks that its grid size matches the current grid (cache_acoustic:staleGrid) and re-runs the acoustic simulation otherwise. A run that reuses another run's grid cache (io.preproc_affix, io.reuse_upstream_caches) keeps its own transducer settings (drive, phases, ISPPA targets) and takes only the grid-space positions from the cache (load_grid_cache_file). Likewise it keeps its own grid settings (e.g. a partial acoustic FOV, grid.acoustic_fov_*) and takes only what the grid stage computes (dims, default_dims, resolution_mm, display_orientation). Pipeline sub-jobs that reuse their own stage-0 caches (io.reuse_upstream_caches) skip the signature check.

Each stage output, except the standard SimNIBS output, has a JSON sidecar (write_sidecar) recording the settings it depends on, compared on reuse by check_sidecar_signature under the same io.cache_signature_check.

Adding a reusable stage output

A new reusable stage output gets a sidecar written with write_sidecar and a signature of the settings it depends on.

items.title: Intensity Scaling
items.text:
Simulations run at the drive elem_p_amp; results are reported at the free-water ISPPA transducer.target_isppa_wcm2, by scaling pressure with sqrt(target / baseline). The baseline comes from a free-water simulation of the same source (modules.run_water_baseline: auto runs it when needed) or from a matching library calibration. A target that cannot be met stops the run rather than being reported unscaled. See ISPPA targeting.

With several transducers each target is that transducer's own free-water ISPPA. Coherent runs cannot scale the combined field per transducer, so coherent_drive_calibration sets each transducer's elem_p_amp before the source is built (baseline: the transducer alone in water, or its matching calibration) and apply_isppa_scaling leaves the result unscaled (acoustic_provenance.coherent_drive). Async runs scale each field in combine_async_intensity. See Multi-transducer: ISPPA targets.

items.title: Acoustic and Thermal Backends
items.text: acoustic_backend (kwave, jwave, babelbrain) and thermal_backend (kwave, babelbrain) select the solver; everything before and after the solver call is shared. run_acoustic_backend dispatches the acoustic call, so a fresh run and a re-run after a stale cache use the same backend and the same scaling. simulation.code_type selects k-Wave's MATLAB or C++ code on CPU or GPU. See Backends and k-Wave.

items.title: Logging and Provenance
items.text: path_log_setup creates the per-subject output folders (io.dir_*), starts a MATLAB diary in log/, writes a parameters snapshot to cache/ and a human-readable resolved-parameters YAML to log/. The acoustic cache carries acoustic_provenance (baseline ISPPA and its source, calibration, BabelBrain version). Errors close the diary and are rethrown with their identifier; opt-in anonymous usage statistics record the run's outcome (Telemetry).

items.title: Checklist for Code Changes
items.text:
• New config key: add it with a comment to config/config_default.yaml and a row to Parameters. If the code reads a key that config_default.yaml does not define, list it under extra: in nexus/prestus_nexus/overlay.yaml, so that neither MATLAB nor the Nexus reports it as unknown.
  • New function: start the file with a help line % NAME Short description; tests/docs/gen_function_index.py adds it to Functions.
  • New stage or behaviour: add a test at the right level (Testing), and for anything that changes numbers a physics or golden-metric check.
  • Before committing, run the checks that CI runs:
python tests/docs/gen_function_index.py --check
python tests/docs/check_param_docs.py
python tests/docs/check_links.py
mkdocs build --strict -d /tmp/prestus-site
(cd nexus && python -m pytest -q -m "not matlab")
matlab -batch "cd tests; run_all_tests('unit')"

items.title: BabelBrain Backend
items.text:
BabelBrain solves the wave equation with a staggered-grid FDTD solver, a different numerical method from k-Wave's pseudo-spectral solver, and PRESTUS gives it the same drive phases and tissue properties. Comparing a BabelBrain run of the same setup with a k-Wave run indicates how far a result depends on the solver. With thermal_backend: babelbrain it also computes the heating, with BabelBrain's own tissue thermal properties.

On this page:

  • Quick Start: selecting the backend and its Python environment.
  • Installation: the submodule and conda environment.
  • Comparison with k-Wave: solver differences and which tissue properties reach BabelBrain.
  • BabelBrain Output Folder: the input package for running BabelBrain on its own.
  • Tissue Labels and Material Properties: label mapping, CT-based skull properties and internal air.
  • Transducer Mapping: how PRESTUS transducers map to BabelBrain presets.
  • Calibration Weights: element phases and the free-water amplitude calibration.
  • Thermal Simulation: BabelBrain heating, its timing and its tissue thermal properties.
  • Limitations and Unsupported PRESTUS Modes: which PRESTUS features work with BabelBrain.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To cross-check a k-Wave result with an independent solver, or to use the Apple Silicon GPU.
  • Before you start: The external/BabelBrain submodule and a BabelBrain conda environment (Installation).

PRESTUS can run BabelBrain (Samuel Pichardo, University of Calgary) in place of k-Wave. Pre-processing (segmentation, grid, medium masks, placement) and post-processing (focal metrics, CEM43, NIfTI export, HTML report) run unchanged. BabelBrain's solver, BabelViscoFDTD, solves the viscoelastic wave equation and adds a Rayleigh integral step for the water coupling layer. PRESTUS runs it in fluid-bone mode (shear off, PRESTUS tissue properties injected), so results are comparable to k-Wave and jwave. On Apple Silicon it has a native Metal backend, where k-Wave has the slower matlab_gpu path and the experimental, not yet validated cpp_mlx binary.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text:
Set three things: the backend, the Python environment and (optionally) the transducer preset.

acoustic_backend: babelbrain

babelbrain:
  python_env: /opt/conda/envs/BabelBrain   # directory containing bin/python; must be set
  tx_system: R15473                        # BabelBrain preset name; auto-detected if empty
  computing_backend: auto                  # 'auto' | 'cuda' | 'opencl' | 'metal' | 'cpu'  (or 1-4)

babelbrain.python_env must be set. Empty falls back to system python3, which fails with No module named 'BabelViscoFDTD'. PRESTUS finds BabelBrain at external/BabelBrain (git submodule); set babelbrain.root to override. For tx_system, see Transducer mapping.

To run the thermal simulation in BabelBrain as well:

acoustic_backend: babelbrain
thermal_backend:  babelbrain   # BabelBrain Pennes BHTE instead of k-Wave; needs acoustic_backend: babelbrain
acoustic_backend thermal_backend Scenario kwave (default) kwave (default) Standard PRESTUS, no BabelBrain babelbrain kwave BabelBrain acoustics, PRESTUS thermal babelbrain babelbrain Full BabelBrain pipeline, PRESTUS post-processing

thermal_backend: babelbrain reads the *DataForSim.h5 file of the BabelBrain acoustic stage, so other combinations are rejected at config load. The thermal step has no CPU backend.

All babelbrain keys 
babelbrain:
  tx_system: R15473            # BabelBrain preset name; auto-detected if empty
  computing_backend: auto      # 'auto' | 'cuda' | 'opencl' | 'metal' | 'cpu'  (or 1-4)
  device_name: auto            # 'auto' selects device based on computing_backend; or set explicitly e.g. 'Apple'
  ppw: 12                      # points-per-wavelength floor (default 12)
  do_refocusing: false         # skull back-propagation refocusing
  z_beyond_focus_mm: 40        # axial domain truncation past the focal point [mm]
  tight_narrow_beam: ~         # BabelBrain narrow-beam domain; empty/false = off; ignored when grid.acoustic_fov_length_mm is set
  python_env: ''               # path to conda/venv environment; empty = system python3
  root: ''                     # path to BabelBrain source; auto-detected if empty
  tx_mech_adjust_z_m: 0.0      # ADDITIONAL transducer z offset into skin [m]; a placement
                               # correction (preset FL − |focus_pos − trans_pos|) is always added
  z_steering_m: ~              # ZSteering [m]; null = auto-derived (0 with explicit phases)
  q_correction: []             # bone Q-factor correction of the relaxation attenuation model; [] = 1.0 non-CT / 3.0 CT
  focal_calibration: true              # geometric fallback only: steer so the achieved FWHM-centre lands at focal_distance_ep;
                                       # locate-only (report) when explicit element phases exist
  focal_calibration_target: flhm_center # quantity placed at focal_distance_ep: 'flhm_center' | 'peak'
  profile_calibration: false   # annular explicit phases only: refit BabelBrain phases to the O'Neil axial profile
  water_amp_calibration: true  # scale output so the free-water peak matches Rayleigh for the same drive
  use_rayleigh_for_water: false # water-only solver: false = full-wave FDTD, true = Rayleigh integral
  ct_mapping: ''               # HU-to-property mapping for CT-based skull; empty = label-based path
  air_regions: false           # pseudo-CT path only: internal air as pressure-release reflector mask
  air_hu_window: [-1200, -400] # HU range classified as air
  air_keep_boundary: false     # keep air components touching the domain boundary
  cleanup_cache: true          # delete the per-subject BabelBrain cache after reading
  dry_run: false               # prepare inputs only; stop after the acoustic stage
  # isppa_w_per_cm2: ~         # thermal only; leave empty: derived from the scaled acoustic field (in-situ brain peak)

Placement correction, z_steering_m and focal_calibration are explained in Placement Correction and Drive Phases.

PPW and resolution. PRESTUS uses max(ppw, round(c_min / (freq × res_mm × 1e-3))), where c_min is the smaller of BabelBrain's bone shear-speed floor (≈1102.5 m/s) and the lowest medium_properties sound speed. PRESTUS resamples the mask to BabelBrain's native step, so resolutions need not be matched by hand. Lower ppw runs faster with more axial numerical dispersion.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Initialise the submodule after cloning PRESTUS:

git submodule update --init external/BabelBrain

BabelBrain needs its own Python environment, because its compiled extension BabelViscoFDTD does not install into a generic system Python. Use the bundled conda file for your platform:

# Apple Silicon (Metal)
conda env create -f external/BabelBrain/environment_mac_arm64-314.yml
# macOS Intel
conda env create -f external/BabelBrain/environment_mac_x64-314.yml
# Linux (CUDA)
conda env create -f external/BabelBrain/environment_linux.yml
# Windows
conda env create -f external/BabelBrain/environment_win-314.yml

conda activate BabelBrain
which python   # e.g. /opt/conda/envs/BabelBrain/bin/python

Put the environment directory (the one containing bin/python) into babelbrain.python_env. For GPU backend choice per platform, see GPU backend selection.

items.title: Comparison with k-Wave
items.text:
PRESTUS (k-Wave) BabelBrain Solver Pseudo-spectral FDTD Explicit staggered-grid FDTD Physics Scalar linear acoustic (pressure/density) Viscoelastic solver; run with shear = 0 (fluid bone) in PRESTUS Skull model Scalar ρ, c, α Scalar ρ, c, α from PRESTUS medium_properties (or BabelBrain HU mapping via ct_mapping) Rayleigh pre-step None Rayleigh integral for the water coupling layer Narrow-beam domain Optional (see limited FOV) Off by default (the pre-focal field would not be returned); enable with babelbrain.tight_narrow_beam: true. Always off when grid.acoustic_fov_length_mm is set (mask already cropped) GPU backends CUDA, MATLAB GPU arrays CUDA, OpenCL, Metal (Apple Silicon)

See k-Wave for the k-Wave backend options.

Tissue properties and comparability

On the default label-mask path, PRESTUS writes medium_properties to <target>_medium_properties.json. BabelBrain then uses PRESTUS density, sound speed and attenuation for skin, cortical bone, trabecular bone and brain (an undifferentiated skull fills both bone slots), with shear = 0. Remaining differences are the solver and the bone Q-correction (q_correction), so validate against a k-Wave run before relying on absolute values.

PRESTUS properties do not apply to:

  • water: BabelBrain keeps 1000 kg/m³, 1500 m/s, no attenuation (PRESTUS default 994 kg/m³, 1500 m/s, 2.17e-3 dB/(cm·MHz²)). For identical water across backends, set medium_properties.water to 1000 kg/m³ / 1500 m/s.
  • skull on the ct_mapping path, where BabelBrain's HU models set bone (skin and brain are still injected).
  • runs where writing the JSON failed, or where the drive frequency has no entry in BabelBrain's table (5 kHz steps). These print a warning and fall back to BabelBrain's built-in table.
  • voxel-wise pseudo-CT properties computed by PRESTUS.
  • thermal properties (see Thermal tissue properties).

items.title: BabelBrain Output Folder
items.text:
With the BabelBrain backend active, or with io.export_babelbrain: true, PRESTUS writes a babelbrain/ folder next to the standard outputs (nii/, log/, cache/). It holds everything needed to re-run BabelBrain on its own:

File Description <target>_<freq>kHz_<PPW>PPW_BabelViscoInput.nii.gz Tissue mask in BabelBrain integer label format, including the focal voxel marker <target>_CalibWeights.h5 Per-element calibration phases from PRESTUS calibration RunBabelBrain.py Ready-to-run Python script with all simulation parameters pre-filled babelbrain_config.yaml Parameter record for reproducibility

To export the package while simulating with k-Wave, set io.export_babelbrain: true with acoustic_backend: kwave (or no acoustic_backend key). Use this to prepare a cross-validation or to run BabelBrain on another machine.

items.title: Tissue Labels and Material Properties
items.text:
By default each tissue gets one set of properties from medium_properties, written as BabelBrain's integer label NIfTI (BabelViscoInput.nii.gz). Tissues without a BabelBrain label are written as water.

Label mapping PRESTUS layer name Default config indices BabelBrain label BabelBrain material water 0, 3, 6, 9, 10 0 Water skin 5 1 Skin skull_cortical 7 2 Cortical bone skull_trabecular 8 3 Trabecular bone skull (undifferentiated) 4 2 Cortical bone (fallback) brain 1, 2 4 Brain (focal voxel) – 5 –

Label 5 marks the focus voxel. It is BabelBrain's only way to specify the target.

items.title: CT-Based Skull Properties (ct_mapping)
items.text:
Set babelbrain.ct_mapping to let BabelBrain derive per-voxel skull properties from a pseudo-CT (HU) volume with one of its fitted models (BabelBrain's bUseCT mode):

babelbrain:
  ct_mapping: Webb-Marsac   # one of the values in the table below
  ct_use_petra: false        # true only for PETRA-sequence-derived pCT
  water_amp_calibration: true # scale output to the analytic Rayleigh free-water peak

Use this path only to apply BabelBrain's own HU conversion to raw UTE or PETRA pseudo-CT HU values. PRESTUS writes a raw-HU CT.nii.gz on the same grid as BabelViscoInput.nii.gz, and the bridge converts it to the format BabelBrain expects.

Warning

Do not set ct_mapping when PRESTUS's pCT pipeline (pct.enabled: 1) has already converted HU to acoustic properties. BabelBrain then receives only a label mask and uses its own bone values, which differ from the pCT-derived values k-Wave uses. PRESTUS's per-voxel acoustic properties cannot be passed to BabelBrain (see Limitations).

ct_mapping value Density SoS Attenuation PRESTUS equivalent Webb-Marsac (default) Marsac linear HU→ρ Webb 2018 tabulated (freq-dep.) Webb 2021 tabulated (freq-dep.) partial: marsac density + no Webb Aubry Porosity→ρ (Aubry 2003) Porosity→SoS Porosity→Att aubry Pichardo HU→ρ air–tissue linear Density→SoS (Pichardo 2D map, freq-dep.) Density→Att (Pichardo map) none McDannold HU→ρ air–tissue linear Density→SoS (McDannold polynomial) Density→Att (McDannold polynomial, freq-dep.) none Marsac-Aubry Marsac linear HU→ρ Porosity→SoS (Aubry) Porosity→Att (Aubry) partial Pichardo-Marsac Marsac linear HU→ρ Pichardo 2D map (freq-dep.) Pichardo map none McDannold-Marsac Marsac linear HU→ρ McDannold polynomial McDannold polynomial (freq-dep.) none

PRESTUS medium_pct_* functions support k-plan, k-wave, marsac and aubry only. For results comparable across backends, use Webb-Marsac (closest to the PRESTUS marsac/mueller combination) or Aubry (available in both).

  • PETRA density. ct_use_petra: true makes Webb-Marsac use Björn's density formula (SimNIBS_PETRApct_Density). Use it for pseudo-CT from a PETRA sequence via SimNIBS's ZTE/PETRA pipeline. For UTE-derived pCT (the PRESTUS default), leave it false.
  • Raw UTE as CT input. A raw UTE volume can be passed as pseudoCT with ct_mapping set. UTE intensities lack standard 120 kVp HU calibration, so Webb-Marsac and McDannold give inaccurate results. Aubry is the most defensible choice for raw UTE. The recommended route is PRESTUS's pCT pipeline (UTE → calibrated pseudo-CT HU → PRESTUS marsac/aubry mapping).

items.title: Internal Air (air_regions)
items.text:
On the pseudo-CT path, BabelBrain can treat internal air (frontal and sphenoid sinuses, mastoid cells) as a pressure-release reflector (reflection close to −1). Its solver does not update the fields inside the air mask. BabelBrain's own GUI enables this by default for CT/ZTE/PETRA input.

babelbrain:
  ct_mapping: Webb-Marsac
  air_regions: true
  air_hu_window: [-1200, -400]   # default, as BabelBrain
  air_keep_boundary: false

PRESTUS writes <target>_<f>kHz_<ppw>PPW_AirRegions.nii.gz next to the CT input, on the same grid, and the log reports the voxel count and volume of internal air kept. Check AirRegions.nii.gz against the anatomy: in PRESTUS's UTE pseudo-CT, air cells inside the skull mask are captured only where their mapped HU falls in the window.

How the air mask is built, and its limits
  1. Take the pseudo-CT voxels within air_hu_window.
  2. Apply a 3-voxel median filter and find connected components (26-connectivity).
  3. Remove the largest component (the air around the head).
  4. With air_keep_boundary: false, also remove every component that touches the domain boundary. This removes exterior air split by the cropped grid, including the transducer–scalp gap (−1000 HU in the pseudo-CT but water in the simulation).

Limitations:

  • Pseudo-CT only. On the label path there is no air label, so the option is ignored with a warning.
  • Free-water runs never get the mask. The water baseline and water_amp_calibration are unaffected.
  • Boundary air is dropped. Set air_keep_boundary: true if the domain edge cuts a sinus and no exterior air touches the boundary.
  • No k-Wave equivalent. k-Wave and BabelBrain differ wherever the beam meets internal air.

items.title: Transducer Mapping
items.text:
By default (babelbrain.tx_system empty) BabelBrain simulates the PRESTUS transducer itself: the rings of transducer.annular (elem_id_mm, elem_od_mm, curv_radius_mm) on BabelBrain's generic focused annular template. This is the geometry the shipped calibrations were fitted on, so their per-ring phases and amplitudes apply ring for ring, and BabelBrain, k-Wave and jwave simulate the same source. Single-element bowls are one ring. The outer ring diameter sets BabelBrain's aperture.

Set babelbrain.tx_system to a BabelBrain preset to use BabelBrain's own device definition instead, for example to compare against it, or for a phased array PRESTUS does not describe as rings (H317, IGT64_500, ...). Presets are listed in BabelBrain's registry, BabelBrain/SelFiles/transducer_list.yaml; REMOPD is accepted for TheraPhas. The Single and BSonix presets take their aperture and focal length from transducer.annular.

items.title: Calibration Weights
items.text: If PRESTUS has explicit element phases for the transducer, it writes them to the input package as an OptimizedWeightsFile, and BabelBrain reproduces the config phases. Without calibrated phases, BabelBrain uses geometric (Rayleigh) focusing, equivalent to the PRESTUS uncalibrated mode. The file format is described in Calibration weights file.

items.title: Free-Water Amplitude Calibration
items.text:
With babelbrain.water_amp_calibration: true (default), PRESTUS scales the output so BabelBrain's free-water peak matches the analytic Rayleigh peak for the same drive. This is the numerical analogue of hydrophone calibration. It requires explicit element phases and is skipped otherwise.

What the calibration factor does

BabelBrain's saved pressure carries a residual bias of a few % from its built-in CFL/dispersion correction (observed: ≈+6% pressure / +13% intensity for R15473 at 300 kHz).

  • k = p_Rayleigh_peak / p_BabelBrain_water_peak scales sensor_data.p_max_all, and k² scales freefield_isppa_wcm2.
  • k is logged and stored in sensor_data.amp_calibration.
  • A factor more than 15% from 1 triggers a warning, because it points to a setup mismatch (geometry, phases, source amplitude) rather than solver bias.

Why the water factor transfers to tissue runs is explained in internals.

items.title: Thermal Simulation
items.text:
With thermal_backend: babelbrain, PRESTUS calls BabelBrain's CalculateThermalProcess on the *DataForSim.h5 acoustic output. BabelBrain solves the Pennes bio-heat equation on the same domain with its GPU solver. What you get:

  • results_heating has the same structure as from the k-Wave thermal path, so the thermal analysis, NIfTI export and HTML report run unchanged.
  • The cooldown starts at ptrd, as in the k-Wave thermal path. End-of-sonication maps come from TempEndFUS/DoseEndFUS; final maps from FinalTemp/FinalDose (after the cooldown).
  • BabelBrain rescales the field so the peak ISPPA in brain equals the in-situ brain peak of the calibrated, ISPPA-scaled PRESTUS acoustic field, so both thermal backends heat from the same acoustic amplitude. The log shows it next to the free-water value and the implied transmission. Set babelbrain.isppa_w_per_cm2 only to force a specific in-situ brain ISPPA.
  • BabelBrain does not compute the ISO CEM43 fields (returned as NaN) or a focal-plane time series.
  • BabelBrain's thermal step is fixed at 10 ms, so run time scales with the total simulated duration, including the cooldown.
  • With babelbrain.do_refocusing: true, the thermal step uses the skull-corrected /p_amp_refocus field.
Timing parameter conversion PRESTUS parameter BabelBrain parameter Conversion Notes timing.pd / timing.pri DutyCycle pd / pri timing.pri PRF 1 / pri [Hz] timing.ptd DurationUS direct [s] ON duration of one pulse train timing.ptri - timing.ptd DurationOff direct [s] Inter-train cooling interval; 0 if ptri ≤ ptd timing.n_ptri_reps Repetitions rounded Number of (on + off) cycles timing.post_ptri_dur PauseBetweenGroupedSonications direct [s]; 0 if unset/NaN Cooldown after the last repetition (NumberGroupedSonications = 1) thermal.temp_0.brain BaselineTemperature direct [°C] in-brain peak of sensor_data.p_max_all Isppa max p²/(2ρc) over brain [W/cm²] Override with babelbrain.isppa_w_per_cm2

PRESTUS reads the result with read_babelbrain_thermal and resamples it onto the PRESTUS thermal grid.

items.title: Thermal Tissue Properties
items.text:
Known limitation: BabelBrain thermal uses its own tissue thermal properties

thermal_backend: babelbrain ignores the thermal fields of PRESTUS medium_properties (thermal_conductivity, specific_heat_capacity, perfusion, absorption_fraction, absorption_coeff), including uncertainty-mode variants. BabelBrain has no input for them. The acoustic field amplitude is matched between the thermal backends; the tissue thermal properties are not. Use thermal_backend: kwave when PRESTUS thermal properties must apply.

On the label-mask path BabelBrain uses this table (CalculateTemperatureEffects.py):

Tissue Conductivity [W/m/°C] Specific heat [J/kg/°C] Perfusion Absorption fraction PRESTUS absorption fraction Water 0.60 4178 0 0 1 Skin 0.37 3391 106 0.85 1 Cortical bone 0.32 1313 10 0.16 0.28 Trabecular bone 0.31 2274 30 0.15 0.28 Brain 0.51 3630 559 0.85 1

Conductivity, specific heat and perfusion match the PRESTUS defaults, except trabecular conductivity (0.31 vs 0.32). The absorption fraction differs: BabelBrain deposits about 15% less heat in skin and brain and roughly 45% less in skull than k-Wave for the same field. Account for this when comparing temperature rise or CEM43 across thermal backends. On the CT path (ct_mapping), all bone voxels get the mean of the cortical and trabecular values (specific heat 1793.5, conductivity 0.315, perfusion 20, absorption fraction 0.155).

items.title: Limitations and Unsupported PRESTUS Modes
items.text: PRESTUS feature BabelBrain support Details Single transducer ✓ Full With grid.mode: focal_axis (default) or transducer_axis. See Geometry limits. Multi-transducer, async (simulation.transducer_coupling: async) ✗ Not supported Errors. Use acoustic_backend: kwave or jwave with thermal_backend: kwave. Multi-transducer, coherent (simulation.transducer_coupling: coherent) ✗ Not supported Errors. See Geometry limits. grid.mode: ras_plus ✗ Not supported The beam is generally off the grid z axis; babelbrain_wrapper errors. Limited acoustic FOV (grid.acoustic_fov_*) ✓ Supported BabelBrain gets the same FOV-cropped box as k-Wave/jwave, voxel for voxel. Its narrow-beam cropping is disabled. Axisymmetric 2D (grid.axisymmetric: 1) ✗ Not supported BabelBrain is 3D only. Use k-Wave. multi_isppa mode ⚠ Unit-tested; end-to-end pending All derived jobs keep acoustic_backend/thermal_backend, on matlab and HPC. With thermal_backend: babelbrain, the per-target thermal jobs run one after another on HPC, because they share one BabelBrain thermal output file. phantom / water test medium ✓ Supported Free water: BabelBrain ISPPA +2.6 % vs k-Wave (kWaveArray), FLHM centre −0.5 mm, −3 dB volume −2.0 %. Bone-slab phantom: realised/specified bone attenuation 0.91 for BabelBrain (Q = 1) and k-Wave; transmission vs free field 0.128 vs 0.144. ITRUSST phantoms (tx_system: Single): no BabelBrain results yet. Post-hoc water simulation ⚠ Unit-tested; end-to-end pending Runs BabelBrain water-only on the run's grid. With babelbrain.cleanup_cache: false and io.overwrite_files: never, it reuses the run's cached *_Water_DataForSim.h5. Thermal tissue properties ⚠ Known limitation BabelBrain heating is lower than k-Wave's for the same field, mostly in skull. See Thermal tissue properties. BabelBrain thermal without BabelBrain acoustic ✗ Not supported thermal_backend: babelbrain needs the *DataForSim.h5 of acoustic_backend: babelbrain. CT-based skull properties ✓ Supported (via ct_mapping) Raw HU from UTE/PETRA only. Pass the pseudoCT HU volume as the 8th argument to babelbrain_wrapper. See CT-based skull properties. PRESTUS pCT acoustic properties ✗ Not supported With pct.enabled: 1, BabelBrain uses the label path; k-Wave's per-voxel properties cannot be passed. Water (coupling medium) properties ⚠ Known limitation, by design PRESTUS medium_properties.water is not applied (see the warning above). Uncertainty mode ⚠ Unit-tested; end-to-end pending Each variant's density, sound speed, alpha_coeff and alpha_power reach BabelBrain. With ct_mapping, skull variants have no effect, while skin and brain variants apply. Variants never change BabelBrain thermal properties. No BabelBrain uncertainty run exists yet.

items.title: Geometry Limits
items.text:
BabelBrain simulates one transducer per run, with its beam along the z axis of its domain. PRESTUS passes its own grid without rotating it, so a beam off z would be simulated in the wrong direction while aiming at the right focus. PRESTUS refuses:

  • More than one transducer with acoustic_backend or thermal_backend babelbrain, coherent or async (error PRESTUS:babelbrain:multiTransducer). Checked at config load, in the async pipeline and in babelbrain_wrapper. The Nexus flags it before launch.
  • A beam more than 2° off the grid z axis (error PRESTUS:babelbrain:obliqueBeam), checked in babelbrain_wrapper from trans_pos and focus_pos. With one transducer, focal_axis and transducer_axis put the beam on z; ras_plus generally does not.

For multi-transducer runs use acoustic_backend: kwave or jwave with thermal_backend: kwave.

Version tracking

PRESTUS records the BabelBrain version with the results:

sensor_data.babelbrain_version.version_txt   % e.g. '0.8.8'
sensor_data.babelbrain_version.git_describe  % e.g. 'v0.8.8'
sensor_data.babelbrain_version.git_commit    % full SHA
sensor_data.babelbrain_version.bb_root       % path used at runtime

It is stored in the cached .mat file as acoustic_provenance.babelbrain_version, so it survives pipeline restarts.

For the call chain, placement, output alignment and debugging, see BabelBrain integration internals.

References

Pichardo, S. BabelBrain: An Open-Source Application for Prospective Modeling of Transcranial Focused Ultrasound for Neuromodulation Applications. IEEE Trans Ultrason Ferroelectr Freq Control 70, 587–599 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1109/TUFFC.2023.3274046

items.title: BabelBrain Backend: Integration Internals
items.text:
PRESTUS runs BabelBrain through a bridge: babelbrain_wrapper.m writes the inputs and calls run_babelbrain_case.py, which patches BabelBrain at runtime and runs it, and the readers map the results back onto the PRESTUS grid. Most problems with this backend are misalignment between the two grids. This page documents each step of the bridge, for debugging a run (start with Output Alignment and the zero-pressure checklist) and for changing the bridge; for using the backend see BabelBrain backend.

On this page:

  • Call Chain: the functions from the pipeline to BabelBrain, and the runtime patches the bridge applies.
  • GPU Backend Selection and Platform Support: computing_backend and device_name per platform.
  • Grid Resolution: why the input mask is resampled to BabelBrain's step.
  • Placement Correction and Drive Phases: the placement correction, steering and phases, and the free-water and bone checks.
  • Calibration Weights File: what the weights store and the HDF5 layout.
  • Free-Water Amplitude Calibration: the correction of BabelBrain's source bias and the water baseline checks.
  • Inputs, Geometry and Modes: CT, air and water inputs, the single-transducer limit and mode-specific behaviour.
  • Output Alignment: how the field lands on the PRESTUS masks.
  • BabelBrain Output Format: the datasets read, axis flips, interpolation and the NIfTI affine.
  • Zero-Pressure Debugging Checklist: a checklist for missing pressure.
  • Built-In Material Table: BabelBrain's own tissue values, used only if material injection fails.

At a glance

  • Tested with: BabelBrain 0.8.8, the external/BabelBrain submodule pinned at the v0.8.8 tag (7aeccd3). Other versions may break the runtime patches below; each run records the version it used (version tracking).

items.title: Call Chain
items.text:
prestus_pipeline.m
  └─ acoustic_stage.m            ← dispatches on parameters.acoustic_backend (run_acoustic_backend)
       └─ babelbrain_wrapper.m   ← MATLAB orchestrator
            ├─ babelbrain_tx_geometry.m      (PRESTUS rings or BabelBrain preset)
            ├─ write_babelbrain_input.m       (NIfTI label mask)
            ├─ export_babelbrain_weights.m    (calibration HDF5)
            └─ system() → run_babelbrain_case.py   ← Python bridge
                 └─ BabelBrain RUN_SIM().RunCases()

The bridge runs in babelbrain.python_env, writes *DataForSim.h5 to <dir_cache>/<subject_id>/ and patches BabelBrain at runtime (never external/). Without the skull-attenuation patch, injected bone attenuation is not realised (QCorr stays 1.0), although the material table looks correct.

Runtime patches Patch Effect Disable (bridge flag, not a config key) _inject_prestus_materials Overwrites MatFreq from --medium_properties_json (attenuation converted from dB/(cm·MHz^y) to Np/m) runs only without --no_skull_atten_fix _patch_noncat_skull_attenuation Bone shear = 0 (fluid bone), so the specified skull attenuation is realised --no_skull_atten_fix _patch_zdomain_reference CalculateDomainZReference returns 0 (see Output alignment) --no_zdomain_fix _patch_annular_surface Ring tessellation samples exactly the configured bands (np.arange endpoint overshoot added a band to some rings) always on _patch_annular_array_weights Expands per-ring calibration weights to sub-elements (focused annular arrays) with a weights file _patch_resave_normalized, _patch_calculate_temperature_effects Crash guards (negative mask index; tissue class absent from the domain) always on

items.title: GPU Backend Selection and Platform Support
items.text:
computing_backend Backend Hardware Notes 1 CUDA NVIDIA GPUs Linux; request a GPU in SLURM (--gres=gpu:1) 2 OpenCL AMD GPUs, Intel GPUs, some NVIDIA Needs pyopencl in the BabelBrain environment 3 Metal Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4); macOS Intel with environment_mac_x64-314.yml (slow) Only GPU acoustic solver on Apple Silicon 4 CPU Any Fallback; much slower

device_name: auto picks the first GPU (nvidia-smi, pyopencl) or 'Apple'. Set it explicitly to choose among several GPUs. Windows is untested (Unix-style path separators in system()).

items.title: Grid Resolution
items.text: BabelBrain's step is SmallestSOS / (PPW × freq) (SmallestSOS normally ≈1102.5 m/s, DensityToSSoSPichardo), but it takes the input array shape as its grid. write_babelbrain_input.m therefore resamples the mask (nearest-neighbour) to that step (bb_native_res_mm, logged as "BabelBrain native resolution").

items.title: Placement Correction and Drive Phases
items.text:
BabelBrain puts the apex at z_mm ≈ 0 and the FocalSpot at preset FocalLength (Babel_{tx_system}/default.yaml); PRESTUS has the apex |focus_pos − trans_pos| from the target. babelbrain_placement_correction.m (shared with export_babelbrain_inputs) moves the transducer by the difference:

TxMechanicalAdjustmentZ = preset_FocalLength − |focus_pos − trans_pos| · res_mm   (+ any user standoff)

The apex-to-target distance differs from the preset (e.g. 71 mm vs 92 mm for R15473 at 85 mm EP with a 64 mm-deep target). Uncorrected, the field shifts by |focus_pos − trans_pos| − FocalLength along the beam (−7.7 mm for R15473 with the target at 85 mm EP; −28.75 mm at 64 mm EP).

The standoff is babelbrain.tx_mech_adjust_z_m. Without trans_pos, the fallback is preset_FocalLength − focal_distance_bowl. BabelBrain aims at center_z = ZDim[FocalSpot] + ZSteering + TxMechanicalAdjustmentZ, so transducer and aim move together.

Drive ZSteering Behaviour Explicit phases (tr.annular.elem_phase_rad) 0 Weights carry the full drive as a delta from the flat natural-focus reference; BabelBrain reproduces the k-Wave/jwave/Rayleigh ring phases. focal_calibration only reports the predicted focus. No explicit phases aim_bowl − preset_FocalLength aim_bowl is the steer D* from calibrate_focal_steering.m (lands flhm_center/peak on focal_distance_ep) with focal_calibration: true, else focal_distance_bowl. babelbrain.z_steering_m set pinned Overrides both; the weight-delta reference follows FocalLength + ZSteering.

Single and BSonix presets lack TxDiam/FocalLength, so the wrapper passes --aperture (max elem_od_mm) and --focal_length (curv_radius_mm).

Free-water check, bowl rim and bone Q-correction

Free-water check. With explicit phases, the BabelBrain axial profile must overlay the Rayleigh profile of the same phases. A rigid offset of near-field lobes and peak means the placement correction is missing. A lobe shape mismatch means the drive phases differ (e.g. weights delta referenced to the wrong aim).

Bowl rim. A rim inside the domain makes BabelBrain snap the transducer back in whole voxels (log Warning: Need to apply correction to reposition Tx for …; non-zero source_residual_mm). write_babelbrain_input.m therefore trims ceil((d_apex + bowl_depth)/dx) + 1 transducer-side slices (bowl depth 5.4 mm for R15473; d_apex negative if the apex is outside the grid). It warns if that slab contains tissue; it is zero-filled on paste-back.

Bone Q-correction. Realised bone attenuation scales ~1/Q. A bone-slab phantom (6 mm cortical, 78.5 Np/m at 300 kHz, PPW 6) gave realised/specified attenuation 0.91 at Q = 1 (k-Wave 0.91), 0.29 at 3, 0.14 at 6, 0.087 at 10 and 0.063 at 14. BabelBrain's CT default of 3.0 gave transcranial Isppa 10.6 vs 7.6 W/cm² for k-Wave (sub-602 pFOV), so the non-CT path uses Q = 1. babelbrain.q_correction > 0 reaches BabelFTD_Simulations_BASE.__init__ via --q_correction → BABEL_PYTEST_QFACTOR. MATLAB setenv does not work here, because run_command uses Java's ProcessBuilder with the JVM start-up environment.

items.title: Calibration Weights File
items.text:
The file stores deltas from BabelBrain's ring phases at its aim FocalLength + ZSteering:

w[n] = exp(i × (elem_phase[n] − geometric_phase_at_aim[n]))
File layout and import/export
  • /CALIBRATION is a 1-D complex64 dataset (h5py compound {r, i}) as in BabelBrain's SaveToH5py; every root item has the type attribute ReadFromH5py requires. convert_weights_if_needed converts the split /CALIBRATION/real + /imag layout.
  • export_babelbrain_weights writes one weight per ring; the bridge expands them to sub-elements.
  • import_babelbrain_weights reads TxCalibration files (one weight per sub-element) given the per-ring element counts (6th argument).

items.title: Free-Water Amplitude Calibration
items.text:
water_amp_calibration removes the few-% pressure bias of BabelBrain's source correction by comparing the free-water field with rayleigh_axial_intensity.m, and applies the same factor to the head simulation. The thermal input is not rescaled, because BabelBrain renormalises it to Isppa.

Why the factor transfers, and water baseline checks

BabelBrain's Correction = 100/(100 − ExpectedError(CFL)), ×√2 (babel_integration_base) leaves a few % pressure bias at CFL ~0.5. The factor transfers to tissue because the simulation is linear and the bias sits in the shared source chain. The transcranial timestep differs (sub-602 pFOV, R15473 300 kHz 6 PPW: CFL/water 0.300 → Correction 0.290 vs 0.471 → 0.465). The correction tracks it within ~2% in pressure (0.290/0.465 = 0.624 vs CFL ratio 0.637), ~4% in intensity.

The thermal renormalisation is PressureRatio = sqrt(Isppa·2ρc)/max(p_amp[brain]).

Water baseline checks (babelbrain_wrapper.m):

  • The --water_only run must get the same --source_amp_pa as the transcranial run. Otherwise BabelBrain drives at ~50 kPa and freefield_isppa_wcm2 is ~(156.6/50)^2 ≈ 10x too low for R15473.
  • Water_DataForSim.h5 is reused if present, unless io.overwrite_files is 'always'/'force'. If the ISPPA-normalised field looks wrong, compare its mtime with the main DataForSim.h5.

items.title: Inputs, Geometry and Modes
items.text:
PRESTUS does not rotate its grid to the trajectory, so the beam must lie on z and one transducer is supported.

Water, CT and air inputs
  • CT. write_babelbrain_input.m writes raw-HU CT.nii.gz on the BabelViscoInput.nii.gz grid. The bridge quantises it (uniform, 10-bit, BabelBrain's default) into the index map BabelBrain expects and writes CT-cal.npz. The wrapper passes --use_ct, --ct_mapping and optionally --use_petra.
  • Air. BabelBrain does not update the fields inside the air mask (ReflectorMask), so air needs no material and no tiny timestep. bExtractAirRegions is on only with air_regions, because PRESTUS otherwise supplies no air mask.
  • Uncertainty. Variants go in via --medium_properties_json; on the CT path only skin and brain apply.
  • Water. Simulated water comes from the module-level Material (the 1120 kHz MatFreq entry), so the injected Water line affects only GetSmallestSOS. Water is not injected, because it also sets the source factor FactorConvPtoU; the impedance difference is ~0.6%.
Geometry rationale and mode-specific behaviour

BabelBrain's own workflow rotates the grid instead (BabelDatasetPreps.GetSkullMaskFromSimbNIBSSTL). Multi-transducer support would need beam-aligned per-transducer domains (as simulation.async_grid_mode: per_transducer for k-Wave) and a thermal step that accepts a combined heat source.

  • multi_isppa. The thermal result is named after the shared acoustic file (<stem>-ThermalField_AllCombinations.h5), so thermal jobs are serialised on HPC.
  • Post-hoc water. The wrapper passes --water_only under the baseline's target name, which enables cache reuse.
  • Limited FOV. The wrapper disables bTightNarrowBeamDomain on a cropped mask, because its lateral footprint under-shoots the beam near the skull.

items.title: Output Alignment
items.text:
Field and MaterialMap must land exactly on medium_masks.

  • ZDomainStart = 0. BabelBrain adds a skin-surface heuristic (GlobalStartSkin − LineOfSightStartSkin) to the source position in CalculateRayleighFieldsForward. PRESTUS already sets TxMechanicalAdjustmentZ, so the patch removes it. The log line "ZDomainStart neutralized: ... mm" shows the removed amount.
  • Marker anchor. The readers anchor the resample on /TargetLocation, the label-5 marker at focus_pos (benchmark: label agreement 83% → 99%, bone 20% → 98%). Preset FocalLength (focal_length_mm) is the fallback for files without it.

<target>_prestus_anchor.json records realised-minus-requested source position. Expect ≤ 1 native voxel; read_babelbrain_output.m warns above 1.5, which points to a missing ZDomainStart patch.

items.title: BabelBrain Output Format
items.text:
sensor_data.p_max_all is /p_amp (peak pressure [Pa], [Nx, Ny, Nz]), or /p_amp_refocus with do_refocusing: true. Axes are permuted to [lateral X, lateral Y, axial] (dim 3 = beam).

Axis flips and interpolation Item Handling (change both sides together) Acoustic arrays BabelBrain flips them (np.flip(axis=2)) before saving, but not z_vec; the reader uses zdim = z_vec_bb(end:-1:1). /TargetLocation Computed before the flip; index the raw /z_vec. Input mask write_babelbrain_input.m pre-flips when the beam runs along +z (focus_pos(3) >= trans_pos(3)), so BabelBrain's flip on load cancels it; with the beam along −z, BabelBrain's flip alone orients it. The reader resamples with the same beam_sign. Thermal arrays Saved in z_vec order; not reversed. Resampled onto parameters_th from thermal_stage, anchored on the thermal focus (grid.thermal_focus_pos_exact etc. from thermal_grid_setup, else transducer(1).focus_pos). Rises over BaselineTemperature, so outside voxels read baseline. Interpolation Fields 'linear'; MaterialMap method='mode', because 'nearest' drops sub-voxel cortical bone.

The NIfTI affine comes from grid_to_ras_affine.m: planimg.inv_transf, planimg.t1_header, planimg.fov_offset_ac, then the dim-3 flip, in that order. A diagonal-only affine misaligns whenever grid.mode rotates the head (the default).

items.title: Zero-Pressure Debugging Checklist
items.text:
Inspect /MaterialMap, /p_amp, /TargetLocation and /z_vec in *DataForSim.h5, then:

Check Points to Console "zero-filled (no BabelBrain data)" line non-zero Domain too short; voxels outside it are zero-filled ZShrink_L > 0, XShrink_*/YShrink_*, or fewer tissue voxels in MaterialMap than in BabelViscoInput.nii.gz Narrow-beam mode cropped tissue "BabelBrain native resolution" vs grid.resolution_mm Mask not resampled to BabelBrain's step No /TargetLocation in the file Fallback anchor; field may be shifted along the beam Skin→trabecular in a central-line label dump Raw segmentation error

simulation.debug: 1 writes axis plots (sub-<id>_babelbrain_fov_debug<output_affix>.png/.csv) and sub-<id>_babelbrain_material_map<output_affix>.nii.gz to <dir_output>/debug/babelbrain/.

items.title: Built-In Material Table
items.text:
Literature fits tabulated every 5 kHz from 100 to 1125 kHz (MatFreq in TranscranialModeling/babel_integration/babel_integration_helpers.py). They apply only if material injection fails.

Built-in values and references Tissue Density [kg/m³] Long. SoS [m/s] 300 / 500 / 650 kHz Long. att. [Np/m] 300 / 500 / 650 kHz Water 1000 1500 / 1500 / 1500 0 / 0 / 0 Skin 1116 1537 / 1537 / 1537 1.4 / 2.3 / 3.0 Brain 1041 1562 / 1562 / 1562 2.1 / 3.5 / 4.5 White matter 1041 1537 / 1537 / 1537 3.1 / 5.1 / 6.6 Gray matter 1045 1520 / 1520 / 1520 1.3 / 2.2 / 2.9 CSF 1007 1507 / 1507 / 1507 0.03 / 0.05 / 0.06 Cortical bone 1897 2452 / 2476 / 2494 49 / 81 / 106 Trabecular bone 1738 2148 / 2205 / 2247 49 / 81 / 105

Bone longitudinal SoS is linear in frequency, fitted at 270 kHz and 836 kHz (Pichardo 2011). PRESTUS sets bone shear to 0:
