  • Tab Overview: what each tab holds and how fields mark changes and problems.
  • Menus and Shortcuts: undo, help, tools and keyboard shortcuts.
  • Segmentation Step: running SimNIBS charm on its own, before anything else.
  • QuickStart Tab: the four steps and the config keys they write.
  • Advanced Options: settings hidden by default and locked cards.
  • Transducer Tab: choosing a device or entering custom geometry.
  • Placement Viewer: viewing and setting the transducer position on the T1.
  • Issues Panel: the config problems found before PRESTUS loads or runs the study.
  • Run Tab: running locally or submitting to a cluster, and the run log.
  • Results Tab: browsing the runs in a results folder and starting follow-up runs.
  • Study Tab: the run table for many subjects or conditions.
  • Timing Diagram and TUS Calculator: drawing the sonication protocol and exchanging it with the TUS calculator.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You change a setting beyond the QuickStart tab's four steps, run many subjects, or look up what a control writes to the config.
  • Before you start: The Nexus installed and started (PRESTUS Nexus (GUI)); A First Simulation walks through the main tabs once.

items.title: Tab Overview
items.text:
The window has one tab per area; each shows its config sections as cards:

Tab Sections Also on the tab QuickStart (the four steps below) Setup subject, paths, environment, input/output Transducer transducer, geometry, drive and steering device panel with the cross-section under it; 'Calibration' sub-tab (calibration coverage and the calibration conventions, e.g. the focal-depth reference) Placement placement (incl. the Localite folders), Localite ingestion sub-tabs Settings, Viewer, Beam axis, 3D, Transducers (with 2+ transducers), Localite, PlanTUS, TUS entry; Localite shortcuts Medium the medium (a row above the sub-tabs); 'Head model': segmentation, head model, tissue layers; 'Acoustic properties': tissue properties; 'Uncertainty': uncertainty analysis; 'Skull CT': CT-based skull mapping (measured CT or UTE pseudo-CT) SimNIBS environment (installs found on the computer, and with SSH submission on the cluster: Scan cluster), its version, the existing segmentation with its charm report, and the re-run switch; tissue property table; uncertainty variants card with the ITRUSST bounds plot; mapping equations and the CT view Sonication sonication protocol, multi-transducer coupling (with more than one transducer), thermal model timing diagram, TUS calculator exchange; coherent vs. async field prediction Solver acoustic and thermal solvers, their compute backend, grid, jwave, BabelBrain, elastic skull, time reversal 'Compute backend' card: the device setting of each solver that runs (k-Wave, also for heating and time reversal; jwave; BabelBrain), several when solvers are mixed Study study, targeting analysis study manifest editor Run sub-tabs Stages (pipeline stages, debug outputs), Where to run (run profile, platform, HPC, pipeline options), Plan (what the run will do), Review YAML, Launch, Jobs run buttons and log, job list Results (none) the runs in the results folder, follow-up runs Fields, change marks and mode availability
  • Each field has a readable name in words, with abbreviations spelled out or in their usual capitals (HU, CT) and intensities in ITRUSST notation (ISPPA, ISPTA; plain ISPPA in drop-downs, file names and copied text). Hovering over it or clicking ? shows the full help from config_default.yaml, with the choices listed one per line, the config key, the default and a link to its documentation page. Choices that a picture explains (placement method, medium, coupling, array type, steering, focal-depth reference and others) show a small schematic before their name in the drop-down and in the help; the coupling choice also shows two larger figures under it. ↗ in a card's header opens the card's page.
  • Changed values are marked ●, fields filled from the equipment library are marked from library, and ↺ resets a field.
  • A tab's label shows a red (errors) or amber (warnings only) dot with the number of problems in its fields. Its tooltip also counts the changed values.
  • Fields appear only when they apply to the current modes (e.g. the Localite settings only with placement.mode: localite).
  • Placement method (the row at the top of the Placement tab) marks each mode for the configured subject. Unavailable (greyed out; the tooltip names the missing input) means PRESTUS cannot produce an input the mode needs: no T1, no SimNIBS segmentation (PlanTUS: also the mesh sub-XXX.msh) and no startup.simnibs_bin_path to run charm, or no recorded Localite poses. Needs setup means charm will run first or the mode's tool paths are still empty. Tool paths never grey a mode out, since they are only shown once it is selected. The mode in use always stays selectable, and why it cannot run yet is written next to it.
Exporting figures

Each figure has a download button in its top-right corner. Plots export as SVG, PDF or PNG at 300 or 600 dpi; drawn figures (timing diagram, transducer cross-section, the R² strip of the Calibration sub-tab) as SVG, PDF or PNG at 3× or 6× the screen size; 3D views as PNG only. Copy image puts the figure on the clipboard. Figures export in the light theme on white unless Keep current theme is ticked. The file name defaults to sub-XXX_<view> plus the output affix.

items.title: Menus and Shortcuts
items.text:
• File: new, open, open recent, save, save as, reload from disk, quit.
  • Edit ▸ Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) step through value changes, resets, and added or removed transducers. Typing in one field counts as one step. Reload from disk clears the history.
  • View: Dark mode, and Issues… (Ctrl+Shift+I) to open the Issues panel.
  • Tools: Localite, PlanTUS, TUS entry and Calibration open those sub-tabs; neuronav_gui and calibration_gui open in MATLAB; Update project defaults… (Project defaults); Usage statistics… (below).
  • Help: the Nexus overview, this page, Docs for this tab (F1, the page of the tab and sub-tab shown), the parameters reference and troubleshooting. Use local documentation files opens the Markdown files in doc/ instead of the published pages, e.g. offline.
  • Keyboard: Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 switch tabs, Ctrl+Shift+V validates in MATLAB and Ctrl+R runs locally.
Usage statistics

The Nexus runs MATLAB with matlab -batch, where PRESTUS never asks whether to share usage statistics. Tools ▸ Usage statistics… shows the recorded decision and records a new one (Allow, Decline or Forget my decision) in ~/.prestus/telemetry.json, the file MATLAB reads. The Nexus itself sends nothing.

When something goes wrong
  • An unexpected error shows a dialog with the details instead of closing the Nexus; the traceback is also written to nexus_errors.log in the cache folder.
  • Saving writes to a temporary file first, so a full or read-only share leaves the old config intact and shows an error.
  • The MATLAB session must start within 180 s, and a request may take up to 600 s; after a time-out the session restarts on the next request.

items.title: Segmentation Step
items.text:
The SimNIBS segmentation (m2m_sub-XXX) feeds the layered head model, heuristic, MNI, PlanTUS and TUS_entry placement, the Viewer's scalp and beam checks and the 3D head. charm takes an hour or more, so it can run on its own, before anything else.

  • The Medium tab's Segmentation card shows whether it is found, incomplete (tissue labels or MNI warps missing: charm unfinished or failed) or missing, and what in the config needs it. Run segmentation runs only charm for this subject (modules.segmentation_only: 1 with simulation.medium: layered): as a cluster job where the Run tab submits there, else in MATLAB here. The card updates when the job has written the segmentation.
  • Segment again… asks first: charm deletes the m2m folder and segments again (io.overwrite_simnibs: 1 for that run only), and placements, head models and MNI conversions made from the old segmentation no longer match it.
  • The Placement tab shows the same row at the top while the placement method needs a segmentation that is not complete; QuickStart offers Run segmentation now in its first step.

items.title: QuickStart Tab
items.text:
The Nexus opens on QuickStart, which sets up a first simulation in four steps. Every other setting keeps its PRESTUS default. Each step shows To do until it is filled in, then Done or the number of problems (hover for the messages). The QuickStart page writes the same config keys as the other tabs, so the two never disagree.

  1. Head image: choose the T1-weighted NIfTI, or drop it onto the window. From the file name it sets path.anat, path.t1_pattern (as sub-%1$03d_… when the name holds sub-<n>) and subject_id. It also finds a T2 next to the T1 (T1w→T2w) and a folder with m2m_sub-XXX in the anatomy folder, one of its subfolders or one of its siblings (path.seg). If the segmentation is missing, it looks for SimNIBS 4 (charm on the PATH, then the newest install in conda environments and the installers' default folders on macOS, Windows and Linux) to set startup.simnibs_bin_path, and Run segmentation now runs only charm (Segmentation step). The results folder defaults to prestus_sim next to the study config, or next to the anatomy folder if the config is unsaved, never inside the anatomy folder.
  2. Transducer: the device and driving system from the equipment library, the focal depth setting (with the device's range) and the free-water ISPPA. The calibration entry PRESTUS will use is shown below.
  3. Target: an MNI target, either alone (placement.mode: heuristic, which needs a target name) or with a transducer position (mni). A study using another mode is pointed to the Placement tab.
  4. Check and run: Run on (platform) and the errors still to fix, each a link to its field. Continue to Run saves the study and opens the Run tab.

Each step's Learn more opens the page that explains it. Already have results? Start a follow-up run opens the Results tab (Follow-up Runs).

items.title: Advanced Options
items.text:
Each tab hides the settings most studies leave at their defaults, and its Advanced toggle says how many, e.g. Advanced (3). Settings the chosen setup does not read stay hidden too: with a water medium, the anatomy, SimNIBS, MNI-saving, defacing, targeting and free-water-comparison settings; settings the pipelines fill in themselves (such as the io.adopted_* start maps of a sequential follow-up) until they hold a value. Every card has an icon and a line saying what it decides; every sub-tab has an icon.

Advanced controls and locked cards
  • The advanced icon in a card's header, with the number of hidden settings next to it in grey, shows that card's advanced settings; it is highlighted while they are shown, and a second click folds them again. Advanced at the top of the tab shows them on every card of the tab, including the fully advanced sections.
  • An advanced setting that holds a value is always shown. Jumping to an issue opens the card it is on.
  • Locked cards. Tissue layers (Medium tab, Head model) is greyed and read-only until unlocked, as below. The Tissue properties card (Medium tab, Acoustic properties) shows medium_properties as one table, tissues as columns (each headed by a glyph of its head layer) and properties as rows, greyed and read-only. With advanced options shown, 🔒 Unlock asks for confirmation and makes the cells editable for the session; Lock reverts. Changed values are bold, and emptying a cell resets it. Hovering a cell shows its default and the uncertainty-variant values. Values from a loaded config still apply.
  • Which tissues. A water medium shows the water column only and hides the Head model and Skull CT sub-tabs. A phantom shows every tissue, with a note that only the tissues its layers assign are modelled, and hides Skull CT.
  • Thermal rows and absorption. Absorption follows attenuation; the absorption rows and those from thermal conductivity on are shaded: they matter for the thermal simulation only. A tissue sets either the absorption fraction or the absorption coefficient; the table shows the other in (brackets) as implied. Both follow the attenuation power law (y = alpha_power). Typing a value into an implied cell switches the tissue to that field.
  • ITRUSST reference. Open ITRUSST tissue properties ↗ in the card header opens the ITRUSST tissue-property overview with the reference values and bounds.
  • Uncertainty sub-tab. The Uncertainty analysis card turns on simulation.uncertainty; the property card's note links to it while it is off. With it on, the card shows the four variant medium files, followed by the Uncertainty variants card: the brain and skull values this config uses (line) plotted against the bound values of the variants, one property per column (Temp-H/L bound brain heating, Trans-H/L brain intensity, acoustic properties only), then the default, Temp-H, Temp-L, Trans-H and Trans-L values. Greyed values are not in the variant file and use the default. The sub-tab is hidden for a water medium.
  • Skull CT sub-tab. Holds the CT mapping switch, the measured CT file pattern (path.ct_pattern; empty = pseudo-CT from the UTE image) and the mapping settings. With the BabelBrain backend it also holds BabelBrain's own HU mapping and internal-air settings (babelbrain.ct_mapping, babelbrain.air_*); the BabelBrain options card links here. From image to skull properties lists the steps from the input image to the skull properties, each marked as run, reused or skipped: for a pseudo-CT, the UTE image, bias correction and normalisation, the UTE→pseudo-HU line (plotted, read from pct_create_pseudoCT.sh or the subject's fit) and the pseudo-CT; for a measured CT, the CT and its resampling. It then plots the HU→density, sound speed and attenuation curves of the selected mappings, evaluated by MATLAB (pct_mapping_curves) when MATLAB runs or on Draw the mapping curves. The equations of the selected mappings (from Skull Property Mappings) fold out below. It shows the measured CT or pseudoCT.nii.gz over the T1 and the in-skull distributions of the mapped skull properties against the band of the uncertainty bound variants' skull values, with the fraction of skull voxels outside it. The distributions come from the default run when it exists; otherwise Predict skull properties predicts them without simulating, labelled as a prediction. See Pseudo-CT runs.
What counts as advanced
  • Setup: extra MATLAB paths, FSL/ANTs locations, HPC modules for pseudo-CT, the individual io.save_* switches, external acoustic NIfTI.
  • Transducer: element geometry (diameters, curvature, exit-plane distance), matrix layout, bowl-referenced depths, focal-depth reference convention. Amplitude, phases and steering stay visible.
  • Placement: Localite ingestion details (export subfolder, pulses per series, tracker offsets), the heuristic search criteria, PlanTUS weights and outputs, TUS_entry options, neuronav naming rules.
  • Medium: the Tissue layers card (the SimNIBS charm labels each tissue takes; locked like the property table), unlocking the tissue property table, charm debug output, --noneck and custom charm settings, and the tuning parameters of Segmentation refinement, Smoothing (thresholds and width, smoothing of property maps) and Grid refinement (padding), and the rubber-wrap display.
  • Sonication: protocol time steps and cool-down, the thermal model.
  • Solver: precision and interactive mode, everything on the grid except its resolution. Debug outputs stay visible.
  • Study: the target area radius.
  • Run: intermediate pipeline stages (grid, medium, source, analyses), report style, cluster profile, reservation, job naming and waiting.
Where locked cards are defined

Locked cards are set by locked: true under sections: in nexus/prestus_nexus/overlay.yaml. The tuning: list there (which keys affect speed, accuracy, memory or disk) is kept for a later Tune for control and is not shown.

items.title: Transducer Tab
items.text:
Pick a device and driving system from config/equipment, or enter custom geometry.

Device panel, drawing and Calibration sub-tab
  • The panel shows the focal range (min_foc/max_foc) and which calibration entry PRESTUS will use.
  • With several transducers, transducer 2 and later inherit transducer 1's values unless set.
  • Once a transducer is chosen, the cross-section under the device panel draws the elements, exit plane, geometric focus, the focal depth you set (✕) and the device's steering range.
  • Geometry (array type, frequency, element geometry) starts collapsed when the equipment library supplies it; open it to check or override a value. Drive and steering holds the values set per run: the target free-water ISPPA, element amplitudes and phases, and matrix steering. Sweep… next to the target ISPPA edits a list of targets, which runs the multi-ISPPA pipeline. Both cards follow the transducer chosen in the Transducer card.
  • The Calibration sub-tab shows what the library entry covers (fit quality, drive and phase corrections per depth) and compares, fits and saves library entries for the config's transducers (Calibration page).

items.title: Placement Viewer
items.text:
The Placement method row at the top of the Placement tab chooses placement.mode, as the Medium row does on the Medium tab. The tab opens on Settings (the method's paths and options, and per transducer the transducer and target positions and the focal depth setting); its other sub-tabs are Viewer (manual placement), Beam axis (the medium and free-water profile along the beam), 3D (head and transducers in 3D), Transducers (with two or more transducers), Localite, PlanTUS and TUS entry. The sub-tab of the method in use is labelled in bold (the Viewer for manual placement). Localite, PlanTUS and TUS entry carry the icon of their method, as in the Placement method drop-down.

Using the viewer
  • Axial, coronal and sagittal T1 slices with the segmentation overlay; a line under them names the markers. Without a T1, the viewer shows what is missing and a button to the field.
  • Click sets (Focus · Transducer · Browse) chooses what a click on a slice does: set the focus or the transducer (bowl apex), or with Browse move the crosshair without writing anything (scrolling always browses). The bowl is drawn from the device geometry.
  • Undo / Redo (the arrows next to Click sets, or Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z while the viewer has focus) step back and forward through placement changes: positions, the focal depth setting, the placement mode, the acoustic FOV, and added or removed transducers. Edits made on other tabs in between are kept.
  • With several transducers, every bowl, beam axis and acoustic FOV box is drawn; the ones not selected are dimmed. Each FOV box is resolved from its own transducer ('auto' diameter and length), as PRESTUS does: coherent coupling simulates their union, async coupling one box per transducer (details).
  • +/− by the transducer selector add or remove a transducer without switching to the Transducer tab. Hovering over the selector or one of its entries shows the transducer's device (transducer.serial, with its equipment-library name).
  • Coordinates… opens a row to type X/Y/Z directly instead of clicking. RAS mm or Voxel need no conversion. MNI mm is converted to this subject's space with SimNIBS when you click, which needs the subject's m2m_sub-XXX folder; Set focus uses the nonlinear warp and Set transducer the affine, as in MNI placement. Go to only moves the crosshair.
  • With manual placement, the readout's red flags are also listed in the Issues panel, for every transducer: a target more than 2 mm from the focal depth setting, an exit plane (centre or rim) inside the scalp, and beam rays through an eye. They are checked once the viewer (or the Run tab) has loaded the T1 and segmentation; clicking one opens the viewer on that transducer.
  • Snap to scalp keeps the beam axis and puts the exit plane a chosen gap outside the scalp. Transducer at focal depth (under More, with the gap) instead puts the transducer where the focal depth setting lands on the target. View holds the overlay opacity, the FOV size and Centre on focus.
  • Beam: with a segmentation, the readout adds skull on the beam (mean ± SD over 37 rays from the aperture to the focus; the central ray), the mean skull incidence (amber above 20°), the gap between the exit-plane rim and the scalp along the beam (mean ± SD; red when the minimum is negative, i.e. the transducer cuts into the head; a large SD means uneven contact) and the share of rays that pass an eye. These are the measures of the placement comparison (placement.beam_qc).
  • The readout keeps two depths apart: the target depth (exit plane → focus_pos, from the placement) and the focal depth setting (focal_distance_ep, the depth set on the equipment). For annular arrays the setting selects the calibrated phases, so the simulated focus lands at the setting even when the target is deeper or shallower; the readout gives the difference (red above 2 mm). Set focal depth to target copies the target depth into the setting.
  • Trajectories can be imported from Brainsight (NIfTI coordinates) or 3D Slicer, using BabelBrain's conventions.
  • Positions are written in the space set by placement.manual.coordinate_space (voxel or ras). See doc_placement.md.
Beam axis
  • A section through the beam axis of the transducer selected on the Viewer, drawn like the transducer schematic: bowl on the left, depth from the bowl apex to the right, 1:1. It shows the simulation medium: the last layered run's medium_masks (nii/sub-XXX_layered_T1w<affix>_medium_masks.nii.gz), or before a run the SimNIBS labels mapped through layers (without PRESTUS's smoothing). On it are the bowl, the exit plane, the scalp on the axis with its distance to the exit plane, the target, the focal depth setting, the device's steering range and the acoustic FOV; for heuristic, MNI, PlanTUS and TUS-entry placement, a dashed line marks where placement.skin_gap_mm puts the exit plane. The key beside it names every marker and line and the medium layers.
  • ⟲ ⟳ or scrolling turn the section about the axis in 15° steps (0°: lateral axis towards superior); a click moves the Viewer's crosshair.
  • Under the section, on the same depth axis, is the free-water profile. After a run it is read from the run's axial profile (img/sub-XXX_<medium>_axial_profile<affix>.csv): the O'Neil free-water intensity of the settings the run used, the k-Wave free-water baseline if it ran, and the simulated intensity in the head. Before a run it is the device's library model (or the geometric model without a calibration entry) at the focal depth setting, predicted in MATLAB as the Calibration page does: with MATLAB running it appears by itself, otherwise use Compute free-water profile (this starts MATLAB; annular library devices only). A ▼ marks the free-water focus (the peak for a run, the FLHM centre for the prediction).
  • Profile: Scaled · Absolute scales each profile to its own maximum, to compare where they peak, or shows W/cm², to compare how much reaches the target. Absolute needs a run: the prediction has no absolute scale.
  • The readout gives the distance from the exit plane to the scalp and to the first tissue of the medium (on the axis, and the smallest across the aperture in this section; ✗ when negative: tissue sits behind the exit plane), the free-water focus, and after a run the simulated peak in brain. It says when the run used another placement or focal depth than the config now, and what is missing (segmentation, medium, profile). Readout values here and on the Viewer carry ✓, ▲ or ✗ as well as their colour. Without a T1, a placement or a transducer geometry, the tab says which and offers the field.
3D
  • The head (scalp and brain, from the SimNIBS segmentation) with every transducer as it is simulated: one curved ring per element on the bowl, the exit plane, the beam axis, the target (focus position, a sphere with a crosshair), the geometric focus and where the focal depth setting puts the focus. The transducer selected on the Viewer is in colour, others grey.
  • With PlanTUS or TUS_entry placement, the run's target mask is drawn as well (placement.tus_entry.target_mask, or the mask the run wrote to its placement run folder); Mask shows or hides it.
  • Each transducer is drawn in a cylindrical housing, as PlanTUS and BabelBrain draw it. Its front face lies in the exit plane; in practice a gel pad or membrane can leave a gap to the scalp. The size comes from the device's equipment entry (housing: in config/equipment/<SERIAL>.yaml, or its model's). Without a size, the cylinder has the aperture's diameter and reaches 15 mm behind the bowl apex, and the legend says so.
  • A slider next to Scalp, Brain, Mask and Housing sets each surface's opacity. The brain is see-through by default, so the target inside it shows; the housing is opaque and hides the element rings until you lower its slider.
  • The face is removed by default: the scalp in front of and below the eyes (SimNIBS eye label; the brain's front without one) is not drawn, so the view does not identify the participant. Face draws it.
  • Drag to turn, scroll to zoom; Reset view looks at the target from the transducer's side. Scalp, Face, Brain, Mask and Housing show or hide the surfaces.
  • It needs a display with graphics support (Qt Quick 3D); without one, the tab says so.
Transducers
  • Shown with two or more transducers. A read-only table lists each transducer's device, positions, focal depth setting, target ISPPA and tilt from the grid z axis; Edit in placement viewer opens the Viewer on the selected one.
  • Grid orientation sets grid.mode (focal_axis, transducer_axis or ras_plus; Grid Alignment) and gives the resulting grid z axis and each beam's tilt from it. It warns when focal_axis falls back to transducer 1's axis because the beams are too spread (grid.focal_axis_min_norm, Mean-axis spread limit), and when a beam tilts 20° or more on a grid with fewer than 6 points per wavelength in water.
  • Coupling shows simulation.transducer_coupling and, for async coupling, simulation.async_grid_mode. Timing explains what the single timing block means for several transducers.
  • The Viewer's View menu draws the grid z axis (Grid z axis (grid.mode)), on by default with two or more transducers.
Other placement modes
  • Other placement modes are shown read-only: the Localite pose from the neuronav_gui outputs, the heuristic choice from transducer_positioning, and for every mode the positions the last run's placement stage resolved (<path.sim>/sub-XXX/sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json). To get them without simulating, run the pipeline once with only modules.run_transducer_placement enabled.
  • With placement.mode: localite, the Placement card offers Localite page and Import into study…; the Localite sub-tab detects, names and writes the recorded series of a session (Localite page).
  • With placement.mode: plantus, the Placement card runs only the PlanTUS placement: Compute maps scores every skin position and takes the composite-score optimum, Choose in Workbench… picks the position on PlanTUS's maps in Connectome Workbench, and PlanTUS page opens the sub-tab below. The run shows on the Run tab, and the Viewer opens on the result.
PlanTUS
  • The skin of the last PlanTUS run for this subject and target (plantus_metrics.mat in the placement run folder), coloured by the composite score or, under Map, one criterion: bright is better, grey is excluded (avoidance area, or no value). Markers show the target, the composite optimum and the vertex placed.
  • A click (left or right) on the skin chooses a position. The panel lists its criteria, composite score and rank, or why it is not eligible; the view draws the beam axis to the target and the transducer where PlanTUS puts it. Go to the optimum chooses the best composite score.
  • Place here sets placement.plantus.vertex and places the transducer there on the same maps (Run tab, no recomputation); a position that is not eligible asks first. Compute maps runs PlanTUS again and clears the choice.
  • The face is scrambled as on the 3D tab; Face draws it. Without maps, the tab offers Compute maps; without a display, it says so.
  • Compute maps and Place here run in MATLAB on this computer, or, where the Run tab submits to a cluster (scheduler or Submit over SSH), as a placement-only job; the page reloads the maps when the job has written them. Choose in Workbench… needs a display and always runs here.
Heuristic
  • With placement.mode: heuristic: the candidates of the last heuristic run (tpars_sub-XXX_<target>.csv in the placement run folder), plotted as distance to the target against the share of the beam path through excluded tissue, and listed in a table (sortable). Candidates above criterion_intersection are grey; ★ marks the heuristic's choice, ◆ placement.heuristic.candidate, ○ the candidate selected here.
  • A click in the plot or the table shows the candidate's position and criteria. Place here sets placement.heuristic.candidate and places it (placement only, reusing the candidate table); Use the heuristic's choice clears it; Compute candidates runs the heuristic again. Runs go to the cluster where the Run tab submits there, as on the PlanTUS page. Distances are in voxels, as the heuristic computes them.
TUS entry
  • With placement.mode: tus_entry: the TUS_entry settings, Run TUS_entry (placement only; here or as a cluster job, as on the PlanTUS page) and the result from tus_entry_report.csv in the placement run folder: scalp entry and target centre (voxels, 1-based), entry–target distance and angle score. Open in Viewer shows the transducer it placed (TUS_entry placement).
MNI coordinates in the viewer

MNI mm is converted with SimNIBS when you click. It needs the m2m_sub-XXX folder (under path.seg/path.anat) for both the nonlinear and affine transform. Setting startup.simnibs_bin_path alone is not enough, and the viewer says so (distinctly from "SimNIBS's bin folder isn't set") when the m2m folder is missing. Set focus uses the nonlinear warp (most accurate in-brain) and Set transducer the affine (12dof, well-defined outside the brain too). If the m2m folder exists but its nonlinear warp failed or was never produced, Set focus retries with the affine and says so; this does not help when SimNIBS has not been run at all. Go to moves the crosshair using the focus's transform, or the transducer's if Click sets transducer is selected. Set focus / Set transducer only work with placement.manual.coordinate_space set to voxel or ras. A study using coordinate_space: mni writes MNI values directly (PRESTUS converts them at placement-stage runtime) and is not shown in the viewer; type an MNI point and use Go to to look at the matching subject-space location.

MNI conversion call

MNI mm is converted with SimNIBS's mni2subject_coords CLI tool, the same one-shot external call mni2subject_coords_LDfix.m uses; it runs only when you click, not on every redraw.

items.title: Issues Panel
items.text:
The panel lists config problems before PRESTUS loads or runs the study; open it from the error and warning counts in the header.

What the panel checks

The panel lists what PRESTUS would otherwise report only at load or run time: unknown or misspelt keys (with suggestions), deprecated keys, wrong types and values, backend combinations and frequency mismatches, missing inputs and missing calibration entries, multi-transducer combinations PRESTUS refuses or reduces, heating timing and thermal FOV problems, too few points per shear wavelength for the elastic solver, a path.acoustic_input, io.adopted_* file or follow-up parent config that is missing or does not match, a target_isppa_wcm2 that cannot be met (no library calibration and modules.run_water_baseline: 0) or that adds a free-water simulation (auto), a project config_default.yaml that lacks keys added to PRESTUS since it was copied, and (manual placement) the placement viewer's checks. Clicking an issue opens its tab and field, showing advanced options if needed. The panel is closed by default: the header shows the error and warning counts, and clicking them (or View ▸ Issues…, Ctrl+Shift+I) opens the list. It closes on Esc, a click outside, or a click on an issue.

items.title: Run Tab
items.text:
The sub-tabs follow the steps of a run: Stages (pipeline stages and debug outputs), Where to run (run profile, Run on and the scheduler settings), Plan (what the run will do), Review YAML, Launch (the run buttons and log) and Jobs.

  • The highlighted button follows Run on: Run locally for platform: matlab, Submit to cluster for slurm or qsub (and for auto when a scheduler or the SSH host is available). The other one, Write launcher and Save log… are under More. The Where to run card shows the scheduler fields for slurm or qsub, and for auto only on a computer with sbatch/qsub or while Submit over SSH is on.
  • Validate in MATLAB only runs load_parameters.
  • Plan follows the config as you edit it: the pipeline mode (single, async, multi-ISPPA or uncertainty); each stage marked as run, reused (e.g. an existing segmentation, pseudo-CT or measured CT), skipped or stopping the run, with one line on what it does; the jobs the run submits; the files and folders it always writes; the optional outputs (io.save_*, simulation.debug) split into saved and not saved, each with its location and the flag or default that decides it, and which of them already have files on disk for this subject, medium and output affix; and a resource estimate from earlier runs of the project (<path.sim>/run_stats.jsonl): acoustic and thermal simulation time and peak RAM, as median and maximum. See Resource estimates.
  • Run locally writes run_<study>.m next to the config and runs it with matlab -batch, streaming the log. It sets platform: matlab for that run only. You can also run the launcher yourself with run('run_<study>.m').
  • Submit to cluster (when sbatch or qsub is on this computer, e.g. on a cluster login node) writes submit_<study>.m, which keeps the config's platform and hpc.* settings, and runs it: PRESTUS submits as usual (chained pipelines submit several jobs). MATLAB exits once the jobs are submitted (unless hpc.wait_for_job is set). Run profile shows which preset the platform and hpc.* fields match (or that none does); Apply fills them in from another (Local sets platform: matlab). The submitted jobs appear in the Jobs sub-tab (details below).
  • Submit over SSH submits from a computer without a scheduler, e.g. a laptop with the project drive mounted. Set the login node (Host, e.g. user@mentat005.dccn.nl or an alias from ~/.ssh/config), the folder mapping (Local folder /Volumes/myproject is on the cluster /project/myproject), the Setup commands run before MATLAB (e.g. module load slurm matlab/R2024a) and, if the cluster uses its own checkout, the Remote PRESTUS folder. The study folder must be under the mapped folder. The settings are kept per user (~/.config/prestus_nexus/last_session.yaml).
  • Review YAML shows the exact YAML that will be written.
  • Pipeline options (on Where to run, folded) holds the sequential follow-ups run after this config with heat carry-over (Sequential runs), per-stage time and memory limits for the multi-ISPPA and uncertainty pipelines, and the multi-ISPPA summary report switch. They are not config keys: the Nexus keeps them per user and study and writes them into run_<study>.m, submit_<study>.m and SSH submissions.
  • Stop ends MATLAB together with its launcher.
The Jobs tab

The Nexus reads the job IDs from the log and lists them in the Jobs sub-tab (brought forward after a submit), refreshing them every 30 s until they finish. Pop out ↗, or double-clicking a job, opens the same view in its own window, which can be maximised or moved to a second screen. For SLURM jobs the list shows the state, elapsed time and time limit, time left (red when under 10 % of the limit, at least 15 min and at most 1 h, i.e. a TIMEOUT is near), the partition with the node (or, while pending, the reason such as (Priority)), peak memory (sstat while running, sacct after) and the exit code; with qsub only the state. Clicking a job shows its logs from <output>/log_hpc in three tabs, Output (sub-XXX_slurm_output_<id>.log), Errors and Report (sub-XXX_job<id>_report.txt, written by the report job after the job ends: wall time, resources, CO₂e, cost), below the job table (drag the divider to share the space), refreshed every 10 s while the job runs. Follow keeps the end of the log in view, Wrap lines wraps long lines, and A−/A+ change the text size (remembered). Logs are read from the file system when the folder is visible (on the cluster, or through the SSH folder mapping), else over SSH. Cancel selected runs scancel/qdel.

Submitting over SSH
  • Submit to cluster runs load_parameters + prestus_pipeline_start on the host with matlab -batch (in a login shell, from the mapped study folder), and the job list follows the jobs over SSH.
  • Connect… logs in once: ssh's prompts (password, one-time code, an unknown host key) appear in a Nexus dialog, and the login is kept as a shared OpenSSH connection that every later submit, status check and cancel reuses until it has been idle for 8 h (Disconnect closes it). With an SSH key, Connect… is not needed. The other commands never prompt (BatchMode=yes), so without a key or an open connection they fail with "Permission denied". Connection sharing needs OpenSSH 8.4 or later on macOS or Linux; on Windows use a key.
  • Test connection reports whether sbatch/qsub, MATLAB and PRESTUS are found on the host. If the host's matlab is a site wrapper that needs a display (at the Donders, module load matlab/… gives one; the log then says "No DISPLAY variable set"), set Remote MATLAB to the MATLAB binary itself (<matlabroot>/bin/matlab); matlab -batch runs without a display.
  • Config values under the mapped folder are translated the same way, e.g. path.sim: /Volumes/myproject/data/sim runs as /project/myproject/data/sim: the Nexus passes them to load_parameters as overrides (listed in the log) and leaves the config file unchanged. This covers the merged config (study, project config_default.yaml copy, transducers). A path on this Mac outside the mapped folder (/Volumes/…, /Users/…) cannot be translated; the Nexus lists those keys and asks before submitting.

items.title: Results Tab
items.text:
One folder usually holds several runs, told apart by their output affix (study conditions, uncertainty variants, async and sequential runs). The Run list names each one from its affix and starts on the run the open config produces (for async coupling: the joint result; a second list switches between the joint result and each transducer's own field, its _trans-NN run). Every sub-tab follows the selected run. Files are read when needed: only the shown sub-tab reads its files, volumes are read in the background (the viewer says Loading …) and kept for the next view, and opening the tab again reloads nothing unless the runs' files changed (Refresh rescans and reloads).

  • Overview (opens first): the selected run grouped as the ITRUSST consensus asks TUS studies to report them: the non-significant-risk check, the transducer, placement and targeting, pulse timing, free-water acoustic parameters, the estimated in situ acoustic parameters and the thermal results. The risk check uses the limits and colours of the HTML report (non-significant risk limits): ✓ below half the limit, ▲ from half the limit up to it, ✗ above it; above a limit means inspecting adherence to the NSR criteria that govern the protocol. Each row names its source: the run's metrics CSV, the free-water run with the same output affix (modules.run_water_baseline), the targeting CSV (modules.run_targeting_analysis), the placement record, the equipment library or the open config. Pulse timing and transducer geometry come from the open config, which can differ from what the run used; PRF and duty cycles are derived from the timing settings. ISPTA is averaged over the pulse repetition within a pulse train (PD/PRI), as PRESTUS computes it; ISPTA per tissue is that tissue's ISPPA times the run's duty cycle (ISPTA/ISPPA of its CSV, else PD/PRI of the open config). The axial and lateral −3 dB focal widths come from the CSV (focal_fwhm_*); for runs written before these columns existed, the Nexus measures them in the background on the run's T1w intensity map, along the transducer axis of its placement record and through the intensity peak inside the −6 dB focal mask, and the row names that map as its source. These can differ from the grid's by a fraction of a voxel. What no output holds reads not available. Copy as Markdown copies the overview as tables.
  • Spatial ▸ Acoustic / Thermal: the run's maps on the T1 (only the maps it wrote are offered), centred on the map's peak (Go to peak re-centres). A colour bar gives the map's unit (W/cm², Pa, °C, min). Intensity, pressure, MI, temperature rise and CEM43 are coloured from 0 to the map's maximum; absolute temperatures from their 1st to 99th percentile. Overlay colormap offers magma (the default), inferno, viridis, plasma and hot. Hide below hides values under a share of the colour scale's top (10 % by default for intensity, pressure, MI and temperature rise). Clicking a slice moves the crosshair; the line under the slices gives its RAS position and the map's value there. Every transducer (square) and focus (x) is marked, as the run's placement stage recorded them (sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json), else from the config; points away from the slice are drawn faint.
  • Heating: the run's thermal time courses from cache/sub-XXX_<medium>_HEAT<affix>.mat (written by the thermal analysis, modules.run_thermal_analysis; not with the BabelBrain thermal backend). Metric picks the peak temperature, temperature rise, CEM43 (k-Wave) or CEM43 (ISO) of each tissue layer (max over the layer), or the temperature, rise or CEM43 on the focal axis (per tissue and at the target). Tick the tissues to show; the choice is kept across metrics and runs. The legend gives each tissue's maximum. Log scale helps with CEM43; Shade sonication marks the sonication periods. Needs SciPy (or h5py for -v7.3 files). For an async transducer's own field the joint run's time courses are shown.
  • Report: the run's HTML report, or any other report in the folder (sequential and multi-ISPPA summaries). Export report as PDF… saves the shown report.
  • Data table: the run's metrics (last CSV row).
  • Poses: shown when the run wrote a time-reversal pose table (_timereversal_poses_T<i>.csv); Use this pose… starts a follow-up at the selected pose.
  • Compare runs: one row per run with the key metrics (ISPPA, MI, focal distance and volume, temperature rise, CEM43); double-click a row to show that run.

items.title: Follow-up Runs
items.text:
Follow-up… in the Results header creates a new study config that starts from the selected run, and opens it. Pick one of five types:

  • New intensity: another target ISPPA on the same beam. It reuses the run's pressure map (path.acoustic_input), so no acoustic simulation runs (Reusing outputs).
  • New timing (thermal only): other pulse timing on the same pressure map; only the thermal simulation runs.
  • New placement, same head: another transducer position; the head model is built once and reused (headmodel.reuse_across_placements).
  • Pose from the time-reversal search: a pose from the run's pose table as a manual placement, or its refocusing phases (Pose search).
  • Sequential: a run that continues from this run's end temperature and thermal dose. It is added to this config's Pipeline options (Run tab) rather than run on its own (Sequential runs).

The dialog lists problems as you edit, and errors block Create. Each follow-up gets a new io.output_affix and is saved next to the parent as <parent>_<type>_<affix>.yaml. The config records its parent in a # nexus-followup: comment line, which MATLAB ignores and the Nexus keeps on every save. The Results header names a run's parent and its follow-ups.

items.title: Study Tab
items.text:
Runs many subjects with per-run settings. See Group analysis.

The run table
  • The table (the study manifest, study.manifest) has one row per simulation run; settings not in the table come from the study config. A single subject does not need it. How to fill the table shows the steps and an example.
  • Add subjects… adds one run per subject ID (1-12, 15, sub-020). Add setting column… adds a config key to vary per run (empty cell = the study value) or the run columns include, config and notes; hovering over a column header shows its help. More holds adding an empty row, removing rows or a column, and Save table as….
  • The table is saved to the Table file (relative to the config). Without one, the first save writes <config name>_runs.tsv next to the config and sets study.manifest.
  • Import from Localite… reads the neuronav_gui outputs under path.localite_post (neuronav_ingest_summary.csv and the per-session InstrumentMarker_*.json). It makes one run per target, or one run per session with the targets assigned to transducers 1, 2, …, with a preview before adding. See Group analysis.
  • The summary under the table checks the manifest as you type: subject IDs, include values, unknown keys (with suggestions), and rows that would write to the same outputs.
  • Check all runs saves the table and runs prestus_study_start(config, 'DryRun', true). Run all runs locally writes run_study_<study>.m and runs it; Write launcher script only writes it. These stay disabled while the table is empty. Build group report runs prestus_group_report_start(config) (group maps + report). Checks, runs and the report stream to the Run tab.

items.title: Timing Diagram and TUS Calculator
items.text:
The Sonication protocol card (Sonication tab) draws the protocol from timing.*: one pulse (with its ramp), one pulse train, and the train repetitions. It labels PD, PRI/PRF, PTD, PTRI and PTRD with the pulse count, duty cycles, the on-time, and the Ipa/Itp factor of the ramp (compute_ramp_factor). It also lists inconsistent settings (e.g. a pulse longer than its repetition interval).

You can edit the protocol in the diagram. Drag an edge to change its value: the pulse end (PD), the end of the rise (ramp), the dashed start of the next pulse (PRI), the train end (PTD), the dashed start of the next train (PTRI) or the end of the repetitions (PTRD). Dragged values snap to two significant digits and stay within the other settings (a pulse cannot outgrow its PRI). To type an exact value, click an edge or its label and enter a duration with its unit (20 ms, 500 µs); the PRI also accepts a frequency (5 Hz). Enter applies the value and Esc cancels. The fields for these six values are folded under Show the values as fields; a field whose value is invalid stays in view.

The TUS calculator (Radboud University, MIT licence) estimates derived quantities (derated intensities, MI, energy deposition, temperature rise) for a protocol. The Nexus does not copy its calculations. It exchanges settings files with it instead:

  • Export for TUS calculator… writes a JSON file for the calculator's Upload settings: pulse duration, ramp duration and shape, PRI, PTD, PTRI, PTRD (in ms), whether the train and repetition levels are enabled, and (when set) the frequency, target ISPPA, aperture and focal depth.
  • Import from TUS calculator… reads a settings file downloaded from the calculator (JSON or YAML). It shows the values it will set (in seconds), and optionally also sets the frequency and target ISPPA.
  • Open TUS calculator ↗ opens the web app.
Ramp convention

Both use the same ramp convention: the ramp duration is the rise (= fall) time at each end of a pulse (timing.pulse_ramp_dur, timing.pulse_ramp_shape linear or tukey). PRESTUS models pulse ramps only, so the calculator's pulse-train and repetition ramps are exported as 0 and reported when an imported file sets them. A level disabled in the calculator sets the corresponding PRESTUS durations to 0.

items.title: Simulation Outputs
items.text:
A run writes its results as files: a metrics table, NIfTI maps, figures and an HTML report, plus caches and stage outputs that a later run can reuse instead of recomputing. Knowing which file holds a value lets you check that the numbers you report come from the settings you intended.

On this page:

  • Output directory structure: the folders and files of a run.
  • Where outputs live: which folder each stage writes and what it depends on.
  • NIfTI images: the medium, acoustic and thermal maps in T1 and MNI space.
  • Figures: the PNG overlays of intensity and temperature.
  • HTML report: the sections of the per-run report.
  • Group outputs: the files of the group report and maps.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To find a specific file, or to see where a stage writes its results. Read Reading your results first.
  • Before you start: A finished run.

Subpages:

  • Metrics Table Columns: every column of the metrics CSV and the reference levels; for anyone reporting or checking a value.
  • Reusing Earlier Outputs and Caches: starting a run from earlier stage outputs, overwrite behaviour and cache checks; for anyone re-running, resuming or chaining runs.

items.title: Output Directory Structure
items.text:
A finished run writes to <path.sim>/sub-XXX/:

sub-XXX_<medium>_report<affix>.html       ← self-contained HTML report
sub-XXX_<medium><affix>.csv               ← quantitative metrics
sub-XXX_<medium><affix>_targeting.csv     ← targeting accuracy (layered or phantom)
sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json             ← resolved transducer positions (T1 voxels; every placement mode)

nii/                                       ← NIfTI maps (medium, acoustic, thermal); not created with modules.run_nifti_creation: 0
img/                                       ← PNG figures (acoustic, thermal, preprocessing)
babelbrain/                                ← BabelBrain inputs (io.export_babelbrain or acoustic_backend: babelbrain)

cache/                                     ← regenerable intermediates
    sub-XXX_<medium>_parameters_<yyMMdd_HHmm><affix>.mat   parameters snapshot at start
    sub-XXX_<medium>_report_parameters<affix>.mat          final parameters (report re-rendering)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_cropped_smoothed<affix>.mat           cropped/smoothed head (layered)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_grid_cache<affix>.mat                 grid stage (io.save_grid_cache)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_planimg<affix>.mat                    planning-image sidecar (always)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_medium_cache<affix>.mat               medium stage (io.save_medium_cache)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_kwave_source<affix>.mat               source (io.save_source_matrices)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_results<affix>.mat                    acoustic results + provenance
    sub-XXX_<medium>_heating_res<affix>.mat                thermal results (io.save_thermal_matrices)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_HEAT<affix>.mat                       thermal time courses (thermal analysis; not BabelBrain)

log/
    sub-XXX_<medium>_<timestamp><affix>.txt                MATLAB diary of the run
    sub-XXX_<medium>_parameters<affix>.yaml                resolved parameters (human-readable)

debug/                                     ← diagnostic artefacts (debug=1 only)
    preproc/        head preprocessing (rotation, cropping, skull visualisations)
    medium/         medium mapping (grid-space property matrices, pCT)
    source/         source/transducer setup (element distribution plots)
    babelbrain/     BabelBrain FOV and domain-coverage diagnostics
  • Cache files are regenerable. With io.overwrite_files = 'never', existing files are reloaded instead of recomputed (Overwrite behaviour). io.save_matrices = 0 writes none of the optional cache matrices; 1 saves all of them. The parameter snapshots and the planning-image sidecar are always written. Per-step flags such as io.save_acoustic_matrices override it when set.
  • Debug files are written only with parameters.simulation.debug = 1.
  • Run statistics: each run with an acoustic or thermal simulation adds one line to <path.sim>/run_stats.jsonl (one file per path.sim, shared by all subjects): grid size, time steps, thermal steps, simulation durations, solver, partition and peak RAM. The Nexus estimates resources from it (Resource estimates).

items.title: Where Outputs Live
items.text:
Each location belongs to one level. A level only reads the levels above it, and each folder has one writer.

Level Depends on Locations Written by Inputs none path.anat (T1/T2), path.localite_raw (raw Localite exports), path.localite_t1 (planning T1s) you / the scanner / Localite; PRESTUS only reads them Subject derivatives the subject's images path.seg (SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX), path.pct (pseudo-CT), path.localite_post (ingested Localite markers) segmentation (layered media; io.overwrite_simnibs), pseudo-CT generation, neuronav_ingest_markers Placement subject derivatives, target, transducer geometry, placement settings path.placement (default <path.sim>/placement): sub-XXX/<mode>/<target_name>/ the placement stage (heuristic, PlanTUS, TUS_entry) Simulation everything above, plus the acoustic/thermal setup path.sim/sub-XXX/ (this page) the simulation pipeline
  • Placement does not depend on the medium, grid or drive level. Point several setups at one path.placement to reuse a heuristic, PlanTUS or TUS_entry result. Each run folder holds everything the run produced and a run record, placement_run.json. manual, mni and localite placements have no run folder. The simulation records the positions it used in sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json.
  • path.localite_export is a hand-off folder, not a level. It holds copies of placement results for import into Localite (heuristic position table, Localite-ready T1).
  • SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX folders are only read after segmentation. For the pseudo-CT location, see (pseudo-)CT.

items.title: NIfTI Images
items.text:
PRESTUS exports 3D volumes (2D for axisymmetric simulations) in subject-native T1 space and MNI-152 space. Each group of maps is written as soon as its stage finishes.

  • Subject T1 space: sub-XXX_<medium>_T1w<affix>_<type>.nii.gz
  • MNI space: sub-XXX_<medium>_MNI<affix>_<type>.nii.gz
Medium maps (written after medium setup) Type Resampling Description medium_masks nearest Tissue label mask (integer indices) sound_speed nearest Speed of sound [m/s]; edges filled with water value density nearest Mass density [kg/m³]; edges filled with water value alpha_coeff nearest Attenuation coefficient [dB/(cm·MHz^y)]; edges filled with water value Acoustic maps (written after acoustic analysis) Type Description intensity Pulse-average intensity (IPA) [W/cm²] MI Mechanical index pressure Peak pressure [Pa]; with a JSON sidecar so a later run can start from it (Starting from earlier stage outputs) focal_mask_3dB −3 dB focal zone binary mask (IPA ≥ 50 % of peak; restricted to brain for layered, to beyond-exit-plane for free-field) focal_mask_6dB −6 dB / FWHM focal zone binary mask (IPA ≥ 25 % of peak = P ≥ Pmax/2; same region restriction) Thermal maps (written after thermal analysis) Type Description heating Maximum temperature during sonication [°C] heating_end Temperature at end of last pulse [°C] heatrise Temperature rise above baseline [°C] heatrise_end Temperature rise above baseline at end of last pulse [°C] CEM43 CEM43 thermal dose, kWave form [min] CEM43_end CEM43 (kWave) at end of last pulse [min] CEM43_iso CEM43 thermal dose, ISO form [min] CEM43_iso_end CEM43 (ISO) at end of last pulse [min]

items.title: Figures
items.text: PRESTUS saves PNG overlays of intensity and temperature on the segmentation.

items.title: HTML Report
items.text:
sub-XXX_<medium>_report<affix>.html is a self-contained report in the output directory. Sections:

Section Content Safety dashboard colour-coded cards for all ITRUSST-limited metrics (green / amber / red); thermal cards use the formulation selected by parameters.thermal.cem43_iso Simulation summary key acoustic and thermal values Methods ITRUSST-aligned methods text (CC0) with reference list: software, transducer, grid, tissue properties, pulse timing, thermal model, exposure values. Copy methods text / Copy text + references copy it as formatted text with a plain-text fallback. Check it against your study before use Configuration summary parameters used for the run Medium properties per-tissue acoustic and thermal properties (layered only) Acoustic results intensity overlays and the full acoustic metrics table Thermal results temperature, CEM43 (kWave) and CEM43 (ISO) plots (if heating was simulated) Post-hoc water simulation free-field reference results (if run) Log full pipeline execution log

Example report on a phantom: Download example HTML

items.title: Group Outputs
items.text:
The group tools read existing per-run outputs and never simulate; see Group analysis.

Study (prestus_group_report_start on a config with study.manifest, or the end of prestus_study_start), written to <path.sim>/group/<study.name>/:

group_<name>_report.html                  ← self-contained group HTML report
group_<name>_runs.csv                     ← one row per run: settings, metrics, targeting
plots/
    group_<medium>_<metric>_<name>.png      box plots (intensity, mi, conditions, targeting, maxT, riseT, cem43)
    group_<cond>_focal_overlap.png          MNI overlap figure per condition
maps/
    group_<cond>_focal_overlap_3dB.nii.gz   fraction of runs covering each voxel
    group_<cond>_<Ipa|Itp>_mean.nii.gz      mean intensity (and _sd)
    group_<cond>_heatrise_mean.nii.gz       mean temperature rise (heating runs)
log/
    plan_<time>.tsv / launch_<time>.tsv     study dry-run plan / launch log
log_hpc/                                  ← dependent study-report job (HPC)

Subjects (no manifest: all subjects with the same simulation.medium and io.output_affix; prestus_group_report_start, or modules.generate_group_report = 1 after each subject), written to path.sim:

group_<medium>_report<affix>.html         ← self-contained group HTML report
group_<medium>_runs<affix>.csv            ← one row per subject
group_plots/
    group_<medium>_<metric><affix>.png      box plots: intensity (Isppa / Ipa_target), mi (per tissue),
                                            targeting (MNI centroids, focus error), maxT, riseT, cem43
group/<medium><affix>/maps/, plots/       ← group MNI maps (manual prestus_group_report_start only)

Thermal plots (maxT, riseT, cem43) need a layered medium with heating results. See Group HTML report for the report contents.

items.title: Metrics Table Columns
items.text:
The metrics CSV holds every number a run reports: intensities, pressures, mechanical indices, focal volumes and, with heating, temperatures and thermal doses. Each column has a precise definition and unit, and several are checked against the ITRUSST non-significant risk limits, so the column you quote decides what your reported value means.

On this page:

  • Metrics table: the file and where targeting accuracy is written.
    • Intensity nomenclature: how IPA, ISPPA and the mechanical index are computed.
    • Acoustic metrics: global and tissue-specific acoustic columns.
    • Thermal metrics: global and tissue-specific thermal columns.
    • Non-significant risk limits: the reference levels the report flags against.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To report a value from the CSV, or to check what a column measures.
  • Before you start: A finished run; see Simulation Outputs for where the CSV is written.

items.title: Metrics Table
items.text:
Filename: sub-XXX_<simulation_medium><affix>.csv

One CSV holds all quantitative metrics: acoustic metrics first, then thermal metrics if heating was simulated. Tissue-specific columns exist for layered simulations only.

Targeting accuracy (modules.run_targeting_analysis, layered or phantom media) goes to sub-XXX_<simulation_medium><affix>_targeting.csv; see Targeting accuracy.

items.title: Intensity Nomenclature
items.text:
All intensity values are pulse-average intensity (IPA), computed from the steady-state peak pressure amplitude:

I = p² / (2ρc)   [W/cm²]

p is the peak pressure amplitude, ρ density and c sound speed. The factor 2 averages over the sinusoid's cycle. The result is the temporal-peak intensity (ITP). IPA, the time-average intensity during the pulse, is ITP times the ramp factor of timing.pulse_ramp_dur and timing.pulse_ramp_shape; for pulses without a ramp IPA = ITP. The average over the repetition interval (ISPTA) also applies the duty cycle PD/PRI: it is the average within a pulse train, without the pulse-train duty cycle PTD/PTRI.

The spatial peak of IPA is ISPPA. IPA at a specific location (target point, radius average) is labelled IPA.

The mechanical index per voxel is MI = p⁻ / √f, with p⁻ the peak rarefaction (negative) pressure in MPa and f the centre frequency in MHz (IEC 62359 / FDA). PRESTUS uses the absolute value of p_min_all from k-Wave. For multi-transducer async combinations it uses the per-voxel most-negative pressure across transducers (p_min_async).

Darmani et al. (2022, Clinical Neurophysiology) give an overview of the nomenclature.

References

Darmani, G., Bergmann, T. O., Butts Pauly, K., Caskey, C. F., de Lecea, L., Fomenko, A., Fouragnan, E., Legon, W., Murphy, K. R., Nandi, T., Phipps, M. A., Pinton, G., Ramezanpour, H., Sallet, J., Yaakub, S. N., Yoo, S. S., & Chen, R. (2022). Non‑invasive transcranial ultrasound stimulation for neuromodulation. Clinical Neurophysiology, 135, 51–73. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinph.2021.12.010

items.title: Acoustic Metrics
items.text:
Focal distances come in two references: columns ending in _ep_mm count from the exit plane, as focal_distance_ep does; columns ending in _bowl_mm from the bowl apex (trans_pos). Group and comparison reports read the earlier real_focal_distance_mm as real_focal_distance_bowl_mm. See Transducer-Target Distance.

Global acoustic columns Column Unit Description subject_id none Subject identifier freq_Hz Hz Transducer centre frequency Isppa W/cm² ISPPA: maximum pulse-average intensity across the entire simulation grid Isppa_after_exitplane W/cm² Maximum IPA beyond the transducer exit plane (or within brain if modelled) real_focal_distance_bowl_mm mm Distance from the bowl apex (trans_pos) to the location of maximum IPA real_focal_distance_ep_mm mm Distance from the exit plane to the location of maximum IPA; compare with focal_distance_ep Ipa_target W/cm² IPA at the specified target coordinate Ipa_target_radius W/cm² Mean IPA within a sphere of radius analysis.focus_area_radius mm centred on the target trans_pos_vox voxels Transducer position in simulation grid coordinates focus_pos_vox voxels Target focus position in simulation grid coordinates

Water/free-field simulations also include Psptp (spatial peak temporal peak pressure), Ptp_target (temporal peak pressure at the target) and MI (global mechanical index from peak rarefaction pressure, unitless; ITRUSST limit 1.9, labelled "MI (free water)" in the report). They also include the ITRUSST focal metrics (focal_vol_3dB_mm3, focal_vol_6dB_mm3, focal_centroid_3dB_bowl_mm, focal_centroid_3dB_ep_mm, focal_flhm_center_bowl_mm, focal_flhm_center_ep_mm, focal_fwhm_axial_mm, focal_fwhm_lateral_min_mm, focal_fwhm_lateral_max_mm), computed beyond the transducer exit plane.

Tissue-specific acoustic columns (layered simulations only) Column Unit Description Isppa_brain W/cm² Maximum IPA within brain tissue (GM + WM) Isppa_skull W/cm² Maximum IPA within skull bone Isppa_skin W/cm² Maximum IPA within skin Psptp_brain Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure within brain tissue Psptp_skull Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure within skull bone Psptp_skin Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure within skin Psptp Pa Global spatial peak temporal peak pressure across the entire grid (also written for water/free-field runs). Max pressure safety limit: 2 MPa Ptp_target Pa Temporal peak pressure at the target coordinate MI_brain none Maximum mechanical index within brain tissue (GM + WM) MI_skull none Maximum mechanical index within skull bone MI_skin none Maximum mechanical index within skin MI_tc none Transcranial MI: maximum mechanical index across all intracranial voxels (WM, GM, CSF, blood; skull bone excluded). Primary safety metric for cavitation risk at the sonication target. ITRUSST limit: 1.9 Ix_brain_vox, Iy_brain_vox, Iz_brain_vox voxels Grid coordinates of peak IPA within brain halfmax_ISPPA_volume_brain_mm3 mm³ Volume of the −3 dB intensity region within brain (IPA ≥ 50 % of Isppa_brain); equals focal_vol_3dB_mm3 focal_vol_3dB_mm3 mm³ Volume of the −3 dB focal zone within brain (IPA ≥ 50 % of peak; 10·log₁₀(0.5) = −3 dB) focal_vol_6dB_mm3 mm³ Volume of the −6 dB focal zone within brain (IPA ≥ 25 % of peak = pressure ≥ 50 % of peak; FWHM) focal_centroid_3dB_bowl_mm mm Distance from the bowl apex to the geometric centroid of the −3 dB focal region focal_centroid_3dB_ep_mm mm Distance from the exit plane to the geometric centroid of the −3 dB focal region focal_flhm_center_bowl_mm mm Distance from the bowl apex to the FLHM centre on the beam axis (calibration.focal_reference) focal_flhm_center_ep_mm mm Distance from the exit plane to the FLHM centre; the manufacturer-style focal distance focal_fwhm_axial_mm mm −3 dB focal width (FWHM of IPA) through the brain peak along the transducer axis (trans_pos to focus_pos); crossings of half the peak interpolated between grid points. Empty when the focal lobe reaches the grid edge focal_fwhm_lateral_min_mm, focal_fwhm_lateral_max_mm mm Narrowest and widest −3 dB focal width through the brain peak in the plane perpendicular to the transducer axis, measured every 5°; equal for a round focus

items.title: Thermal Metrics
items.text:
Thermal columns are only written when heating simulations are run. Temperature is simulated over the full sonication protocol (on/off cycles) with the Pennes bioheat equation. All values are spatial maxima within the respective tissue.

Global thermal columns Column Unit Description maxT °C Global maximum temperature reached at any point during sonication endT °C Global maximum temperature at the end of the last sonication pulse maxCEM43 min Global maximum CEM43 (kWave form) over the full protocol maxCEM43end min Global maximum CEM43 (kWave form) at end of last pulse maxCEM43iso min Global maximum CEM43 (ISO form) over the full protocol maxCEM43isoend min Global maximum CEM43 (ISO form) at end of last pulse Tissue-specific thermal columns Column Unit Description maxT_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature in each tissue during sonication. ITRUSST limit: 39 °C endT_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature in each tissue at end of last pulse riseT_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature rise above baseline (maxT − baseline). ITRUSST limit: 2 °C rise_endT_brain/skull/skin °C Temperature rise above baseline at end of last pulse CEM43_brain/skull/skin min Maximum CEM43 (kWave form) in each tissue. ITRUSST limits: brain 2 min, skull 16 min, skin 21 min CEM43_end_brain/skull/skin min CEM43 (kWave form) in each tissue at end of last pulse CEM43iso_brain/skull/skin min Maximum CEM43 (ISO form) in each tissue CEM43iso_end_brain/skull/skin min CEM43 (ISO form) in each tissue at end of last pulse

Both CEM43 formulations are always computed; see Thermal simulations for the formulas. The HTML report shows the one selected by parameters.thermal.cem43_iso.

items.title: Non-Significant Risk Limits
items.text:
The HTML report flags each metric against the ITRUSST consensus non-significant risk limits for transcranial ultrasound (Aubry et al., 2025, Brain Stimulation):

Metric Limit MI transcranial 1.9 MI (free water) 1.9 Max pressure 2 MPa Temperature rise (a) 2 °C Maximum temperature (b) 39 °C CEM43 (brain) (c) 2 min CEM43 (skull) (c) 16 min CEM43 (skin) (c) 21 min

For thermal estimates, non-significant risk can be characterised by a, b, or c. These limits are for quick reference. Always check the original reference and possible consensus updates. PRESTUS does not make independent recommendations.

items.title: Reusing Earlier Outputs and Caches
items.text:
A run can start from results an earlier run wrote instead of recomputing them: a segmentation, pseudo-CT, placement or pressure map, or the caches in its own cache/ folder. Reuse saves time, but a reused file built from other settings gives results that do not match the configuration, so PRESTUS records and checks the settings each file depends on.

On this page:

  • Starting from earlier stage outputs: starting a run from a placement, pseudo-CT or pressure map.
  • Overwrite behaviour: when existing files are reused or recomputed.
  • Cache reuse checks: how a reused cache is checked against the current settings.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You re-run or resume a subject, run a chained pipeline, or start a run from an earlier placement or pressure map.
  • Before you start: An earlier run's output folder; see Simulation Outputs for the folder layout.

items.title: Starting from Earlier Stage Outputs
items.text:
PRESTUS keeps two kinds of intermediate results apart:

  • Within-run caches (cache/ of a simulation folder) are reloaded only by the run that wrote them, or a re-run of it. io.overwrite_files decides reuse (Overwrite behaviour).
  • Stage outputs are complete results that a later, separate run starts from. Each has a BIDS-style JSON sidecar whose signature lists the settings the output depends on. The later run compares it with its own settings.
Stage outputs and compared settings Stage output Sidecar Picked up by Compared settings SimNIBS segmentation, path.seg/m2m_sub-XXX/ none (standard SimNIBS output) every layered run, when final_tissues.nii.gz exists (io.overwrite_simnibs) SimNIBS version (charm_log.html) and charm settings (settings.ini): a warning, see Segmentation Pseudo-CT, <pct folder>/pseudoCT.nii.gz pseudoCT.json every run with pct.enabled: 1, when it exists pct.skull_mapping (with custom_slope / custom_intercept) and the segmentation (checksum of final_tissues.nii.gz) Placement run, <path.placement>/sub-XXX/<mode>/<target_name>/ placement_run.json heuristic, PlanTUS and TUS_entry placement, per placement.reuse placement.<mode> (without tool install paths), the transducer without its positions, and the segmentation (checksum of final_tissues.nii.gz) Pressure map, nii/sub-XXX_<medium>_T1w<affix>_pressure.nii.gz …_pressure.json a run with path.acoustic_input set to the NIfTI simulation.medium, grid (without thermal_*), layers, headmodel, pct, medium_properties, the transducer (geometry and grid positions), the subject and, for layered, the segmentation

io.cache_signature_check handles a mismatch (error by default, warn, off). An output without a sidecar (e.g. a pressure map from another tool) is used with the warning prestus:cache:unverified.

Placement (placement.reuse).

Value Effect auto (default) Reuse a recorded run whose settings match; otherwise run the placement again and replace the record. Under io.overwrite_files: never, a mismatch is handled like always always Require a recorded run never Always run the tool

placement.reuse is independent of io.overwrite_files: a PlanTUS or TUS_entry result is reused while the simulation stages are recomputed. placement_run.mat records are also read.

Pressure map (path.acoustic_input). Point path.acoustic_input at a T1w pressure NIfTI from an earlier run. The new run skips the acoustic simulation and the free-water baseline, puts the map onto its own grid (including an acoustic FOV), rescales it to its transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 using the sidecar's isppa.level_wcm2, and then runs acoustic analysis and the thermal stage as after a simulation. It needs the T1 → grid transform (simulation.medium layered or phantom, a 3D grid) and the k-Wave grid of the source stage (modules.run_source_setup: 1). In the Nexus, Results ▸ Follow-up… with New intensity or New timing writes such a config for you (Follow-up runs).

Limits:

  • The map is stored at T1 resolution, so a map from a finer simulation grid has lost some peak sharpness.
  • The map has no peak negative pressure, so the mechanical index uses the peak pressure (with a warning).
  • A map without a sidecar is used as it is and cannot be rescaled.
Sidecar format

Every sidecar starts with the same header:

{
  "sidecar_version": 1,
  "kind": "acoustic_pressure",
  "created": "2026-10-07T16:00:00",
  "generated_by": {"name": "PRESTUS", "version": "v0.6.1-42-gabc1234"},
  "subject_id": 1,
  "...": "kind-specific fields",
  "signature": {"...": "settings the output depends on"}
}

items.title: Overwrite Behaviour
items.text:
io.overwrite_files controls whether existing files are reused or recomputed.

Value Single run Chained pipelines: intermediate stages Chained pipelines: output stages never Reuse every existing file Resume from cache Skip if the output exists always (default) Recompute everything Resume from cache Always re-run, overwrite outputs force Same as always Always re-run Always re-run, overwrite outputs ask Prompt per file (interactive only) Resume from cache Skip if the output exists

Under never or ask, an acoustic or thermal stage that recomputes its results (no cache to reuse, e.g. with io.save_matrices: 0) still replaces its existing NIfTI outputs, so the NIfTI and CSV outputs of a folder always come from the same run. io.overwrite_simnibs governs SimNIBS segmentations separately.

Use force when an input of the intermediate caches has changed: transducer placement, transducer or source parameters, grid, segmentation, or medium properties. Grid, medium and acoustic caches detect such changes when they are reused (Cache reuse checks); force rebuilds them instead of stopping the run. Alternatively, delete the relevant cache/ files before resubmitting.

Chained pipelines

Chained pipelines split one run into separate jobs. Each job reuses what the previous stage wrote:

Pipeline Intermediate stages Output stages Async multi-transducer (doc) Stage-0 preproc, per-transducer acoustic, combine Joint thermal + report, water validation Multi-ISPPA (doc) Stage-1 acoustic Per-ISPPA thermal + report, summary report Uncertainty (doc) Stage-1 preprocessing Variant simulations + reports, uncertainty report

With the default always, resubmitting a finished chained run reuses the acoustic simulations and regenerates the CSV, NIfTI and HTML outputs. Within a chained run, sub-jobs that consume a shared cache (e.g. per-transducer acoustic jobs loading the Stage-0 grid) always load it, even under force. Only the stage that owns the cache rebuilds it.

items.title: Cache Reuse Checks
items.text:
Grid, medium and acoustic caches are named by subject, medium and affix only. Each cache therefore stores the settings it depends on (cache_signature). A reused cache built from different settings stops the run by default (io.cache_signature_check).

Mismatch handling

When a cache is reused (under io.overwrite_files: never, after a declined overwrite prompt, or in the intermediate stages of a chained pipeline under always) and the settings differ, io.cache_signature_check decides:

Value Effect error (default) Stop with prestus:cache:signatureMismatch, naming the differing keys. warn Warn and reuse the cache anyway. off No check.

A cache without a signature is reused with the warning prestus:cache:unverified. Stage-output sidecars are checked the same way (Starting from earlier stage outputs).

What each cache compares Cache Compared settings Grid (*_grid_cache*.mat) simulation.medium, grid, layers, headmodel, pct, and the transducer (geometry and positions after placement) Medium (*_medium_cache*.mat) the grid settings above, plus medium_properties Acoustic (*_results*.mat) the medium settings above except absorption_coeff (thermal only), plus subject_id and grid.acoustic_fov_*; not grid.thermal_*

For simulation.medium: phantom, each also compares the phantom file (size and modification date of final_tissues.nii.gz). For layered, each compares the segmentation by content (checksum of final_tissues.nii.gz), so a re-run of charm with another SimNIBS version or other settings is detected, while a copied or moved segmentation still matches. A cache written before the checksum was recorded counts the segmentation as changed when final_tissues.nii.gz is newer than the cache file.

Not compared, because they do not change these caches: paths, I/O, HPC and module flags; the drive level (target_isppa_wcm2, tx_calibration), which only scales the acoustic field; and, for grid and medium caches, the partial acoustic FOV (grid.acoustic_fov_*), which is cropped after the grid and medium stages. A run that reuses a cache keeps its own values of these settings.

Sub-jobs that load a cache owned by another stage of the same chained run are not checked.

items.title: PRESTUS Parameters
items.text:
This page lists every configuration parameter with its default, grouped by the YAML struct it belongs to.

On this page:

  • Subject and Platform (subject_id, platform): subject identifier and execution platform.
  • Simulation Type (simulation): medium, k-Wave code type, precision, interactive and debug modes, transducer coupling.
  • Simulation Backends (acoustic_backend, thermal_backend): which solver runs the acoustic and thermal steps, and its settings.
  • Data Paths (path): input, segmentation, simulation and Localite folders.
  • Environment & Toolbox Paths (startup): SimNIBS, MATLAB and other external tool paths.
  • I/O Management (io): output affix, overwriting, cache checks and which matrices are saved.
  • Pipeline Modules (modules): which pipeline stages run.
  • Transducer Specification (transducer): ISPPA target, transducer type, frequency, library entry and positions.
  • Transducer Placement (placement): placement mode, skin gap, reuse and the per-mode keys.
  • Simulation Grid (grid): resolution, dimensions, axisymmetric mode and PML.
  • Segmentation (segmentation): options passed to SimNIBS charm, and defacing.
  • Head Model & Segmentation Preprocessing (headmodel): padding and mask preprocessing of the head model.
  • Pseudo-CT Skull Property Mapping (pct): pseudo-CT generation and its mapping to skull properties.
  • Tissue Layers (layers): which segmentation labels form each tissue layer.
  • Tissue Acoustic & Thermal Properties (medium_properties): per-tissue acoustic and thermal properties.
  • Sonication Timing (timing): pulse and pulse-train durations and repetition intervals.
  • Thermal Settings (thermal): CEM43 variant, baseline temperatures and thermal sensor and logging.
  • Time Reversal (time_reversal): the extra point-source run per target.
  • Output Analysis (analysis): focus-area radius and MNI target or ROI for analysis.
  • Study Setup (study): study manifest and output folder name.
  • High-Performance Computing (hpc): GPU, partition, time and memory limits for cluster jobs.
  • Transducer Calibration (calibration): keys of config_calibration.yaml.

Parameters are organised in nested structs that map directly to YAML keys. config_default.yaml defines all parameters and their default values and should not be edited; a study config is merged on top and only needs the values that differ (see Configuring a study for the full layering, project defaults and overrides).
