Parameters can also be set in MATLAB before calling prestus_pipeline_start(parameters). Mandatory parameters have no meaningful default and must always be provided.

items.title: Subject and Platform (subject_id, platform)
items.text: Parameter Description Default Comments subject_id Subject identifier used for file naming and folder management. none Mandatory. Set before calling prestus_pipeline_start(parameters). platform Execution platform. 'auto' auto / slurm / qsub / matlab. auto detects SLURM or qsub and errors when neither is installed; use matlab to run in the current session. See HPC.

items.title: Simulation Type (simulation)
items.text: Parameter Description Default Comments medium Simulation medium type. 'layered' water / layered / phantom. Mandatory. code_type k-Wave backend. 'matlab_gpu' matlab_cpu / matlab_gpu / cpp_cpu / cpp_gpu / cpp_mlx. See k-Wave. precision Computational precision for acoustic and thermal simulations. 'single' single / double interactive Interactive mode with prompts and evolving plots. 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. If 0, see overwrite_files. debug Verbose debug mode with additional intermediate outputs. 0 1 = yes, 0 = no transducer_coupling How several transducers interact acoustically. 'coherent' coherent: pressure fields superpose in one k-Wave run (interference). async: each transducer is simulated separately and intensities are summed incoherently before the thermal simulation. See doc_multitransducer.md. uncertainty_temp_high Medium properties of the Temp-H variant (bounds that maximise brain heating) when simulation.uncertainty is on. '' A YAML file with a medium_properties block, merged onto the run's config: an absolute path, or a file name in config/uncertainty/. '' = config/uncertainty/config_medium_temp_high.yaml. The options.temp_high_config argument of uncertainty_pipeline takes precedence. See doc_uncertainty.md. uncertainty_temp_low Medium properties of the Temp-L variant (bounds that minimise brain heating). '' As uncertainty_temp_high; '' = config/uncertainty/config_medium_temp_low.yaml; options.temp_low_config takes precedence. uncertainty_trans_high Medium properties of the Trans-H variant (bounds that maximise brain intensity; acoustic only). '' As uncertainty_temp_high; '' = config/uncertainty/config_medium_trans_high.yaml; options.trans_high_config takes precedence. uncertainty_trans_low Medium properties of the Trans-L variant (bounds that minimise brain intensity; acoustic only). '' As uncertainty_temp_high; '' = config/uncertainty/config_medium_trans_low.yaml; options.trans_low_config takes precedence.

items.title: Simulation Backends (acoustic_backend, thermal_backend)
items.text:
Top-level keys (not nested under simulation). Pre-processing (segmentation, medium, grid, placement) and post-processing (analysis, NIfTI export, report) are shared by all backends. See Simulation backends for how the backends compare and when results are directly comparable.

Parameter Description Default Comments acoustic_backend Acoustic solver. 'kwave' kwave / kwave_elastic / babelbrain / jwave. Validated in load_parameters. babelbrain takes one transducer, with the beam along the grid z axis (not grid.mode: ras_plus); see BabelBrain geometry limits. kwave_elastic models shear waves in the skull (see Elastic skull). thermal_backend Bio-heat solver. 'kwave' kwave / babelbrain. babelbrain requires acoustic_backend: babelbrain, one transducer and no path.acoustic_input; invalid combinations error at config load. jwave has no thermal solver; pair it with kwave.

items.title: BabelBrain Settings (babelbrain)
items.text:
Used when acoustic_backend or thermal_backend is babelbrain, or when io.export_babelbrain: true. Full explanation in BabelBrain.

BabelBrain settings Parameter Description Default Comments python_env BabelBrain conda env (directory containing bin/python) or Python executable. '' Must be set; system python3 lacks BabelViscoFDTD. root BabelBrain source tree. '' Empty = external/BabelBrain submodule. computing_backend GPU/CPU backend. 'auto' auto / cuda / opencl / metal / cpu (or 1–4). auto: Metal on macOS, else CUDA if nvidia-smi finds a GPU, else CPU. The thermal engine has no CPU backend. device_name Device name. 'auto' Set explicitly when several GPUs are present. tx_system BabelBrain transducer preset. '' Empty = the PRESTUS transducer's ring geometry (as calibrated). A preset name uses BabelBrain's device definition. See Transducer mapping. ppw Points-per-wavelength floor for BabelBrain's own FDTD grid. 12 Lower = faster, more numerical dispersion. do_refocusing Apply BabelBrain's refocusing step. false Thermal then uses /p_amp_refocus. z_beyond_focus_mm Domain extent past the focus [mm]. 40 tight_narrow_beam BabelBrain's own lateral domain shrink. false Always off when grid.acoustic_fov_* is set. focal_calibration Geometric-fallback steering calibration. true Locate-only when explicit element phases exist. focal_calibration_target Quantity placed at focal_distance_ep. 'flhm_center' flhm_center / peak profile_calibration Refit drive phases to the continuous-bowl ideal. false BabelBrain only; moves it away from the k-Wave/jwave phases. Leave off for cross-backend comparison. water_amp_calibration Scale output so its free-water peak matches the analytic Rayleigh peak. true Removes BabelBrain's CFL-correction amplitude bias; requires explicit element phases. use_rayleigh_for_water Water-only solver. false false = FDTD (like-for-like with k-Wave/jwave). q_correction Bone Q-factor correction (BabelBrain QCorrection) of the relaxation attenuation model. [] [] = 1.0 on the non-CT path (realises the specified bone alpha_coeff), BabelBrain's 3.0 on the CT path. Realised bone attenuation scales ~1/Q; values > 0 override both paths. ct_mapping BabelBrain HU→property mapping. '' Empty = label mask with PRESTUS medium_properties. See CT-based skull properties. air_regions Internal air (sinuses, mastoid) as a pressure-release reflector mask. false Pseudo-CT path only (ct_mapping set); not applied to the free-water run. See Internal air. air_hu_window HU range classified as air for air_regions. [-1200, -400] BabelBrain's default. air_keep_boundary Keep air components touching the domain boundary. false By default they are removed with the exterior air (cropping can split it). ct_use_petra PETRA density formula for Webb-Marsac. false tx_mech_adjust_z_m Additional transducer standoff [m]. 0 Added to the automatic placement correction. z_steering_m Pin BabelBrain ZSteering [m]. ~ Empty = auto-derived. isppa_w_per_cm2 Override the Isppa given to BabelBrain thermal [W/cm²]. ~ Interpreted as the in-situ peak ISPPA in brain. Empty = derived from the scaled acoustic field (recommended; matches k-Wave thermal). cleanup_cache Delete the per-subject BabelBrain cache after reading. true Result HDF5s are moved out first. dry_run Prepare the BabelBrain inputs without simulating. false The pipeline stops after the acoustic stage; nothing is cached.

items.title: jwave Settings (jwave)
items.text:
Used when acoustic_backend: jwave.

jwave settings

PML thickness is set by grid.pml_size. Full reference: jwave configuration.

Parameter Description Default Comments python_env Python environment or executable with jwave. '' Empty = system python3. python_env_gpu GPU-capable Python environment. '' Empty = same as python_env. use_gpu Use GPU acceleration. ~ true / false / ~ (auto-detect). solver jwave solver. 'helmholtz' helmholtz (frequency-domain GMRES) / pseudo_spectral (time-domain, as kspaceFirstOrder*) / finite_differences (time-domain, FD stencils). fd_accuracy FD stencil order. 8 finite_differences only. gmres_restart GMRES restart parameter (Krylov subspace size). 10 jwave's default; larger values can destabilise GMRES in single precision. gmres_maxiter Maximum GMRES iterations. 1000 jwave's default. gmres_tol GMRES convergence tolerance. 1.0e-3 jwave's default. convergence_threshold Relative Helmholtz residual above which the run errors. 0.05 See ignore_convergence_threshold. ignore_convergence_threshold Warn instead of erroring above convergence_threshold. false The unconverged result is then returned. helmholtz_operator Density term of the Helmholtz solver. 'conservative' conservative: ρ∇·((1/ρ)∇p), source scaled by the local sound speed. jwave: jwave's built-in term, which underestimates transmission through density jumps (~20 % through a skull plate). See jwave: density term. precision Computational precision. 'single' single / double dry_run Write the HDF5 solver inputs only. false The pipeline stops after the acoustic stage and caches nothing. cleanup_cache Delete the HDF5 solver input after a successful run. true The input is rewritten on every run and never reused. Kept on dry runs and failed runs; set false to keep it for debugging.

items.title: Elastic Skull Settings (elastic)
items.text:
Used when acoustic_backend: kwave_elastic.

Elastic skull settings

Applied to the skull layers (skull, skull_cortical, skull_trabecular). Attenuations are power laws a·f^y [dB/(cm·MHz^y)], converted to the solver's y = 2 law so the value at the source frequency is exact. Sources and rationale: k-Wave elastic backend.

Parameter Description Default Comments shear_mapping Skull shear speed mapping. 'pichardo' pichardo: cS = a(f0)·ρ + b(f0), Pichardo et al. 2017 fits (a = 0.458, b = 545.52 at 270 kHz; a = 0.386, b = 815.51 at 836 kHz), interpolated linearly to the transducer frequency, extrapolated with a warning outside that range. Uses the density map (pseudo-CT or layer densities). off: cS = 0 (fluid skull through the elastic solver). shear_density_min No shear support at or below this density [kg/m³]. 1200 poisson_min Minimum Poisson ratio; caps cS at cL·√((1−2ν)/(2(1−ν))). 0.1 Bone: ν ≈ 0.2–0.35. alpha_coeff_shear Shear attenuation [dB/(cm·MHz^y)]. 43.63 Power law through Pichardo et al. 2017 (57 Np/m at 270 kHz, 373 Np/m at 836 kHz). alpha_power_shear Shear attenuation exponent y. 1.662 alpha_coeff_long Skull longitudinal attenuation in elastic runs [dB/(cm·MHz^y)]. 27.31 Power law through the values Pichardo et al. 2017 paired with their shear fit (33 Np/m at 270 kHz, 231 Np/m at 836 kHz). Used with long_attenuation: elastic. alpha_power_long Longitudinal attenuation exponent y. 1.722 long_attenuation Source of skull longitudinal attenuation. 'elastic' elastic: alpha_coeff_long. medium: keep the fluid/pCT skull alpha_coeff (effective values that already include shear losses). min_ppw_shear Warn below this many points per shear wavelength. 6

items.title: Data Paths (path)
items.text: Parameter Description Default Comments anat Absolute path to structural input data. none Mandatory sim Absolute path to simulation outputs. none Mandatory seg Absolute path to SimNIBS segmentations (m2m folders). none Mandatory placement Placement outputs: one folder per run, <placement>/sub-XXX/<mode>/<target_name>/ (heuristic, PlanTUS, TUS_entry). '' Empty = <sim>/placement. Share one folder across setups to reuse placements. See Where outputs live. localite_raw Raw Localite exports, <localite_raw>/sub-XXX/ses-XX/[<loc_folder>/]…. '' See Localite I/O. localite_post Ingested Localite markers, <localite_post>/sub-XXX/ses-XX/InstrumentMarker_sub-XXX_ses-XX.xml/.json. '' Written by neuronav_ingest_markers / neuronav_gui; read by placement.mode: 'localite' (automatic mode). localite_t1 Folder with the planning T1s loaded into Localite ([sub-XXX/]<localite_t1_pattern>). '' Empty = localite_raw. localite_t1_pattern File-name template of the planning T1; %s = sub-XXX. '%s_*T1*.nii*' Replaces neuronav_t1_pattern (still read). localite_export Output folder for files to import into Localite (heuristic placement), per subject sub-XXX/. '' Resolved into io.dir_localite_export. transducer_library Your own transducer library for every study of this project: equipment entries (*_transducer.yaml, *_driver.yaml), calibration entries and profiles/. '' A folder or a list of folders. Set it in the project copy of config_default.yaml. Checked after transducer.library_path and before the PRESTUS_TRANSDUCER_LIBRARY environment variable and the shipped library. See Your own transducers and calibrations. pct Pseudo-CT outputs, per subject <pct>/sub-NNN/. '' Empty = <parent of path.seg>/pct/sub-NNN/, next to the SimNIBS folder (never inside it). Resolved into io.dir_pct. acoustic_input Start from a prior pressure map instead of simulating: a peak-pressure NIfTI [Pa] in this subject's T1w space, e.g. an earlier run's nii/*_T1w*_pressure.nii.gz. '' Its JSON sidecar is checked against the current settings and used to rescale the map to transducer.target_isppa_wcm2; acoustic analysis and thermal simulation then run as usual. Replaces io.external_acoustic_nifti (still read). See Starting from earlier stage outputs. localite Deprecated. '' Read as localite_raw and as localite_export when those are empty. t1_pattern T1 image path template relative to path.anat. 'sub-%1$03d_T1w.nii*' Supports %03d-style subject ID substitution t2_pattern T2 image path template relative to path.anat. '' Optional; empty skips the T2 (e.g. 'sub-%1$03d_T2w.nii*'). ct_pattern Measured CT path template relative to path.anat, read by the skull mapping when pct.enabled is 1. '' In Hounsfield units and co-registered to the T1w. Empty = the pseudo-CT generated from the UTE image in t2_pattern. See doc.

items.title: Environment & Toolbox Paths (startup)
items.text:
Segmentation and MNI conversion need startup.simnibs_bin_path. The other paths are needed for pseudo-CT generation or to add folders to the MATLAB path.

Environment and toolbox paths Parameter Description Comments simnibs_bin_path Absolute path to the bin folder of a SimNIBS 4 install (holds charm). Mandatory for segmentation and MNI conversion. Selects the SimNIBS version. matlab_bin_path Absolute path to MATLAB binary. Required for pseudoCT generation on HPC (e.g. /opt/matlab/R2024a/bin/matlab). Local execution falls back to matlabroot. fsl_bin_path Absolute path to FSL bin directory. Required for pseudoCT generation (e.g. /opt/fsl/bin). Prepended to PATH at runtime. ants_bin_path Absolute path to ANTs bin directory. Required for pseudoCT generation (e.g. /opt/ants/bin). Prepended to PATH at runtime. ants_simg_path ANTs Singularity image (.simg/.sif). When set, ANTs tools run via singularity exec. modules_to_load HPC environment modules loaded before pseudoCT generation. e.g. ['matlab/R2023b', 'fsl/6.0.7', 'ants/2.5.3'] paths_to_add Paths to add with addpath(). [cell] e.g. {"path/to/x"} subpaths_to_add Paths to add recursively with addpath(genpath()). [cell]; relative to the MATLAB working directory

items.title: I/O Management (io)
items.text:
Parameter Description Default Comments output_affix Optional affix for output file names. '' Differentiates outputs for the same subject/transducer (e.g. different intensities or targets) overwrite_files File overwrite behaviour. 'always' never / always / force / ask. Does NOT apply to SimNIBS segmentations. In chained pipelines (async, multi-ISPPA, uncertainty), always re-runs only the output stages (CSV, NIfTI, HTML report) and reuses cached intermediates; force re-runs every stage. See Overwrite behaviour. cache_signature_check Response when a reused grid, medium or acoustic cache, or a stage output a run starts from (placement run, pseudo-CT, pressure map), was built from different settings. 'error' error / warn (reuse anyway) / off. Caches: applies when one is reused because of overwrite_files: never (or a declined overwrite). See Cache reuse checks and Starting from earlier stage outputs. overwrite_simnibs Overwrite SimNIBS segmentation results? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. Re-runs charm (--forcerun), which deletes the m2m folder first. Without it, an existing segmentation is reused even when another SimNIBS version or other charm settings are selected (with a warning). save_matrices Save all intermediate matrices (.mat / cache files)? [] 1 = save all, 0 = save none, [] = use the per-step defaults. Applies to every per-step matrix flag left empty; a per-step flag set to 0/1 always wins. 0 also triggers cleanup of uncertainty intermediates. save_source_matrices Save kwave_source.mat (transducer source array)? [] → 1 [] inherits save_matrices, else default. Needed by multi-stage pipelines (e.g. uncertainty). save_acoustic_matrices Save acoustic results (sensor_data, kgrid, medium; can be very large)? [] → 0 [] inherits save_matrices, else default. Needed to reload acoustics (e.g. separate thermal runs, calibration debugging). save_thermal_matrices Save heating_res.mat (temperature time series and field maps)? [] → 1 [] inherits save_matrices, else default. save_grid_cache / save_medium_cache Save grid / medium caches? unset → 0 Inherit save_matrices when unset. save_property_maps Save per-property NIfTIs to nii/properties/ (layered medium only)? 0 Not affected by save_matrices. save_MNI Save NIfTI outputs in MNI space in addition to native T1w space (requires SimNIBS m2m folder)? 1 Not affected by save_matrices. save_heatingvideo Save a video of incremental heating? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no save_Ipa Save the pulse-average intensity (Ipa) NIfTI map? 1 Suppressed automatically when timing.pd is absent. save_Ita Save the temporal-average intensity (Ita) NIfTI map? 1 Suppressed automatically when timing.pd/timing.pri are absent. save_p_complex Save the complex pressure field (p_complex) in the acoustic cache? 0 Large. deface_plots Remove facial anatomy from all QC figures? 1 1 = yes, 0 = no. Uses the SimNIBS eye label to anchor the cut plane ~30 mm posterior to the eye socket (ear-canal level). Requires the SimNIBS segmentation (path.seg). Has no effect on saved NIfTIs; see segmentation.deface for that. adopted_heatmap Path to an existing temperature heatmap NIfTI (heating_end.nii.gz) to use as the thermal starting point for a follow-up simulation. Set automatically by the sequential dispatcher; can be overridden manually. none Optional. Used for sequential multi-target runs. adopted_cem43 Path to an existing CEM43 heatmap NIfTI to accumulate heating across runs. Set automatically by the sequential dispatcher. none Optional. Used for sequential multi-target runs. adopted_cem43_iso Path to an existing ISO-variant CEM43 heatmap NIfTI (CEM43_iso_end.nii.gz) to accumulate across runs. Set automatically alongside adopted_cem43 by the sequential dispatcher. none Optional. Used for sequential multi-target runs. Runtime-derived io fields

Runtime-derived (set by path_log_setup):

Field Description dir_output Resolved per-subject output directory. Set from path.sim (+ subject subfolder). dir_nii NIfTI output subfolder (nii/). Created automatically. dir_nii_T1w Alias for dir_nii; space encoded in filename. dir_nii_MNI Alias for dir_nii; space encoded in filename. dir_img Image/figure output subfolder (img/). Used for all acoustic, thermal, and preprocessing figures. Created automatically. dir_tabular Directory for per-subject CSV results tables (same as dir_output). dir_reports Directory for simulation reports (same as dir_output). dir_logs Log subfolder (log/). Created automatically. dir_cache Cache subfolder (cache/). Created automatically. dir_debug Debug subfolder (debug/). Created when simulation.debug = 1. dir_debug_preproc Debug subfolder for preprocessing (debug/preproc/). dir_debug_medium Debug subfolder for medium setup (debug/medium/). dir_debug_source Debug subfolder for source setup (debug/source/). dir_pct Resolved subject pCT directory (get_pct_dir): <path.pct>/sub-NNN, or <parent of path.seg>/pct/sub-NNN. dir_localite_export Per-subject Localite export folder (<path.localite_export>/sub-XXX/, fallback path.localite); '' if unset. filename_table Path to the per-subject CSV results table. filename_kwave_source Path to cached k-Wave source .mat file. Set by source_sensor_setup.

items.title: Pipeline Modules (modules)
items.text:
Parameter Description Default Comments run_transducer_placement Resolve trans_pos/focus_pos from placement.mode. 1 Required when placement.manual.coordinate_space is ras or mni (positions are converted here). run_grid_setup Setup grid and run head processing. 1 Mandatory for simulations. run_medium_setup Map medium acoustic properties. 1 Mandatory for simulations. run_source_setup Set up acoustic source. 1 Mandatory for simulations. run_water_baseline Run a free-water simulation that records the ISPPA of the current drive, for scaling to transducer.target_isppa_wcm2. 'auto' auto: when a target is set and the transducer has no calibration ISPPA or the target differs from it. 1: always. 0: only when the target differs from a calibration ISPPA. A target that cannot be met stops the run (prestus:isppa:noBaseline). See ISPPA targeting. run_acoustic_sims Run acoustic simulations. 1 run_acoustic_analysis Run acoustic analysis. 1 run_heating_sims Run thermal simulations. 0 Enable after acoustic results are validated. run_thermal_analysis Run thermal analysis. 1 run_nifti_creation Export results as NIfTI files. 1 run_posthoc_water_sims Run free-water reference simulations after head simulations. 1 generate_report Generate self-contained HTML simulation report. 1 report_style Visual skin of the HTML report: instrument, classic (pre-v0.6.1 look), compact, paper. Changes presentation only, not content. 'instrument' Try skins on an existing output folder with preview_report_styles(<subject dir>). report_style_switcher Embed all skins plus a dropdown to switch between them in the report. 0 run_targeting_analysis Measure targeting accuracy from the focal-mask NIfTIs: simulated focus vs planned focus (native), vs MNI target / ROI (MNI). Writes sub-XXX_<medium><affix>_targeting.csv. 1 Layered or phantom media; needs run_nifti_creation. See Targeting accuracy. generate_group_report Aggregate completed subjects into a group HTML report at the end of the run. 1 Best-effort; auto-discovers subjects. Or run prestus_group_report_start manually. Switched off for runs started by prestus_study_start, which builds one study report at the end. segmentation_only Stop after segmentation; skip grid setup and all simulations. 0 Only has effect when simulation.medium = 'layered'.

All flags: 1 = yes, 0 = no.

items.title: Transducer Specification (transducer)
items.text:
See doc_transducer.md.

Except target_isppa_wcm2 (default 30), the fields have no defaults and must be set in the study config or come from the equipment library (serial).

Parameter Description Comments target_isppa_wcm2 Target free-water ISPPA [W/cm²] of this transducer alone. Default 30. Scalar: the field is scaled to it (needs a free-water baseline; see modules.run_water_baseline). Vector: one thermal job per value (multi-intensity). Empty []: no scaling, the field is reported at elem_p_amp. Several transducers: each transducer's own target; coherent runs set each drive before the simulation, async runs scale each field before combining (see Multi-transducer: ISPPA targets). type Type of transducer array. annular / matrix. Mandatory. freq_hz Fundamental frequency [Hz]. Shared across all elements. serial Equipment serial; geometry, phases and drive come from the equipment config and transducer library. See doc_transducer_library.md. Values set in the study config take precedence. combo.ds_serial Driving-system serial. Selects the calibration entry for <serial> with this driving system; without it only the driving-system-agnostic entry is looked up. library_path Folder with your own library entries. Calibration entries there are used when one exists for this combo, otherwise the shipped config/calibration/ (with a warning). Equipment entries there (*_transducer.yaml, *_driver.yaml) add transducers or replace shipped ones. See Your own transducers and calibrations. max_elem_p_amp Largest drive your driving system delivers [Pa, as elem_p_amp]. Empty = the drive_limit of the combo in the equipment entry, if any. A library drive above it warns (resolve_transducer_from_serial:driveLimit) with the largest ISPPA reachable at that depth. See Drive limits. condition Experimental, not validated. Dephased library condition (conditions.<label> in the library entry). Replaces the focal-depth lookup; focal_distance_ep defaults to the condition's nominal setpoint. See Dephased conditions. trans_pos Transducer position (XYZ, bowl apex). T1 voxels by default; RAS+ or MNI mm via placement.manual.coordinate_space. focus_pos Focus (target) position (XYZ). T1 voxels by default; RAS+ or MNI mm via placement.manual.coordinate_space. focal_distance_ep Focal depth setting: the depth the device is set to focus at, from the exit plane [mm]. For annular arrays it selects the library phases and drive, so the simulated focus lands here whatever the trans_pos→focus_pos distance (the planned target depth). Empty = that distance minus focal_distance_offset (focal_distance_calculation). focal_distance_bowl Focal depth setting from the bowl apex [mm]. focal_distance_ep + bowl-to-exit-plane offset; set either. focal_distance_offset Offset between transducer bowl and exit plane [mm]. Derived from curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm. Not set by user.

items.title: Annular Array Definition (annular)
items.text: Parameter Description Comments elem_p_amp Pressure amplitude [Pa]; scalar or one value per element. Advanced: from calibration. Empty with a target ISPPA: a nominal drive scaled to it. elem_amp is the deprecated name (renamed on load with a warning). elem_phase_deg Source phase per element [degrees]. Advanced: from calibration. Empty: steered to focal_distance_ep (geometric phases for custom geometry). elem_n Number of transducer elements. elem_id_mm Inner diameter of each element [mm]. elem_od_mm Outer diameter of each element [mm]. curv_radius_mm Radius of curvature of the transducer bowl [mm]. Inf (YAML .inf) = flat element, e.g. a plane piston: its face at trans_pos is the exit plane; needs grid.use_kWaveArray: 1, in 3D a single disc. See Flat elements. dist_geom_ep_mm Distance from geometric focus to transducer plane [mm]. If not provided, the exit plane is the bowl rim: √(curv_radius_mm² − (max(elem_od_mm)/2)²) (Inf for flat elements). depth_mm Transducer depth [mm]. Visualization only.

items.title: Matrix Array Definition (matrix)
items.text: Parameter Description Comments elem_p_amp Pressure amplitude [Pa]; scalar or one value per element. Advanced: from calibration. Empty with a target ISPPA: a nominal drive scaled to it. elem_amp is the deprecated name (renamed on load with a warning). depth_mm Transducer depth [mm]. Visualization only. steering Steering mode of the transducer. 1D = axial only, 3D = volumetric steering. elem_shape Shape of individual elements. Options: rect, disc, bowl. Element area is defined using the rectangular dimensions and projected onto the selected shape, unless elem_diameter_mm is set. elem_height_mm Element height [mm], along y. rect elements: size along y; disc/bowl: sets the equal-area diameter. elem_width_mm Element width [mm], along x. rect elements: size along x; disc/bowl: sets the equal-area diameter. elem_diameter_mm Aperture diameter of disc/bowl elements [mm]. Optional. Empty = equal-area diameter from elem_width_mm × elem_height_mm (flat disc area for disc, spherical-cap area for bowl). Also sets the element size in the transducer mask. elem_phase_override_deg Calibrated per-element phases [deg]. Optional, one value per element (after Clover replication). Replaces the geometric steering phases toward focus_pos; element orientation is unchanged. Empty = geometric steering. use_steering_correction Scale the element drive by the steering correction k(target). Default true. Used when the transducer library (or steering_correction) holds one; see Steering correction of matrix arrays. steering_correction Steering correction given inline. Optional struct as written by build_steering_correction. Empty = from the transducer library. outer_diameter_mm Outer diameter of the transducer [mm]. Defines active aperture boundary. is_curved Whether the array has a curved surface. false = flat array: every element faces +z, curv_radius_mm is not used, elem_shape must be rect or disc. curv_radius_mm Radius of curvature (ROC) of the transducer bowl [mm]. Defines natural focus. Depends on is_curved. dist_geom_ep_mm Distance from geometric focus to transducer plane [mm]. If not provided, the exit plane is the bowl rim: √(curv_radius_mm² − (outer_diameter_mm/2)²). Depends on is_curved. is_clover_setup Enables Clover (multi-array) configuration. Replicates array into multiple leaves. matrix_shape.type Method used to define element positions. Options: define_here, extract_from_file.

items.title: Matrix: Clover (clover)
items.text: Clover keys Parameter Description Comments n_leaves Number of Clover leaves. Any positive integer; one leaf stays on the parent axis unless elevation_deg is set. ROC_parent Radius of curvature of the combined Clover setup [mm]. items.title: Simulation Grid (grid)
items.text: Parameter Description Default Comments resolution_mm Grid resolution (must be isotropic) [mm]. 0.5 default_dims Requested grid dimensions [voxels per dimension], or 'auto'. 'auto' Directly sets the simulation grid for water and phantom media (a phantom uses its own size unless it matches). For layered, the grid is determined by head preprocessing and this value is not used. 'auto' (water only, water_grid_dims) sizes the grid to the transducer, as the acoustic FOV of a head simulation: aperture + 2 × water_margin_mm (default 5 mm) laterally, focal distance from the bowl + z_beyond_focus_mm (default 40 mm) axially; [Nlateral, Naxial] with axisymmetric. For the shipped transducers this is 15–80 % of the points of [144, 144, 400] (the default until 2026-10) with the same free-water ISPPA (within 0.003 %) and focus (k-Wave drive benchmark). A non-annular (matrix) transducer placed by trans_pos/focus_pos, which are grid indices, keeps [144, 144, 400] ([144, 400] axisymmetric) with a warning. axisymmetric Run axisymmetric 2D simulation (kspaceFirstOrderAS). 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. See doc_simulations-acoustic.md. axisymmetric_output Form of axisymmetric results. 'auto' 'auto': expanded to 3D for phantom media or when heating is requested, otherwise the mirrored 2D plane. '2d': always the plane (not with heating); for fine grids, where the 3D expansion would not fit in memory. '3d': always expanded. mode Grid orientation before cropping. 'focal_axis' focal_axis: rotate so the mean beam axis of all transducers (beams averaged as axes) is z. transducer_axis: focal axis of transducer 1. ras_plus: no rotation, only rescaling. (principal_axis was removed and errors.) See Head preprocessing. focal_axis_min_norm Fallback threshold of focal_axis mode. 0.5 When the mean beam-axis vector is shorter than this (beam axes too spread; only possible with three or more transducers), transducer 1's axis is used. pml_size Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) size [voxels]. 'auto' 'auto' chooses a size that keeps FFT grid sizes small-prime (k-Wave getOptimalPMLSize); a number fixes it. Absorbs waves at boundaries. Recommended for 3D. See k-Wave docs. water_baseline_grid Grid of the k-Wave free-water baseline (ISPPA targeting). 'beam' 'beam': the box around the source and each beam axis from the bowl to 40 mm beyond the deeper of focus and geometric focus, +10 mm (WATER_BASELINE_BOX); in water nothing outside reflects back, so the free-field result is the same at a fraction of the cost. 'full': the whole simulation grid. jwave and axisymmetric runs use the full grid. pml_size_range Search range [min, max] of pml_size: 'auto' [grid points]. [10, 40] Passed to k-Wave's getOptimalPMLSize, which picks the FFT-friendliest size in the range. A thicker layer absorbs better at grazing incidence and costs grid points. pml_alpha PML absorption [Nepers per grid point]. [] Empty: k-Wave's default (2). Passed as k-Wave's PMLAlpha. source_ppw Points per wavelength (PPW) override. [] Calculated internally from resolution_mm and the medium's maximum sound speed if not set. Setting this overrides the internal calculation and fixes the number of spatial samples per wavelength used to derive the time step. min_ppw Minimum acceptable PPW at the fundamental frequency. 6 Checked against the slowest medium sound speed (worst-case spatial sampling). A warning is raised if the actual PPW falls below this value, along with the maximum resolution_mm that would satisfy it. source_cfl Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) fraction. 0.15 Controls temporal resolution independently of spatial resolution. Given a fixed spatial step dx, the time step is dt = CFL × dx / c_max, where c_max is the fastest medium sound speed (typically skull at ~2800 m/s). Smaller CFL = finer temporal sampling and must remain below the stability limit. Set to 0.15 (half k-Wave's default of 0.3) for additional stability margin in heterogeneous skull simulations. Can be relaxed toward 0.3 to reduce runtime, but should be validated against checkStability output. source_limit_fraction Fraction of the stability limit to use for time step. 0.9 After source setup, checkStability is called; if the CFL-derived dt exceeds the estimated limit, source setup reruns with dt = source_limit_fraction × dt_stability_limit. The final effective dt may therefore be smaller than CFL × dx / c_max. Set to 0 to disable. steady_state_transits Number of domain-diagonal one-way transits (at min. sound speed) before recording starts. 1 Total simulation duration is transits × diagonal / c_min. Compact, highly reflective domains (e.g. a partial-FOV crop with a high skull/water impedance mismatch, ~50% reflection coefficient for typical skull properties) may need more than one transit for multiply-reflected energy to decay to true periodic steady state. jwave's own cross-validation test uses roundtrips=20. steady_state_num_periods Number of trailing wave periods recorded as the steady-state window. 3 sensor.record_start_index is set so the last num_periods periods of the simulation are recorded for p_max_all/p_min_all/p_final. Increase together with steady_state_transits if reported Isppa/focal depth are still drifting as either is increased; a converged setup should stop changing further. bli_tolerance kWaveArray band-limited interpolation (BLI) tolerance. [] Empty: 0.1 (3D), 0.01 (axisymmetric). Smaller values keep more of the sinc tails (more source grid points). bli_upsampling_rate kWaveArray integration points per grid point. [] Empty: 10 (3D), 100 (axisymmetric). source_ppp Time steps per wave period (PPP) override. [] When set, dt = period / source_ppp; source_ppw and source_cfl are not used. For matching a reference simulation's time step (e.g. the ITRUSST k-Wave references). The stability recheck (source_limit_fraction) still applies. sim_time_us Fixed simulation duration [µs]. [] When set, replaces steady_state_transits (and jwave's PML margin); the last steady_state_num_periods periods of this duration are recorded. max_expand Maximum grid expansion for prime-number FFT optimisation [voxels]. 40 use_kWaveArray Use the kWaveArray class for transducer modelling? 1 1 = yes, 0 = no acoustic_fov_diameter_mm Lateral extent of the acoustic simulation FOV [mm], centred on the beam axis. When set together with acoustic_fov_length_mm, the acoustic simulation runs on a cropped sub-grid rather than the full head grid. Thermal simulation runs on the full head grid unless thermal_use_acoustic_fov: 1. [] Optional. 'auto': the outer element diameter of transducer(1). See doc_limited_fov.md. acoustic_fov_length_mm Axial extent of the acoustic simulation FOV [mm], starting from the bowl apex (trans_pos) and extending distally. Must be large enough to enclose the focus and any near-field region of interest. [] Optional. Requires acoustic_fov_diameter_mm. 'auto': the trans_pos-to-focus_pos distance + z_beyond_focus_mm. See doc_limited_fov.md. thermal_use_acoustic_fov Run the thermal simulation within the acoustic FOV instead of the full grid. 0 1 is faster, with a less accurate cooling boundary. See doc_limited_fov.md. thermal_resolution_mm Grid resolution for the thermal simulation [mm]. When set to a value larger than resolution_mm, the acoustic pressure field is resampled to a coarser grid before thermal simulation, reducing memory and runtime. [] Optional. Defaults to resolution_mm (same grid). thermal_fov_mm Spatial extent of the thermal simulation domain [mm], as a [1×3] vector [x y z]. When set, the thermal grid is cropped to a box of this size centred on the focus. Unlike the acoustic FOV crop, the thermal FOV has no physical justification for excluding regions: heat diffuses well beyond the focal zone, and cropping can underestimate temperature rise in neighbouring tissue. Use only for rapid prototyping, not for safety-critical results. [] Optional. See doc_limited_fov.md.

items.title: Head Model & Segmentation Preprocessing (headmodel)
items.text:
See doc_preproc.md.

Head model keys Parameter Description Default Comments head_pad_mm Symmetric padding of the rotated head volume before CSF expansion and cropping [mm]; bowls outside the volume are auto-padded. 0 csf_expansion Dilation of the CSF brain mask into surrounding head regions [mm]. 40 Converted to voxels at the grid resolution (preproc_crop_eCSF). smooth_method Mask smoothing filter type. 'gaussian' gaussian / box / off smooth_threshold_skull Binarisation threshold for skull mask; higher = thinner mask. 0.5 smooth_threshold_other Binarisation threshold for other masks; higher = thinner mask. 0.5 smooth_fwhm_mm FWHM of smoothing kernel [mm]. 1 smooth_properties Apply smoothing to acoustic property maps as well? false skull_fill_method Method for filling holes in the skull. 'rubberwrap' rubberwrap / imclose skull_wrap_radius_mm Rubber-wrap radius [mm]. 5 The wrap bridges skull holes up to about twice this width where brain meets skin; larger fills wider holes. Replaces skull_wrap_radius [grid voxels], which is converted at the run's grid.resolution_mm. skull_wrap_visualize Visualize rubber-wrap result? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. Avoid on HPC. reuse_across_placements Build the smoothed head model once per subject and only rotate and crop it for each transducer placement. false Saves the smoothing and hole filling (most of head preprocessing at fine resolution) in every run after the first of a subject: other poses, aims or affixes in the same output folder. Cached as <dir_cache>/sub-XXX_<medium>_headmodel_<res>mm.mat with the settings it depends on; rebuilt when they change. With grid.mode: ras_plus the result equals per-placement preprocessing exactly (checked on one head, two poses). With a rotated mode the smoothing precedes the rotation and the labels are resampled once more (nearest neighbour), which changes thin skull layers (skull-layer Dice 0.80–0.90 against per-placement preprocessing at 1 mm; a warning says so). Needs the planning T1 and the segmentation on one voxel grid.

items.title: Tissue Layers (layers)
items.text:
See doc_preproc.md.

Maps tissue compartment names to their SimNIBS charm label indices. Compartments are modelled in listed order; any voxel label not assigned to a named compartment is treated as water. Charm label values are hardcoded in charm_seg_labels(). Layers can be removed or added.

Layer Default charm labels Comments water [0, 3, 6, 9, 10] Baseline layer; all unassigned voxels are treated as water brain [1, 2] White matter + grey matter skin [5] skull [4] Single skull layer; used when cortical/trabecular split is not needed skull_cortical [7] Cortical bone; used in multi-layer skull model skull_trabecular [8] Trabecular bone; used in multi-layer skull model

items.title: Tissue Acoustic & Thermal Properties (medium_properties)
items.text:
See doc_medium.md.

Each tissue compartment (water, brain, skin, skull, skull_trabecular, skull_cortical) carries the following fields:

Field Description Units / Reference sound_speed Speed of sound. m/s; source: ITRUSST benchmarks density Density. kg/m³; source: ITRUSST benchmarks alpha_coeff Attenuation coefficient. dB/cm/MHz alpha_power Attenuation power law exponent. dimensionless thermal_conductivity Thermal conductivity. W/m/°C; source: Tissue Properties DB specific_heat_capacity Specific heat capacity. J/kg/°C; source: Tissue Properties DB perfusion Perfusion / heat transfer rate. mL/min/kg; source: Tissue Properties DB absorption_fraction Fraction of attenuation converted to heat. Set this or absorption_coeff; a config layer that sets one empties the other (Heat deposition). Default for every tissue. [0–1]; source: Pinton et al., 2012 absorption_coeff Absorption coefficient, with the power law alpha_power; empty by default. Set this or absorption_fraction. dB/cm/MHz; source: Pinton et al., 2012

items.title: Sonication Timing (timing)
items.text:
See doc_simulations-thermal.md.

Protocol duration fields must be set for thermal simulations.

Parameter Description Default Comments pd Pulse Duration (PD) [s]. 0 Duty cycle = pd/pri. pri Pulse Repetition Interval (PRI) [s]. 0 PRF = 1/pri. ptd Pulse Train Duration (PTD) [s]. 0 pt_timestep Modelling time step within a pulse train [s]; used with equal_step_duration: 1. 0.02 ptri Pulse Train Repetition Interval (PTRI) [s]. 0 OFF duration = ptri − ptd. ptrd Pulse Train Repetition Duration (PTRD) [s]. 0 post_ptri_dur Cooling period after the PTRD [s]. 0 post_pt_timestep Modelling time step between pulse trains and after the PTRD [s]. 1 equal_step_duration Equal step durations for on and off cycles? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no pulse_ramp_dur Rise (= fall) duration of the amplitude ramp at each end of a pulse [s]. (not set) = 0 Not in config_default.yaml. Scales the pulse-average intensity: Ipa = factor × Itp (compute_ramp_factor). pulse_ramp_shape Ramp shape: 'linear' or 'tukey' (raised cosine). (not set) = 'linear' Used with pulse_ramp_dur.

The Nexus draws this protocol (pulse, pulse train, repetitions) and exchanges it with the TUS calculator; see Nexus.

items.title: Thermal Settings (thermal)
items.text:
See doc_simulations-thermal.md.

'grid' 'grid': ± along each grid axis, as when editing voxel coordinates (6 poses per distance; the bowl is not re-seated, so beyond ~1 mm it can cut into or lift off the scalp). See Pose workflow. pose_workflow.n_top Number of best poses (by predicted target pressure after aim correction) to verify. 5 The planned pose is always verified as the reference. pose_workflow.poses Pose ids of the pose table to verify as well. [] pose_workflow.aim Aim of the verification runs. [] [] = no limit. pose_workflow.final_run Run the best pose on the full grid with the configured modules. true Affix <affix>_posebest. pose_workflow.search_memorylimit hpc.memorylimit of the search run [GB]. [] [] = hpc.memorylimit. The search records the field over all candidate poses.

items.title: Transducer Calibration (calibration)
items.text:
See doc_calibration.md.

Calibration keys

A separate config_calibration.yaml applies for calibration workflows and is loaded as parameters.calibration.

Parameter Description Comments path_input_axial Directory containing axial intensity profiles; char_data_path in the equipment YAML is relative to it. Usually <PRESTUS>/local/profiles/ (see doc_transducer_library.md, Appendix). path_output Directory for saving free-water simulation results. path_output_profiles Directory for saving optimised profile data. filename_calibrated_CSV Filename of calibrated CSV data. Mandatory only when not generated within standalone script. save_in_calibration_folder Save in path_output (TRUE) or sim_path (FALSE). If TRUE, results are appended to existing calibration data. combinations Equipment combinations (must refer to entries in config_equipment.yaml). Multiple combinations can be specified. focal_depths_wrt_exit_plane List of focal depths to characterise [mm]. desired_intensities Desired free-water intensities [W/cm²]. add_FDO Append Focal Distance Offset (bowl-to-exit-plane distance)? Set to 1 if zero point in profiles reflects exit plane rather than bowl. axisymmetric2D Use axisymmetric 2D instead of default 3D free-water simulations? 1 = yes, 0 = no force_kwavearray Force use of kWaveArray for free-water simulations? If 0, uses the setting in the default/study config. opt_method Optimisation method. FEXminimize (open source) / GlobalSearch (MATLAB Global Optimization Toolbox) opt_limits Distance limits for optimisation [mm]. opt_weights Weighting of original profile during fitting. 1 = equal; >1 = Gaussian (narrower with larger values) opt_seed Random seed for optimisation. opt_use_initial_phases Use phases from transducer.annular.elem_phase_rad as the initial guess instead of random initialization. false (default); set to true when manufacturer-provided or previously calibrated phases are available. opt_upper_velocity Upper velocity in global search opt_phase_precession Constrain element phases during optimisation. false (default) = independent; 'linear' = strict ramp (phase_start + i * phase_step, 2 free params); 'monotonic' = ordered phases via cumulative non-negative increments (N params, monotonically constrained). opt_amp_validation Run free-water simulation to validate phases and amplitudes? 'always' (default) / 'never' / 'initial' (only for the first target intensity) / 'final' (only for the final target intensity) skip_front_peak_mm Distance from profile start to ignore [mm]. Avoids near-field artefacts in peak/FWHM calculations. profile_align Focus alignment when interpolating measured profiles to an unmeasured focal depth. 'label' (default) = column focal-depth headers; 'peak' = intensity peak beyond skip_front_peak_mm. See interpolate_axial_profiles. max_extrapolation_mm How far outside the measured depth range a desired depth may lie [mm]. 0 (default) = no extrapolation (error). Otherwise the nearest measured profile, shifted to the desired depth. focal_reference Convention for what a quoted focal depth means. flhm_3db (default, ITRUSST, intensity ≥ peak/2) / flhm_6db (Imasonic/IGT, intensity ≥ peak/4) / peak (raw intensity peak). Recorded into the sidecar YAML's meta.calibration.focal_reference. See doc_calibration.md.

items.title: Transducer Placement
items.text:
The transducer position decides where the beam enters the head, which part of the skull it crosses and where the focus lies relative to the target, so it shapes every acoustic and thermal result of a head simulation. This page covers how PRESTUS obtains the transducer and focus positions: entered by hand, or derived by one of several placement modes that share one exit-plane geometry.

On this page:

  • Choosing a Placement Mode: the modes, what each optimises and what each needs.
  • Placement Report: the HTML report written after placement.
  • Manual Coordinate Selection: entering positions in voxels, RAS mm or MNI mm.

At a glance

  • When you need it: Every head simulation. Free-water simulations need no target.
  • Before you start: The T1w planning image; most modes also need a SimNIBS segmentation.

PRESTUS works with the transducer (transducer.trans_pos) and the target (transducer.focus_pos) as voxels of the T1w planning image. The transducer coordinate is the bowl apex, not the exit plane of a curved transducer. All modes put the exit plane curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm in front of the apex (BabelBrain's FocalLength − NaturalOutPlaneDistance) and, where they place the transducer on the scalp, leave placement.skin_gap_mm (default 5 mm) between scalp and exit plane. You can enter both points directly (in voxels, subject RAS mm or MNI mm), or let a placement mode derive them.

items.title: Choosing a Placement Mode
items.text:
Mode Primary objective Requires manual User-specified Coordinates in config (T1 voxels, RAS+ mm or MNI mm) localite Recorded neuronavigation pose Localite XML mni Transducer and focus given in MNI mm; transducer snapped to the scalp SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX folder heuristic Skull-surface proximity to MNI target SimNIBS segmentation plantus Beam–target overlap + skull acoustics SimNIBS mesh + PlanTUS install tus_entry Transducer-scalp coupling geometry Scalp mask + TUS_entry R install

Each mode has its own page: manual, MNI, heuristic, PlanTUS, TUS_entry and Localite. Whatever the mode, the resolved positions are written to sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json in the output folder. Coordinate conventions are described in Coordinate systems.

Heuristic or PlanTUS? heuristic plantus Input final_tissues.nii.gz (label volume) Full SimNIBS mesh (sub-XXX.msh) + SimNIBS Python env Strategy Single-objective sphere-expansion on skull surface Multi-objective optimisation (beam overlap, skin/skull angles, skull thickness, target distance) Focal distance sweep No Yes External dependency None PlanTUS + SimNIBS installation

Use heuristic when only a tissue-label segmentation is available or for batch jobs on an HPC cluster. Use plantus when the full SimNIBS mesh is available and you want multi-objective optimisation or transducer selection across focal distances.

items.title: Placement Report
items.text:
After placement, PRESTUS writes a stand-alone HTML report, sub-XXX_placement_<mode><affix>.html, to io.dir_reports (placement.report, default true).

Report contents

It holds the target, the transducer and focus positions (T1 voxels and subject RAS mm, with transducer–focus and focus–target distances), the T1 overlay figure and the placement configuration. For placement.mode: 'plantus' it adds the criteria evaluation: diagnostics, each criterion at the placed spot, the criterion maps and the weight sweep. A failed report is a warning, not an error. The report is skipped when no output directory is known.

items.title: Manual Coordinate Selection
items.text:
Identify the coordinates in your imaging software, for example from an fMRI hotspot or an anatomical marker. By default they are 1-based T1 voxel indices. Set placement.manual.coordinate_space to enter millimetres instead:

placement:
  mode: 'manual'
  manual:
    coordinate_space: 'ras'   # 'voxel' (default) | 'ras' | 'mni'
transducer:
  trans_pos: [-62.1, 12.4, 48.0]   # bowl apex, subject RAS+ mm
  focus_pos: [-21.5, 10.2, 2.3]
  • ras: subject RAS+ mm of the T1 (read from a viewer or neuronavigation), converted with ras_to_grid() via the T1 affine.
  • mni: MNI mm. The transducer point is converted with the linear (12dof) transform and the focus with the nonlinear warp, as in MNI placement, but the transducer is not snapped to the scalp. The points are used exactly as given. Requires the SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX folder.

Conversion happens once per transducer in the placement stage, so modules.run_transducer_placement must be 1.

After conversion, the positions become voxel indices and coordinate_space is set to 'voxel'. The original inputs are kept in placement.manual.input_trans_pos / input_focus_pos. If neither focal_distance_ep nor focal_distance_bowl is set, the distance fallback from the positions is computed after conversion.

items.title: Heuristic Transducer Placement
items.text:
When only a target is known, the transducer position still has to be chosen, and it decides how much skull lies in front of the transducer. placement.mode: 'heuristic' searches the skull surface for a transducer position whose geometric focus reaches an MNI target, keeps candidates whose exit plane intersects little skull and selects the one closest to the target. Besides the target and the focal depth (transducer.focal_distance_ep or focal_distance_bowl), which sets the search radius, no manual input is needed, which suits automatic end-to-end workflows.

On this page:

  • Candidate Table: the metrics computed for every candidate position.
  • Ear Exclusion Zones: optionally excluding candidates over the ears.
  • Position Selection: the selection criteria and the coordinate output.
  • Placement Figures: the overview and T1 overlay figures.
  • Localite Planning Image: a header-adjusted T1 for Localite.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When you have a target but no planned transducer position, e.g. for many subjects at once.
  • Before you start: A SimNIBS segmentation, an MNI target and the focal depth (transducer.focal_distance_ep).
placement:
  mode: 'heuristic'
  heuristic:
    mni_target_mm: [-29, -6, 7]   # target in MNI mm
    target_name: 'target'         # used in output file names

The search converts the target to subject space with SimNIBS tools, finds candidate positions on the skull by expanding a sphere, scores each candidate (target distance, intersection with skin, mean and variance of the distances to skin and skull), optionally removes positions over the ears, and selects one position by the criteria below. Candidates and the selected position are written to the placement run folder, <path.placement>/sub-XXX/heuristic/<target_name>/; a copy of the selected position also goes to path.localite_export when set. All parameters: overview.

transducer_positioning runs the search; transducer_positioning_start calls it. Candidate positions come from an expanding sphere on the skull. For each candidate it computes the intersection proportion between the transducer and skin, mean and variance of the distances to skin and skull, and the geometric focus and exit plane positions. Each candidate's exit plane lies placement.skin_gap_mm (default 5 mm) off the scalp.

items.title: Candidate Table
items.text:
tpars_sub-XXX_target.csv lists every candidate with the columns below. Use it to pick a candidate yourself, e.g. one with prop_intersect < 0.05 and minimal distance to the target, supported by visual inspection.

Metric Description Interpretation idx index trans_x Transducer x-coordinate (voxels) trans_y Transducer y-coordinate (voxels) trans_z Transducer z-coordinate (voxels) targ_x Target x-coordinate (voxels) targ_y Target y-coordinate (voxels) targ_z Target z-coordinate (voxels) dist_to_target Euclidean distance transducer-to-target (voxels) prop_intersect Fraction of voxels in the transducer’s orthogonal plane that intersect with the skull mask. Low values (≈ 0) indicate minimal skull obstruction; high values (> 0.3) indicate significant bone interference. mean_dist_skin Mean distance from non‑intersecting voxels to the skin boundary. Average proximity of the plane to the skin surface. var_dist_skin Variance of distances from non‑intersecting voxels to the skin boundary. Higher variance: surface curvature or oblique intersection. mean_dist_skull Mean distance from all voxels in the plane to the nearest skull boundary. Average clearance between the plane and skull. var_dist_skull Variance of distances to the skull boundary. Irregularity of skull spacing within the beam footprint.

items.title: Ear Exclusion Zones
items.text: Optional. Transducer locations over the ears are not wanted. Candidates within placement.heuristic.ear_radius (radius of the no-go zone in voxels, default 35) around left_ear_center and right_ear_center (approximate ear coordinates, voxels) are removed when the centres are set.

items.title: Position Selection
items.text:
The accepted intersection with the skull is set by placement.heuristic.criterion_intersection. If no candidate meets it, the criterion is expanded by expand_step (default: 1%) until one does. The keys below sit under placement.heuristic; an empty value ([], the default) switches a criterion off.

Criterion Default Explanation criterion_intersection < 0.05 [Fraction] Reduce skull traversal criterion_skin_mean [] (off) [Quantile] Short EP distance to skin criterion_skull_mean [] (off) [Quantile] Short EP distance to skull criterion_skin_var [] (off) [Quantile] Coherent transducer exit plane toward skin (e.g. little curvature) criterion_skull_var [] (off) [Quantile] Coherent transducer exit plane toward skull surface (irregular bone distorts phase and the wavefront)

Among the candidates that meet the criteria, the one closest to the target is selected. To place another candidate instead, set placement.heuristic.candidate to its idx in the candidate table; the criteria are then not applied (an idx the table does not hold stops the run). The Nexus Heuristic sub-tab sets it: it plots and lists the candidates of the last run, and Place here places the one you click, reusing the candidate table rather than recomputing it. The output table gives its coordinates in voxel (grid space), mm (Localite space) and mm (RAS+ space), based on the image header of the segmentation image.

Warning

Localite mm coordinates assume that the Localite planning image has canonical_affine_transform applied (see Localite planning image). They are the 0-based voxel indices (MATLAB index − 1) rescaled by the voxel sizes in the header, with no affine transformation. Always verify coordinates visually.

Example coordinate output table

trans_y 138
trans_z 246
targ_x  117
targ_y  139
targ_z  161

<...>

LOCALITE_Transducer_mm  Inf
loc_trans_x_mm  144.9

loc_trans_z_mm  221.02

LOCALITE_Target_mm  Inf
loc_targ_x_mm   105.3
loc_targ_y_mm   124.88

RAS_Transducer_mm   Inf
ras_trans_x_mm  43.35
ras_trans_y_mm  -16.17

RAS_Target_mm   Inf

ras_targ_y_mm   -20.71
ras_targ_z_mm   5.19

items.title: Placement Figures
items.text:
PRESTUS generates an overview of the selected transducer placement:

If path.localite_export is set, a copy of the plot and the position table is also written to <path.localite_export>/sub-XXX/ (io.dir_localite_export).

A T1 overlay plot (plot_placement_t1_overlay) is generated after the position is selected. It shows the transducer position and target on orthogonal T1 slices and is written to the subject output folder next to the standard placement figure.

items.title: Localite Planning Image
items.text: Optional. Localite can struggle with images that contain affine matrices in the image header. With placement.heuristic.save_localite_t1: true, PRESTUS writes a header-adjusted T1 planning image for Localite, based on the T1.nii.gz in the SimNIBS m2m directory. path.localite_export must be set; the image is written as <path.localite_export>/sub-XXX/sub-XXX_T1_forneuronav.nii.

items.title: MNI Transducer Placement
items.text:
A transducer site and target given in MNI coordinates let one plan apply to every subject, but each subject's simulation needs both points in its own anatomy. placement.mode: 'mni' converts both points to the subject's T1 grid, snaps the transducer to the scalp and sets its exit plane placement.skin_gap_mm (default 5 mm) off the scalp; no search is performed, so the result is deterministic. The heuristic mode, by contrast, takes only an MNI target and searches the scalp for a transducer position.

On this page:

  • How a Position Is Resolved: coordinate conversion, scalp snap and standoff.
  • Limitations: the transducer types the mode assumes and what to check.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When you know both points in template space, e.g. a group target and a standard scalp position.
  • Before you start: A SimNIBS segmentation of the subject (for the MNI-to-subject transforms).
placement:
  mode: 'mni'
  mni:
    trans_pos_mm: [-52,  -8,  58]   # desired transducer (scalp entry) in MNI mm
    focus_pos_mm: [-29,  -6,   7]   # focus / target in MNI mm
  skin_gap_mm: 5                    # gap between scalp and exit plane [mm]

A SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX folder (under path.seg) is required: the conversion relies on final_tissues.nii.gz and the SimNIBS coordinate transforms.

items.title: How a Position Is Resolved
items.text:
1. Coordinate conversion. Both points are mapped MNI → subject RAS+ → grid voxel, each with the SimNIBS transform suited to where it sits:

    Point Transform Why focus_pos_mm nonlinear (nonl) A deep in-brain target; the nonlinear warp is most accurate here, identical to the heuristic target. trans_pos_mm linear (12dof affine) The transducer is outside the brain (scalp), where the nonlinear deformation field is extrapolated and unreliable. The affine is defined everywhere.

  2. Snap to scalp. The converted transducer voxel is snapped to the nearest scalp voxel, so a slightly off MNI entry coordinate still lands on the head surface.

  3. Standoff. The transducer is offset outward from the scalp along the focal axis (target → scalp) so that its exit plane lies placement.skin_gap_mm (default 5 mm) off the scalp, as in the heuristic. The bowl apex sits a further curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm behind the exit plane.

The resolved trans_pos / focus_pos (T1 grid voxels) are written into every configured transducer, and a QC overlay is saved. Downstream simulation is unchanged.

Functions involved
  • Conversion: transform_coordinates and mni2subject_coords_LDfix, shared with the heuristic.
  • Scalp snap: tp_scalp_boundary (nearest scalp / outer-boundary voxel).
  • Standoff: transducer_scalp_geometry, shared with tp_candidate_mesh; the geometry the heuristic applies to every candidate.
  • QC overlay: plot_placement_t1_overlay.

items.title: Limitations
items.text:
• The standoff geometry assumes annular-style transducer fields (curv_radius_mm, elem_od_mm), as the heuristic does. The mode is intended for annular (CTX-style) transducers.
  • trans_pos_mm is a desired scalp entry. It is snapped to the scalp, so the converted point need not lie exactly on the surface.
  • Check the QC overlay. Converting a scalp coordinate through any registration is approximate.

See also: Transducer Placement overview, Heuristic placement, Coordinate systems.

items.title: Neuronavigation Read-In
items.text:
PRESTUS reads transducer poses recorded with the Localite neuronavigation system and simulates them post hoc, to verify the focus of the realised stimulation. The recorded pose decides where the simulated transducer sits and where its beam points, so the file you read it from and the offset from the tracker to the transducer shape every focus position and intensity the simulation reports. An example demo (without data) is in examples/demo_localite.m.

On this page:

  • Placement from a Recorded Pose: placement.mode: 'localite' and the focal distance it needs.
  • Realised Angle vs Planned Trajectory: which Localite export answers which question, and how the recorded pose becomes the simulated transducer and focus.

At a glance

  • When you need it: After a session, to simulate where the transducer actually was.
  • Before you start: Localite exports of the session and the planning T1 that was loaded into Localite.

Localite data pass through two stages. Ingestion (neuronav_gui, or neuronav_ingest_markers in a script; see GUI and script workflows) reads the raw exports of one subject and session, averages each recorded series and writes one normalised file pair. Placement (placement.mode: 'localite') reads that pair, or in file mode a single XML you point to.

Subpages:

  • Placing from a Recorded Pose: automatic and file mode, several transducers, many sessions; for anyone setting up a Localite run.
  • Localite Files, Offset and Coordinates: folder layout and path keys, the tracker-to-bowl offset and coordinate transforms; for anyone setting up paths, checking the transducer offset or converting positions to voxels or MNI.
  • Localite Ingestion: GUI and Script Workflows: turning raw exports into named, averaged targets in neuronav_gui or with neuronav_ingest_batch; for anyone ingesting sessions.
  • Named Target Coordinates: resolving several named targets per session from several sources in your own script; for studies with more than one target per subject.

items.title: Placement from a Recorded Pose
items.text:
Set placement.mode: 'localite'. The pose's column 4 (position) and column 1 (beam direction) become the transducer and focus positions.

Focal distance required

transducer.focal_distance_ep (or focal_distance_bowl) must be set for Localite placement; config_default.yaml ships it as []. Other placement modes derive it from trans_pos/focus_pos, but here those positions are what the step produces. If neither is set, localite_matrix_to_positions raises PRESTUS:localite:missingConfig naming the missing field. The same check covers placement.mode = 'plantus', which resolves its final position through the same function.

How to select the recorded pose (automatic or file mode, several transducers, many sessions) is described in Placing from a Recorded Pose.

items.title: Realised Angle vs Planned Trajectory
items.text:
The Localite file types answer different questions. The wrong one silently mismatches the reported angle and the reported target.

  • The realised angle at the moment of stimulation is only available from TriggerMarkers (the tracked pose during the pulses, averaged per series) or InstrumentMarker (a static saved pose). Both store a measured rotation.
  • GUMMarkers (EntryTargetPair) carries no measured angle. Its 4×4 matrix is synthesised from the static Target point and a RotationReference vector, which is often unset in the source file (<Rotation angle="0.0" used="false">). With used="false", the angle neuronav_compute_series_statistics produces is a placeholder. Treat it as a real angle only if the source XML has Rotation used="true".
  • Static planned Entry/Target coordinates are never read by placement. This includes the Target field of a GUMMarkers EntryTargetPair and a standalone EntryTarget.xml. For single-target placement they are optional: TriggerMarkers or InstrumentMarker alone is sufficient. They matter only for target resolution, which uses them to identify which planned target a coil's series corresponds to (neuronav_match_entry_targets) and as a cross-check against pre-hoc planned coordinates (neuronav_resolve_target).
  • The reported focus position is axis-projected, not a stored coordinate. localite_matrix_to_positions computes focus_pos = trans_pos + focal_distance_bowl * ref_vec, where trans_pos = ref_pos + d * ref_vec is the bowl rear centre and d is the resolved transducer offset (with the default exit-plane origin this equals ref_pos + focal_distance_ep * ref_vec): it projects forward from the tracked position along the tracked beam axis by the calibrated focal distance. This keeps the reported target self-consistent with the reported angle. A separately clicked static Target point need not lie on the tracked beam axis.
Localite XML file formats

All formats are parsed by neuronav_compute_series_statistics, which handles single markers, repeated trigger trains and multi-position recordings alike.

TriggerMarkers. Multiple triggers can be sent during stimulation to record the transducer location over time. Files are named TMSTrigger/TriggerMarkers_Coil0_<timestamp>. Recorded locations are averaged within each position series (identified by time-gap segmentation). Multiple positions per recording session are supported.

GUMMarkers. One or more static marker positions. Each Element is expected to be of type EntryTargetPair (with a Target/Marker/ColVec3D position and a Rotation/RotationReference/ColVec3D beam direction), from which a synthetic 4×4 matrix is constructed. Some Localite versions write a GUMMarkerList file that mixes EntryTargetPair and InstrumentMarker elements (type="InstrumentMarker" on the Element tag). Each element becomes its own series: InstrumentMarker elements keep their recorded 4×4 pose, EntryTargetPair elements the synthesised matrix. Only the former are instrument poses; placement refuses an EntryTargetPair series (PRESTUS:localite:notAPose).

InstrumentMarker. Static instrument positions stored as full 4×4 matrices in an InstrumentMarkerList file. Each InstrumentMarker entry contains a Marker/Matrix4D block with the same data{row}{col} field layout as TriggerMarkers. The ingested output of neuronav_ingest_markers uses this format.

EntryTarget (not for position or angle). Some Localite versions export an EntryTargetList XML with flat Target/Marker/ColVec3D and Rotation/RotationReference/ColVec3D entries at the top level (not wrapped in GUMMarkerList/Element). neuronav_compute_series_statistics does not read it, and placement never uses it. neuronav_read_entry_target reads it for one purpose: matching an operator-confirmed brain-target label against a target_map in multi-target studies (see Target coordinates from several sources).

items.title: Localite Files, Offset and Coordinates
items.text:
A Localite pose is a 4×4 matrix in the coordinates of the planning image, and its origin is a point on the tracked instrument that need not be the transducer. A wrong origin offset shifts the whole simulation along the beam axis, and converting with the wrong image header displaces positions by tens of millimetres. This page gives the folders PRESTUS reads and writes, how the offset from the tracked origin to the transducer is set, and how positions are converted to voxels and MNI space.

On this page:

  • Localite File Layout: the folder layout PRESTUS reads from and writes to, and the path keys.
  • Transducer Offset (tracker_to_bowl_mm): from the tracked matrix origin to the bowl apex.
  • Coordinate Transforms: planning-image space, native voxels and MNI.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You set up the Localite paths, check where the tracked origin sits on the transducer, or convert Localite positions to voxels or MNI.
  • Before you start: The planning T1 that was loaded into Localite and the transducer geometry (curv_radius_mm, dist_geom_ep_mm).

items.title: Input Layout
items.text:
<path.localite_raw>/
└── sub-XXX/                          subject folder (pipeline: sub-%03d of subject_id)
    └── ses-XX/                       session (a number n in the config means ses-0n)
        └── <placement.localite.loc_folder>/     default 'loc'; '' = no such level
            └── …any depth…           e.g. Session_<ts>/ or <patient>/Sessions/Session_<ts>/
                │                     (optionally restricted by placement.localite.session_folder_pattern)
                ├── TMSTrigger/TriggerMarkers_Coil<N>_<yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS>.xml
                ├── GUMMarkers<yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS>.xml       any depth
                └── EntryTarget<yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS>.xml      any depth; planned targets, used for naming only

This is Localite's own export structure placed below a sub-XXX/ses-XX/ pair; nothing inside the export needs renaming. Selection rules:

Rule Detail Marker type TriggerMarkers first; GUMMarkers only if no usable TriggerMarkers file exists Newest wins Files are ordered by the 17-digit timestamp in the file name (file dates change on copying) Size TriggerMarkers files ≤ 10 kB (no or few pulses) are skipped De-duplication A file byte-identical to one in the previous session (ses-(XX-1)) is skipped; Localite re-exports older sessions Series TriggerMarkers pulses are split into series at time gaps > 3× the median interval; series whose pulse count differs from expected_segment_length (default 80) by more than 20 are dropped ([] keeps all) Coils Without neuronav.coil_map: Coil0 only. With it: one TriggerMarkers_Coil<N> file per entry; each coil contributes one series per configured sequence; untracked blocks (all positions at 0) are skipped

The planning T1 that Localite coordinates refer to (see Coordinate transforms) is looked up as <path.localite_t1>/[sub-XXX/]<path.localite_t1_pattern> (default pattern sub-XXX_*T1*.nii*; path.localite_t1 defaults to path.localite_raw).

items.title: Output Layout
items.text:
<path.localite_post>/sub-XXX/ses-XX/
├── InstrumentMarker_sub-XXX_ses-XX.xml    InstrumentMarkerList, one entry per target:
│                                          Marker description = target name, Matrix4D = mean pose of the series
└── InstrumentMarker_sub-XXX_ses-XX.json   QC sidecar, one object per target (key = target name)
JSON field Meaning series_index Index of the detected series (after the pulse-count filter; as used by placement.localite.position) transducer_id Coil index markertype TriggerMarkers or GUMMarkers source_file Raw file the series came from N_pulses Pulses averaged position_dev_mm.mean/std Distance of the pulses from the series mean position [mm] rotation_dev_rad.mean/std Angle of the pulses from the mean orientation [rad]

With io.overwrite_files: 'never', an existing pair is kept.

items.title: Path Keys
items.text: Key Meaning path.localite_raw Raw Localite exports (read-only) path.localite_post Ingested outputs (written by ingestion, read by placement) path.localite_t1 Planning T1s; empty = path.localite_raw path.localite_t1_pattern File-name template of the planning T1 (%s = sub-XXX) path.localite_export Outputs meant for import into Localite (heuristic placement: position table, plot, Localite-ready T1), per subject in sub-XXX/ path.localite Deprecated. Read as path.localite_raw and as path.localite_export when those are empty (with a warning for the former)

items.title: Transducer Offset (tracker_to_bowl_mm)
items.text:
PRESTUS models the transducer position as the bowl rear centre, the bowl apex (trans_pos; bowl_pos in k-Wave's makeBowl); the acoustic focus lies focal_distance_bowl beyond it along the beam direction. What the Localite matrix origin (column 4) refers to depends on how the instrument was registered in Localite. The offset from that origin to the bowl rear centre is taken, in this order, from placement.localite.tracker_to_bowl_mm (explicit), the transducer geometry -(curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm) (assumes the origin is at the exit plane) or placement.localite.reference_distance_mm (fallback). All three share one sign convention along the beam direction (column 1, towards the head): negative puts the bowl rear centre behind the matrix origin, positive in front of it. A wrong assumption shifts the whole simulation along the beam axis by the difference between the assumed and actual origin.

placement:
  localite:
    tracker_to_bowl_mm: -15   # example: mm from the Localite matrix origin to the bowl rear centre
                              # negative = bowl rear is on the housing side (away from head)

The shipped fallback reference_distance_mm: 15 is positive: it places the bowl rear centre 15 mm in front of the matrix origin, which fits only an origin behind the bowl rear. PRESTUS does not document which physical origin this value assumes. The geometry-derived offset is used whenever curv_radius_mm and dist_geom_ep_mm are set (a flat element gives 0); with empty geometry PRESTUS falls back to reference_distance_mm. Set tracker_to_bowl_mm when the origin is not at the exit plane.

Determining the offset

Column 4 of the Localite 4×4 matrix is the position in RAS mm; column 1 is the beam direction (from the transducer face toward the target). These are the only two columns PRESTUS uses.

Possible matrix origin Value of tracker_to_bowl_mm Exit plane centre -(curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm) (negative; bowl rear is behind exit plane) Bowl rear centre 0 IR tracker cluster centroid Measured distance from cluster to bowl rear centre (positive when the cluster sits behind the bowl rear) Housing reference point Measured distance from reference to bowl rear centre

Option 1: Localite instrument definition file (recommended). The instrument definition is an XML file, stored in the Localite installation under Instruments/ or provided by the manufacturer. Its <ReferencePoint> or <Origin> tag describes which physical point the matrix origin corresponds to and its distance from transducer landmarks in mm.

Option 2: Empirical measurement (ruler / phantom). Place the transducer on a flat phantom surface and record a Localite position. Measure the distance from the phantom surface (= exit plane) to the IR tracker attachment on the housing. The bowl rear centre is about curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm mm behind the exit plane. Set tracker_to_bowl_mm = (bowl rear centre position) − (matrix origin position), in mm along the beam axis. Alternatively, acquire an MR image of a gel phantom with the transducer in place and compare the PRESTUS-predicted bowl voxel position against the visible gel/transducer interface.

Option 3: Contact Localite support (https://www.localite.de) with the instrument type and firmware version used during the recording.

tracker_to_bowl_mm takes priority over the geometry-derived distance and over reference_distance_mm. The geometry-derived value is correct only when the matrix origin is at the exit plane.

items.title: Coordinate Transforms
items.text:
See the coordinate system documentation.

Recorded Localite coordinates are relative to the planning image (e.g. T1_forneuronav) loaded in the neuronavigation software. That image has a zero-origin, diagonal affine (world = voxel × voxel_size_mm), not a scanner-isocentre world-space affine. Localite trigger matrices are therefore in planning-image space, not scanner world-space RAS.

The InstrumentMarker XML written by neuronav_ingest_markers keeps these coordinates as they are and labels the space "RAS": the axes are RAS-oriented, but the origin remains at the image corner. To convert to voxels, use ras_to_grid() with the planning T1 header, not the SimNIBS m2m T1 header. The m2m T1 has a full world-space affine; applying its inverse to planning-image coordinates displaces positions by tens of millimetres.

When SimNIBS is run on the planning T1, the resulting m2m_{sub}/T1.nii.gz shares the same voxel grid (SimNIBS keeps voxel dimensions and layout and updates only the affine). Voxel indices from ras_to_grid(localite_mm, planning_t1_header) are therefore valid for PRESTUS simulations that load the m2m T1; no reprojection is needed. See Coordinate Reference Systems.

SimNIBS' nonlinear transform matrices to MNI are relative to the final_tissues.nii.gz segmentation image, so PRESTUS applies a transform from the planning to the segmentation image before porting coordinates to MNI space. The chain is:

  1. Trigger to voxel (neuronav_convert_trigger_to_voxels): subject voxel indices
  2. Voxel to mm (neuronav_grid_to_mm_batch): subject mm
  3. Native mm to MNI mm (neuronav_apply_deformation): MNI mm

Optional, to average positions across subjects:

  1. Aggregate means in MNI mm across subjects (neuronav_get_group_mean_mni)
  2. Group mean MNI mm to subject mm (neuronav_apply_inverse_deformation)
  3. Subject mm to subject voxel (neuronav_mm_to_voxel)
Coordinate spaces of the neuronav functions Function Input Operation Output neuronav_convert_trigger_to_voxels Localite/trigger data (planning-image space mm, zero-origin RAS) Planning T1 header Subject (native) voxel indices neuronav_grid_to_mm_batch Subject voxel indices (i, j, k) Subject T1 NIfTI affine Subject native mm (scanner/world space) neuronav_apply_deformation (forward warp) Native mm locations Queries the subject's Conform2MNI_nonl.nii.gz MNI mm (for reporting, plotting, averaging) neuronav_get_group_mean_mni CSVs with columns like Mtrans_pos_MNI_x/y/z Mean across subjects/sessions MNI mm group-mean locations (mm, not voxels) neuronav_apply_inverse_deformation (inverse warp) MNI mm group-mean locations Subject's MNI2Conform_nonl.nii.gz nonlinear field Native mm location in that subject's world/scanner space neuronav_mm_to_voxel (helper) Native mm (x, y, z) Subject T1 affine Subject voxel indices neuronav_export_session_csv Native voxel indices for target and transducer, native mm, MNI mm (from the deformation step) and MNI voxel indices (may be inaccurate with limited FOVs)

items.title: Placing from a Recorded Pose
items.text:
Localite placement reads one recorded pose per transducer, either from the ingested markers of a session or from a single XML file you name. The series or marker it reads sets the position and beam axis of the simulated transducer, so a wrong target or position simulates another pose than the one used for stimulation.

On this page:

  • Automatic Mode: Ingested Markers: reading the ingested pair of a subject and session.
