The peak of |F| gives the shift (predict_focal_shift). The approximation degrades with the size of the shift and the strength of the aberration: large predicted shifts mean "this pose focuses badly", not an exact focus position.

items.title: Applying the Phases
items.text: With apply_phases: true, the time-reversal phases replace the element phases before the acoustic simulation, and the source is rebuilt. The free-water baseline has already run with the geometric phases, so ISPPA targeting (target_isppa_wcm2) keeps the element drive amplitudes of the geometric drive: the refocused run shows what the same transducer output delivers when refocused. Whether your hardware can apply arbitrary phases (and with which precision) is not checked.

items.title: Pose Search
items.text:
For transducers that cannot refocus, the pose is the main lever: where the transducer sits on the scalp and where it points. With placement_search.enabled: true (curved annular transducers, 3D grid), the same reverse run also scores poses around the planned one. Each pose costs an interpolation of the recorded field, not a simulation.

The result is <prefix>_timereversal_poses_T<i>.csv, sorted by p_corrected_rel (target pressure relative to the planned pose with geometric aim), with the apex, corrected aim point and target in grid voxels, T1 voxels and RAS mm. A pose is set up as a manual placement with trans_pos = apex and focus_pos = aim point (placement.manual.coordinate_space: ras), and transducer.focal_distance_ep = the apex-to-aim distance minus the bowl depth (curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm). The acoustic run keeps the planned pose. To verify the best poses with forward simulations and run the chosen one, use the pose workflow, or set up a pose by hand with time_reversal_pose_parameters(parameters, pose_row). In the Nexus, Results ▸ Poses ▸ Use this pose… creates a follow-up config at the selected pose (Follow-up runs).

time_reversal.only: true stops the run after this stage (no water baseline, acoustic or thermal simulation), for a report or pose table on its own.

Candidate poses and scoring

Candidates (reciprocity_pose_candidates): beam directions tilted from the planned one up to max_angle_deg, in steps of angle_step_deg, all aimed at the target. For each direction the exit plane sits placement.skin_gap_mm off the scalp (heuristic, MNI, PlanTUS and TUS_entry placements) or at the planned pose's gap (manual and Localite), so the required focal depth changes with the direction. Where the scalp curves, the bowl is moved outward until its surface overlaps the scalp no more than the planned bowl does (push_mm in the pose table), so all poses are seated alike. A single element cannot steer: its apex is placed at the curvature radius from the target instead, and its aim correction is lateral only. With jitter_mm (one or more distances, e.g. 0.5 or [0.5 1 2 5]), the planned pose with its apex moved by each distance is scored too (rows of kind jitter), the local search often run with forward simulations. jitter_mode: grid moves the apex ± along each grid axis, as when editing voxel coordinates; jitter_mode: scalp slides the transducer over the scalp perpendicular to the beam in 8 directions and seats it against the scalp, which suits shifts beyond about 1 mm. Poses whose surface overlaps the head by more than the planned surface does plus 2 % of its points are dropped (inside_fraction); the planned pose is always kept. The reverse run records the field over the region these poses cover.

Scoring (reciprocity_score_poses): for each pose, the surface is sampled (annular_aperture_points) and the target pressure is a sum over the reverse field there. Per pose:

  • target pressure and coherence with geometric aim and steering;
  • predicted focal shift;
  • aberration-corrected aim: aim and steer at target − predicted shift (tilting the bowl about its apex), repeated aim_iterations times, so that the predicted focus lands on the target; the target pressure after this correction ranks the poses;
  • the gain ring refocusing would add.

Grid. The simulation grid ends close to the planned transducer, so tilted poses can lie outside it. The reverse run of a pose search therefore uses its own grid: the full grid (also with a limited acoustic FOV, whose crop the forward run keeps), padded with water on the sides the candidate poses need (the log reports the padding). The padding makes the reverse run larger, and so longer, than the forward run.

items.title: Pose Workflow
items.text:
time_reversal.pose_workflow.enabled: true turns a run into the whole placement workflow, in one call of prestus_pipeline_start (pose_workflow_pipeline). It needs one curved annular transducer (ring array or single element) and a head model (simulation.medium: layered). The placement_search settings apply; placement_search.enabled is set by the workflow.

  1. Search (<affix>_posesearch): the reverse run on the full grid scores the candidate poses; no forward simulation.
  2. Verify (<affix>_pose<id>_<geo|aim>): forward runs, acoustics only, of the planned pose (the reference, aimed at the target) and the n_top best poses by predicted target pressure after aim correction, plus the pose ids in poses. aim sets the aim of each run: corrected (at the aberration-corrected aim point; the planned pose is then run with it too), geometric (at the target) or both. verify_fov: partial (default) runs them on an acoustic FOV around each beam. The poses run are listed in <prefix><affix>_poseverify_selection.csv.
  3. Results and final run: per verification run, the mean intensity in a sphere of target_radius_mm around the target and the distance of the −3 dB focal centroid and peak from the target (axial and lateral), next to the predicted values, in <prefix><affix>_poseverify_results.csv. The runs are ranked by rank_by (target_intensity or focus_error), among those within max_focus_error_mm of the target if set; the log reports the rank agreement between predicted and simulated intensity. With final_run: true, the best pose then runs on the full grid with the configured modules (thermal, report): <affix>_posebest.

On MATLAB the stages run one after the other. On SLURM or qsub, each stage is submitted: a small CPU job after the search job submits the verification runs, and another after those (whether they succeeded or not) collects the results and submits the final run. This needs a cluster that lets jobs submit jobs. A stage whose outputs exist is skipped unless io.overwrite_files: always, so calling the workflow again after a failure continues where it stopped.

The verification and final runs place the transducer as a manual placement in RAS mm (apex = trans_pos, aim point = focus_pos), with the focal depth of the pose:

  • a drive from the calibration library (transducer.serial) is resolved again for the pose's focal depth (calibrated phases and amplitudes);
  • inline ring phases are replaced by geometric steering to the aim point in water, the drive the pose scores assume;
  • a single element has no phases; its poses already place the geometric focus on the target or the corrected aim point.

The runs keep the config's intensity setting. With target_isppa_wcm2, each run is scaled to the same free-water ISPPA, so the simulated intensities compare poses at the same device setting; the predictions compare them at the same element drive. The two differ where the poses' focal depths differ much (the free-water focal intensity changes with steering depth).

Cost: one reverse run (as long as a full-grid acoustic run, more memory: search_memorylimit), n_top + 1 (or twice that with aim: both) partial-FOV forward runs, and one full run.

items.title: Run Time and Memory
items.text:
One k-Wave run per distinct target, about as long as the acoustic simulation (longer by the padding of a pose search), recording the pressure time series (grid.steady_state_num_periods periods) at the sensor points: the transducer surface (refocusing), plus the candidate region (pose search). Scoring takes seconds per pose.

Memory stays below that of the acoustic simulation: the forward source is released during the stage and rebuilt afterwards, the padded grid reuses the forward source's element weights (no second source is built), and the recording is reduced to one complex amplitude per point in blocks, without a double-precision copy (0.5 mm head runs of the forward simulation peak at 25–31 GB).

items.title: Assumptions and Limits
items.text:
• Linear, fluid acoustics. With acoustic_backend: kwave_elastic the reverse run uses the fluid medium (warning). jwave forward runs use the same medium, so the k-Wave reverse run applies.
  • The transducer surface lies in one medium (coupling water); k-Wave scales a pressure source by the local sound speed.
  • Cartesian grids only (no axisymmetric runs).
  • Not with acoustic_backend: babelbrain, which has its own refocusing (babelbrain.do_refocusing, phased-array presets only).
  • The pose search ignores calibrated phase offsets of the library entry (it steers geometrically in water) and treats each pose as a rigid bowl. The verification runs use the library drive, so they include the offsets.
  • The pose scores interpolate the recorded field (cubic) at the transducer surface; at ~7 points per wavelength the interpolation error is about 1 % of the target pressure, the size of the differences between ±0.5 mm poses.
References: related work and benchmarks
  • Pinton (2026), Whole-skull acoustic transparency from a single time-reversal solve for reciprocity-based transducer placement and aperture optimization in transcranial focused ultrasound, arXiv:2609.27852: the same principle (one time-reversal solve, then placement, aperture and orientation searched on the recorded map), with Fullwave 2 on a CT skull.
  • BabelBrain refocusing: phase correction for phased arrays from a back-propagated field (babelbrain.do_refocusing).
  • SCOUT (2024, PMC11592240): position of a single-element transducer optimised with repeated forward k-Wave simulations.
  • Park et al. (2019), Comput Methods Programs Biomed 179: placement by the lowest average reflection coefficient along straight beam lines (no wave simulation).
  • PlanTUS: geometric placement criteria (skull angle, thickness, distance).

items.title: Transducer Definition
items.text:
The transducer definition sets the source of the simulated pressure field: its frequency, element geometry, drive amplitude and phases, and its position relative to the target. The simulated focus position, focal size and intensity follow from these fields. For a device in the transducer library, transducer.serial fills them in; this page explains each field and how to define a device the library does not hold.

On this page:

  • Transducer Fields: the fields of a transducer and a full inline definition.
  • Amplitude and Phases: the drive, set by the focal depth setting and target ISPPA, and the calibrated phases and amplitudes behind it.
  • Transducer and Focus Positions: the transducer and focus positions.
  • Transducer-Target Distance: exit-plane and bowl distances to the focus.
  • Annular Array: ring geometry, including flat elements.
  • Matrix Array: element layouts, steering and its beam-axis constraint.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When your device is not in the transducer library, or to understand the fields the library fills in. With transducer.serial you rarely set these yourself.
  • Before you start: The geometry of your device (from the manufacturer).

items.title: Transducer Fields
items.text:
A transducer comes from the shipped transducer library (transducer.serial: geometry, phases and drive are filled in) or is defined in full in the study config. Every field is listed in the parameter documentation.

A full definition of an annular array, bypassing the library:

transducer:
  serial: IS_PCD15473_01001
  type: annular
  freq_hz: 300000.0
  focal_distance_ep: 60.0
  annular:
    elem_n: 10
    elem_id_mm: [10.0, 22.1, ...]
    elem_od_mm: [21.1, 28.8, ...]
    curv_radius_mm: 100.0
    dist_geom_ep_mm: 92.7

The fields fall into three groups:

Group Fields Where described Type and geometry type (annular or matrix), freq_hz, and the sub-struct of that type (annular or matrix) Annular definition, matrix definition Drive and steering focal_distance_ep and target_isppa_wcm2; calibrated annular.elem_phase_deg and annular.elem_p_amp (advanced); matrix arrays steer automatically Amplitude and phases Position and target trans_pos, focus_pos, focal_distance_ep or focal_distance_bowl Transducer and focus positions, Transducer-target distance

items.title: Amplitude and Phases
items.text:
An annular array is driven by two settings: the focal depth setting (transducer.focal_distance_ep) steers it, and the target free-water ISPPA (transducer.target_isppa_wcm2) sets the drive level. PRESTUS derives the element phases and amplitudes from them:

  • With a library serial, from the device's calibration entry at that depth (the transducer library).
  • Without one (custom geometry), geometric steering phases to that depth (compute_phases, as a library device's geometric baseline) and a nominal uniform drive, which ISPPA targeting then scales. Flat rings (curv_radius_mm: .inf) need element phases.

The element values are advanced settings, for a drive found by calibration against free-water hydrophone measurements:

  • transducer.annular.elem_p_amp: amplitude of the acoustic source per element (Pa). Without a target ISPPA (target_isppa_wcm2: []) it sets the drive level and is required.
  • transducer.annular.elem_phase_deg: phase of the acoustic source per element (degrees). Replaces the steering to the focal depth setting.

Note

Per-element calibration of phases, gains and drive against axial hydrophone profiles (the transducer library) is implemented only for annular arrays. Matrix arrays can instead get a steering correction, which scales the element amplitudes by the measured focal-peak factor at each steering target. For matrix arrays, PRESTUS computes the phase of each element from transducer.trans_pos and transducer.focus_pos. Calibrated phases (one per element) can replace the geometric phases via transducer.matrix.elem_phase_override_deg.

items.title: Transducer and Focus Positions
items.text:
See transducer placement for how a position is chosen.

  • transducer.trans_pos: position of the transducer bowl (XYZ; T1 voxels by default, or RAS/MNI mm via placement.manual.coordinate_space). Used for placement and for the phase calculation of matrix arrays.
  • transducer.focus_pos: position of the stimulation target (XYZ; same coordinate space as trans_pos). Defines the focal point and the automatic steering of matrix arrays.

In water simulations with annular arrays, the placement is determined from the edge of the PML layer.

Positions in mm for phantom and water simulations

For phantom and water simulations the transducer and focus positions can be given in millimetres rather than voxel indices, with two optional config fields:

Field Description trans_pos_mm Transducer position in mm from the centre of grid voxel [1, 1, 1] ([x, y, z]; 0 mm = voxel 1). Converted to voxel indices at runtime as round(mm / grid.resolution_mm) + 1. focus_pos_mm Focus position in mm from the centre of grid voxel [1, 1, 1] ([x, y, z]). Same conversion applies.

These fields are resolution-independent: the same config works unchanged when grid.resolution_mm changes. When both voxel-index and mm fields are present, the mm fields take precedence. Phantom NIfTI outputs reuse the input header, so world-space orientation and voxel dimensions stay consistent across all pipeline stages.

items.title: Transducer-Target Distance
items.text:
The figure shows the PRESTUS definitions for annular transducer distances. Specify one of the two fields. Without either, PRESTUS computes a geometric distance from trans_pos and focus_pos, if both are set.

  • focal_distance_ep: expected distance from the transducer exit plane to the stimulation focus (mm). This often corresponds to the focal depth setting of the driving system or the transducer calibration (BabelBrain's TPO distance). The exit plane lies curv_radius_mm − dist_geom_ep_mm in front of the bowl apex; dist_geom_ep_mm is BabelBrain's NaturalOutPlaneDistance.
  • focal_distance_bowl: expected distance from the transducer bowl to the stimulation focus (mm). Computed internally from focal_distance_ep, dist_geom_ep_mm and curv_radius_mm.

items.title: Annular Array
items.text:
An annular array consists of concentric ring-shaped elements on a spherically curved surface. All elements share one acoustic axis, so focusing is axial only. Lateral steering is not possible; the transducer must be repositioned to change the target.

Use an annular array when your hardware is a single-focus or multi-ring bowl transducer with calibrated per-element amplitudes and phases. This is the simpler and better-validated configuration.

Element geometry is defined by inner and outer diameters (elem_id_mm, elem_od_mm) and bowl curvature (curv_radius_mm). Each element has an independent pressure amplitude (elem_p_amp) and phase (elem_phase_deg), calibrated empirically. PRESTUS includes a calibration pipeline for annular arrays that matches the simulated pressure to free-water measurements.

items.title: Flat Elements
items.text:
curv_radius_mm: .inf makes the elements flat, e.g. a plane piston (the ITRUSST benchmark's 20 mm source). The face lies at trans_pos, normal to the trans_pos → focus_pos direction, and is also the exit plane (bowl depth 0); focus_pos only sets the beam direction. Supported with the kWaveArray source (grid.use_kWaveArray: 1):

Grid Element Rings (elem_id_mm > 0) 2D axisymmetric line across the axis (addLineElement) yes 2D line normal to the beam no 3D disc (addDiscElement) no (single disc)

Not supported: the makeBowl source (use_kWaveArray: 0), BabelBrain, transducer calibration and the placement planners, which assume a bowl.

items.title: Matrix Array
items.text:
A matrix array consists of many small elements on a curved or flat surface. Each element is driven with an independent phase delay, so the focus can be steered electronically in three dimensions without moving the transducer.

Use a matrix array when your hardware supports electronic steering (e.g. a phased array system) or to simulate volumetric targeting without repositioning the transducer. The focal pressure a steered array delivers can be calibrated against hydrophone measurements over the steering range: see Steering correction of matrix arrays.

Phase delays are computed from the geometry of each element, trans_pos and focus_pos; no manual phase input is required. elem_phase_override_deg replaces them with calibrated phases.

Matrix element layout and shape
  • Element positions are defined analytically (Fibonacci, Fermat spiral or rectangular grid) or loaded from a coordinate file.
  • Element shape is rectangular (rect), circular (disc) or curved (bowl). The aperture of disc/bowl elements is equal-area to elem_width_mm × elem_height_mm unless elem_diameter_mm is set.
  • For curved arrays, curv_radius_mm and dist_geom_ep_mm define the bowl geometry used for visualisation and offset calculations.
  • Flat arrays (is_curved: false) have every element facing +z and need rect or disc elements; their coordinate file is in the transducer frame (origin at the array centre).
  • Rectangular elements laid out in more than one orientation take a per-element rotation from the coordinate file (extract_from_file.rot_col).
  • An optional Clover configuration replicates the array into a multi-aperture arrangement of n_leaves leaves on a parent bowl (ROC_parent), az_sep_deg apart (default 360 / n_leaves) and tilted by elevation_deg (default: the smallest non-overlapping tilt).

items.title: Beam Axis Constraint
items.text:
Element orientation and phase delay computation (create_matrix_karray) assume that the transducer's natural beam axis is aligned with the grid +Z direction. This holds for the standard single-transducer placement (transducer at one face of the grid, firing toward the target). In multi-transducer configurations where a matrix transducer fires along a different axis (e.g. a second transducer opposing the first along −Z), element normals and phase delays are computed incorrectly. Annular transducers are not affected. A matrix bilateral setup would need the beam direction derived from (focus_pos − trans_pos) rather than hardcoded to [0, 0, 1] in create_matrix_karray.

KWaveArray vs. simple elements

source_create builds the acoustic source for k-Wave simulations in one of two ways:

  1. Realistic kWaveArray elements (use_kWaveArray = 1, recommended). Uses the k-Wave kWaveArray class to define elements via physical parameters (position, radius, apodisation) rather than discrete grid voxels. Elements render smoothly at any grid resolution. Independent per-element delays and weights enable dynamic focusing. Element overlap is handled through weighted contributions. Supports annular rings, axisymmetric 2D simulations, matrix arrays and GPU acceleration.
  2. Simple custom elements (use_kWaveArray = 0). Creates bowl-shaped (3D) or arc-shaped (2D) pressure source regions per element with the k-Wave makeBowl function. Each element receives an identical continuous wave (CW) signal. Suited to uniform single-element setups. Grid discretisation can introduce staircasing artefacts in the source mask.

items.title: Transducer Library
items.text:
A simulation reproduces a real device only if it uses that device's ring geometry, phases and drive. PRESTUS ships a static library that holds these settings for each supported transducer and driving-system combination, fitted to free-water hydrophone axial profiles where profiles exist, so that a study names the device and a focal depth instead of entering element settings. You can refine an entry against your own hydrophone measurements (Calibration).

On this page:

  • Using a Library Entry: selecting an entry, the lookup order, how phases and drive are computed, and the entry schema.
  • Shipped Entries and Fit Quality: the shipped entries and how well each fits its hydrophone profiles.
  • Dephased Conditions: named defocused settings, which are experimental and not validated.
  • Library Limitations: where the library is less accurate and how to mitigate it.

At a glance

  • When you need it: Whenever you simulate a device from the library: set serial, combo.ds_serial, focal_distance_ep and target_isppa_wcm2.
  • Before you start: Nothing. To fit an entry to your own hydrophone profiles, see Calibration; to add a device, see Adding & Maintaining Entries.
Folder Content Purpose config/equipment/ One YAML per physical device Ring geometry, frequency, steerable range config/calibration/ One YAML per transducer–driving-system combo Per-depth refinements (phases, gains, drive) on geometric steering your folder (optional) Same schema Your own refinements; set transducer.library_path

items.title: Using a Library Entry
items.text:
Name the transducer and driving system, the focal depth and the target intensity:

transducer:
  serial: IS_PCD15473_01001
  combo:
    ds_serial: IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch
  target_isppa_wcm2: 32.0
  focal_distance_ep: 60.0
  # resolves config/calibration/model-IS_PCD15473/tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_ds-IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch_calib.yaml

PRESTUS resolves geometry and calibrated parameters at load time: the ring geometry from config/equipment/, and the phases, per-ring gains and drive at focal_distance_ep from the calibration entry. Fields already set in the study config override library values. Shipped entries lists the entries and how well each one fits its hydrophone profiles.

To use an entry you refined yourself (Calibration), add library_path:

transducer:
  serial: CTX_250_001
  combo:
    ds_serial: SC_105_010
  library_path: /project/my_study/transducer_library   # written by refine_transducer_library
  target_isppa_wcm2: 30.0
  focal_distance_ep: 35.0

The run records what was used: transducer.tx_calibration.phase_model (geometric, static, refined or blend), amplitude_source (refinement, blend or global) and library_meta (the library model version). Record the version with your results; results are not comparable across versions.

To bypass the library, give the full geometry, phases and drive inline: see Transducer definition.

Library keys and layout

Each entry has a key: <TRAN>_<DS> for a transducer with a driving system, <TRAN> for an entry without one (the geometric baselines of the device models). A library folder holds entries in either of two layouts, and PRESTUS reads both:

Layout File Used by Nested model-<MODEL>/tran-<TRAN>_ds-<DS>_calib.yaml, model-<MODEL>/tran-<TRAN>_calib.yaml the shipped library (config/calibration/) Flat <TRAN>_<DS>.yaml, <TRAN>.yaml your own libraries (transducer.library_path) and libraries from earlier versions

library_entry_file(library_path, key) returns the file of an entry. PRESTUS resolves in order:

  1. transducer.library_path (your folder), if set and it contains an entry for this transducer
  2. the shipped entry <TRAN>_<DS>
  3. the shipped entry <TRAN>, with a warning
  4. If none exists, an error with instructions

Without combo.ds_serial, PRESTUS looks only for the entry <TRAN>.

items.title: Your Own Transducers and Calibrations
items.text:
Keep your own devices, calibrations and hydrophone profiles in a library folder of your own, outside the PRESTUS folder, so that updating PRESTUS never touches them. Do not add them to config/equipment or config/calibration. Name the folder in one of three places; PRESTUS checks them in this order, then its shipped library:

Setting Scope transducer.library_path This study (per transducer) path.transducer_library Every study of a project: set it in the project copy of config_default.yaml (project defaults). A folder or a list PRESTUS_TRANSDUCER_LIBRARY This machine or user: an environment variable, folders separated by : (; on Windows). calibration_gui and the Nexus read it too

The first library that has an entry wins: an equipment entry replaces entries with the same serial from later libraries and from the shipped library (with a message), and a calibration entry for the driving system is taken from the first library that has one. The folder can hold:

File Content tran-<SERIAL>_transducer.yaml An equipment entry: a new unit, or a replacement for a shipped entry with the same serial ds-<DS>_driver.yaml A driving system, optionally with its drive limit <TRAN>_<DS>.yaml (or tran-<TRAN>_ds-<DS>_calib.yaml) A calibration entry for that transducer and driving system profiles/ Hydrophone profiles; a relative char_data_path is found here first, then in local/profiles/

A unit of a model in the library needs only its identity and combos; it takes geometry and steering range from the model entry:

# my_library/tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_OPM_transducer.yaml
type: transducer
serial: IS_PCD15473_01001_OPM
model: IS_PCD15473
name: Imasonic 10 ch. IS_PCD15473_01001 (OPM setup)
combos:
  IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch:
    char_data_path: tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_ds-IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch_acq-OPM_axial.csv   # in my_library/profiles/

# study config
transducer:
  serial: IS_PCD15473_01001_OPM
  combo: {ds_serial: IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch}
  library_path: /path/to/my_library

Create the calibration entry from your hydrophone profiles with calibration_gui, refine_transducer_library or calibration_transducer. calibration_gui saves entries and new transducers into its output folder, by default the first folder in PRESTUS_TRANSDUCER_LIBRARY; it does not write into config/equipment (option AllowShipped for maintainers), and an edited shipped transducer is saved as a replacement in your library. If your driving system gives you phases per depth instead, write a short entry by hand:

# my_library/IS_PCD15473_01001_OPM_IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch.yaml
meta: {tran_serial: IS_PCD15473_01001_OPM, driving_system: IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch, calibration_type: user}
global_model:
  depths_ep_mm: [30, 50, 70]
  elem_phase_deg:                 # absolute phase of each ring at each depth [deg]
  - [0, 12, 25, 37, 50, 62, 75, 87, 100, 112]
  - [...]
  - [...]
  amplitude_by_depth: {depths_ep_mm: [30, 50, 70], elem_p_amp: [88000, 103000, 132000], isppa_wcm2: 30}

Between the given depths, PRESTUS interpolates the phases, and outside them it extrapolates and warns. Entries fitted by PRESTUS record the geometry they were fitted for (meta.geometry_fingerprint). When the equipment entry in use has another geometry, for example because your folder replaces a shipped entry, the entry still loads and PRESTUS warns (load_transducer_from_library:geometryMismatch). The Nexus reads the equipment entries in transducer.library_path as well and labels them "(own library)".

items.title: How Phases Are Computed
items.text:
At a requested depth, the entry gives geometric steering plus a fitted per-ring correction, and the drive that reaches the reference ISPPA.

Phase and drive at a requested depth

For any requested focal depth d (mm from the exit plane):

phase(d) = geometric steering phase(d; c_steer) + offset(d)
drive_i  = elem_p_amp(d) · gain_i · exp(i · phase_i(d))
  • Geometric steering (set_real_phases) comes from the ring geometry in config/equipment/, at global_model.steering_sound_speed (default 1500 m/s).
  • Refinement (default): one fit per measured depth (refinement.depths_ep_mm). Each holds a per-ring phase offset (elem_phase_correction_deg), per-ring gains (elem_amp_weight) and the drive that gives the reference ISPPA at that depth (elem_p_amp). Between refined depths, offsets are interpolated per element on the unit circle; gains and drive are interpolated linearly. Outside that span, the nearest refinement fades back to the global model over refinement.blend_mm (default 5 mm).
  • Global model: geometric steering with the measured drive per depth (global_model.amplitude_by_depth). Some entries hold one depth-independent offset and gains instead (global_model.elem_phase_correction_deg, elem_amp_weight). These are read but cannot be fitted.

Amplitude. Hydrophone profiles are recorded at a matched focal ISPPA per depth. The fit therefore uses profile shape only, with a free scale per depth, and derives the drive that produced the measured peak. For a refinement this is refinement.elem_p_amp at refinement.isppa_wcm2; for the global model it is global_model.amplitude_by_depth. Both are normalised to the reference ISPPA, interpolated in depth and scaled as √I at load time. Entries without either use the depth-independent amplitude_scaling. The optional free-water k-Wave drive calibration rescales the refinement drive to the simulated ISPPA.

items.title: Library YAML Schema
items.text:
Entry schema 
meta:
  tran_serial: CTX_250_001
  driving_system: SC_105_010
  calibration_type: empirical        # geometric | empirical | user_empirical
  created_at: '2026-06-12'
  prestus_version: <commit>

global_model:                         # legacy static model (read only)
  elem_phase_correction_deg: [22.3, 56.3, 72.0, 349.9]   # one value per ring
  elem_amp_weight: [0.92, 1.03, 1.06, 0.99]              # per-ring gain, mean 1
  steering_sound_speed: 1500          # [m/s] steering law
  amplitude_scaling: {i30: 114442}    # depth-independent fallback
  amplitude_by_depth:                 # drive giving isppa_wcm2 in water per depth
    depths_ep_mm: [14, 16, ...]
    elem_p_amp: [98000, 101000, ...]
    isppa_wcm2: 30
  forward_model: rayleigh             # model the fit used
  free_params: [phase, amp, z_shift]
  fit_depths_ep_mm: [14, 16, ...]
  fit_z_shift_mm: 0.8                 # diagnostic only
  fit_r2: [0.95, 0.93, ...]           # in-sample R² per depth

refinement:                           # per-depth (default for built and user entries)
  depths_ep_mm: [35, 40]
  elem_phase_correction_deg:
    - [25.1, 60.2, 70.3, 351.0]       # offset at 35 mm
    - [23.8, 58.9, 71.5, 350.2]       # offset at 40 mm
  elem_amp_weight:                    # per-ring gains, mean 1 (NaN: global gains)
    - [0.95, 1.02, 1.05, 0.98]
    - [0.97, 1.10, 1.03, 0.90]
  elem_p_amp: [98000, 104000]         # drive giving isppa_wcm2 in water (NaN: global drive)
  isppa_wcm2: 30
  amp_source: [analytical, kwave]     # kwave: calibrated by the free-water k-Wave drive calibration
  fit_z_shift_mm: [-1.5, -0.4]        # axial registration, diagnostic only
  profile_type: [measured, interpolated]   # profile each depth was fitted to (interpolate_axial_profiles)
  calibration_profiles_csv: /path/{combo}_calibration_profiles.csv   # written when any depth is derived
  kwave_isppa_wcm2: [.nan, 22.1]      # k-Wave ISPPA at the analytical drive (NaN: not checked)
  kwave_r2: [.nan, 0.93]              # k-Wave vs hydrophone profile shape
  kwave_focal_err_mm: [.nan, 0.4]
  blend_mm: 5
  forward_model: rayleigh

elem_phase_correction_deg must have one entry per ring in the current equipment geometry. Otherwise load_transducer_from_library raises an error and validate_transducer_library reports error. Changing the ring geometry of a transducer invalidates its entries; rebuild them.

Per-depth absolute phase tables (global_model.depths_ep_mm + elem_phase_deg) and parametric calibration.focal_depths.f* entries are converted to refinement offsets on load.

items.title: Shipped Entries and Fit Quality
items.text:
Agreement of the shipped entries (library model v3, library_mode: per_depth, built 2026-09-30) with the hydrophone axial profiles they were fitted to, from meta.quality. R² is on peak-normalised intensity beyond 10 mm from the exit plane, as a median over measured depths.

Columns: geo, geometric steering only; in-sample, the refinement at each measured depth (minimum over depths in brackets); held-out, each interior depth predicted from its two neighbours, as at run time between measured depths; worst Δ, the largest held-out loss against geometric steering at any depth.

Geometric steering alone reproduces the Imasonic profiles well (R² ≈ 0.98–0.99). For the Sonic Concepts CTX-500 / CTX-250 it is less accurate (R² ≈ 0.79–0.91), so refinement matters most there.

items.title: Device Models and Units
items.text:
Each device has a model entry, named after the model (CTX_500), and the library's measured units of it, named model plus unit id (CTX_500_026). A unit's calibration is fitted to that unit's hydrophone profiles, so use the unit's serial when your device is in the library. Otherwise name the model, which gives the model's geometry and a geometric baseline calibration: accuracy is that of the geo column above. A serial of a unit that is not in the library (CTX_500_031) falls back to its model (CTX_500), with a warning; to use the unit's own calibration, add it. A model entry has no driving system; with combo.ds_serial set, PRESTUS falls back to the model's generic entry and says so. Each entry names its model in model:; the naming rules are in config/equipment/README.md.

The model geometry is based on the BabelBrain specification, and for Imasonic on the manufacturer's specification and drawings; where the library also has measured units, the unit geometry is identical.

Model Device Rings ROC mm Exit plane → geometric focus mm Steering range mm Frequency kHz Measured units CTX_500 NeuroFUS CTX-500 4 62.94 52.38 33.6–82.5 500 CTX_500_026 CTX_250 NeuroFUS CTX-250 4 62.94 52.38 25–60 250 CTX_250_001, _026 CTX_250_2ch NeuroFUS CTX-250, 2 ch. 2 62.9 56.9 20–80 250 CTX_250_009, _014 DPX_500 NeuroFUS DPX-500 4 150 144.9 50–120 500 DPXPC_300 NeuroFUS DPX-PC-300 4 150 144.9 50–120 300 IS_PCD15287 Imasonic PCD15287 10 75 65.3 7.05–100.3 300 IS_PCD15287_01001, _01002 IS_PCD15473 Imasonic PCD15473 10 100 92.7 7.12–102.7 300 IS_PCD15473_01001, _01003 H246 Sonic Concepts H-246 (flat) 2 flat n/a 25–95 500 BSonix_35mm … _80mm BrainSonix BSonix 1 43 / 68.5 / 74 / 87.5 32.68 / 55.66 / 64.92 / 80.51 fixed 650

The steering range (min_foc–max_foc, from the exit plane) is the hardware range of the model; a unit without its own range uses its model's. The measured range is the span of depths with hydrophone profiles in the calibration entry (column Depths mm above). Within the steering range but outside the measured range, PRESTUS extrapolates the fitted model and warns (load_transducer_from_library:extrapolated); outside the steering range it warns that the device cannot be set there. For the Imasonic models, the provenance of each value is in the equipment YAML. CTX_500_006 (2-channel CTX-500, 500 kHz) has no model entry. H246 has flat rings and needs the kWaveArray source (Flat Elements).

items.title: Drive Limits
items.text:
A driving system delivers a limited drive per channel, so at deep foci it may not reach the target ISPPA. With a limit, PRESTUS compares the library drive for target_isppa_wcm2 with it and warns (resolve_transducer_from_serial:driveLimit), giving the largest free-water ISPPA reachable at that depth. The limit is transducer.max_elem_p_amp in the study config, else the combo's drive_limit.max_elem_p_amp_pa in the equipment entry. Without either, there is no check. The drive is compared as one value; per-ring gains are not included.

The shipped limits are estimates for the IGT 128-channel driver from the Radboud characterisation (full amplitude for a 1.00 MPa focus at about 83–89 mm): IS_PCD15287_01001 and _01002, and IS_PCD15473_01001. Their source is in the equipment entry. Your amplifier may differ (for example the optional 10 W channels), so set transducer.max_elem_p_amp for your setup.

items.title: Deprecated and Excluded Entries
items.text: A unit that is retired or replaced gets status: deprecated; an entry withheld until it is documented gets status: excluded (both optionally with superseded_by and status_note). Both stay in the library, so earlier studies re-run unchanged, and PRESTUS and the Nexus warn when a study names them. Excluded entries are not listed in the Nexus or calibration_gui and are skipped by build_transducer_library. The OPM variants of IS_PCD15473_01001 and _01003 are excluded until their setup is documented.

items.title: Dephased Conditions
items.text:
Experimental, not validated

No dephased hydrophone measurements have been compared with these predictions yet. Every use prints a library_condition:experimental warning. Do not report dephased-condition results without your own validation.

Dephased (defocused) settings drive the rings with explicit phases (e.g. alternate rings shifted by 180°) instead of steering to a focal depth. They cannot be interpolated in depth, so the library entry stores them as named conditions. Select one with transducer.condition: geom_180 (with serial, combo.ds_serial and target_isppa_wcm2). Without focal_distance_ep, it defaults to the condition's setpoint_ep_mm.

Before treating a condition as validated: compare predicted_r2 and the focal/peak errors with those of the focused depths of the same entry, check peak_z_ep_mm against the measured peak, and confirm the free-water ISPPA in a k-Wave water run. Then set validated: true in your copy of the entry.

Adding conditions, with or without measurements

Without measurements:

equip = load_equipment_config();
tran  = equip.trans.CTX_250_001;
lib   = yaml.loadFile(library_entry_file('config/calibration', 'CTX_250_001_SC_203_035'), 'ConvertToArray', true);
cond  = struct('label', 'geom_180', 'phase_shift_deg', [0 180 0 180], 'setpoint_ep_mm', 52.38);
lib   = library_add_conditions(lib, tran, cond, struct('IsppaWcm2', 30));
yaml.dumpFile('my_library/CTX_250_001_SC_203_035.yaml', lib);   % then transducer.library_path: my_library

With measurements, store them as tran-{TRAN}_ds-{DS}_acq-dephased_axial.csv in the usual CSV layout. The depth row holds each column's nominal setpoint. The sidecar describes the columns in order:

columns:
  - label: geom_180
    phase_shift_deg: [0, 180, 0, 180]
  - label: geom_120
    elem_phase_deg: [0, 120, 240, 0]     # absolute driver phases

library_ingest_conditions(lib_file, csv_path) predicts every column, prints the agreement table and writes the conditions to lib_file (struct('DryRun', true) to only score). Do not pass dephased CSVs to build_transducer_library or refine_transducer_library, which read every column as a focal depth.

Condition schema and how phases and drive are derived 
conditions:
  geom_180:
    status: experimental
    validated: false
    phase_mode: shift                    # shift | absolute
    phase_shift_deg: [0, 180, 0, 180]    # shift mode: added to the setpoint's steering phases
    nominal_phase_deg: [...]             # driver phases before the hardware correction
    setpoint_ep_mm: 52.38                # nominal focal setpoint the condition derives from
    inherit_correction: true
    elem_phase_correction_deg: [...]     # hardware offset of the entry at the setpoint
    elem_phase_deg: [...]                # phases used in simulation
    elem_amp_weight: [...]               # per-ring gains of the setpoint
    elem_p_amp: 98000                    # drive for isppa_wcm2 at the model's free-water peak
    isppa_wcm2: 30
    peak_z_ep_mm: 18.5                   # where that peak is (can be a near-field or split focus)
    predicted_r2: .nan                   # model vs measured profile (NaN = no measurement)
    predicted_focal_err_mm: .nan
    source_csv: ''
  • shift mode: geometric steering phases at the setpoint plus phase_shift_deg.
  • absolute mode: the given driver phases.
  • inherit_correction adds the entry's hardware offset and gains at the setpoint. This assumes the correction fitted to focused profiles transfers to dephased drives; a dephased measurement has to confirm it.
  • The drive is set so that the Rayleigh free-water on-axis peak beyond 10 mm reaches isppa_wcm2.
  • Measured profiles only score the prediction (predicted_r2, focal and peak error); they are never fitted.

items.title: Library Limitations
items.text: Limitation Effect Mitigation Refinements are exact only at measured depths Between depths, interpolated phases fit less well (held-out interpolation in meta.quality) Measure closely spaced depths around the targets Axial shift fitted, not applied A real model/hydrophone offset remains in focal placement Correct the equipment geometry if fit_z_shift_mm is persistent Refinement is only as good as your profiles Offsets inherit hydrophone/tank errors Cover the intended depth range; record conditions Water-tank basis Does not account for tissue acoustic properties Combined with the PRESTUS forward simulation in tissue Profiles recorded at matched ISPPA per depth Depth dependence of focal gain is not calibrated Water-baseline ISPPA rescaling DS-agnostic fallback Ignores DS hardware phase offset Use DS-specific entries Outside the measured range Extrapolated from the fitted model, warning emitted Measure the depths you target Outside [min_foc, max_foc] Beyond the hardware steering range, warning emitted Keep focal_distance_ep within range

items.title: Adding and Maintaining Library Entries
items.text:
A study can name a device with transducer.serial only if PRESTUS has its geometry in config/equipment/ and a calibration entry in config/calibration/. This page covers adding a transducer or driving system, starting from a geometric baseline entry that uses geometric steering alone, and how maintainers rebuild, validate and contribute shipped entries.

On this page:

  • Adding a Transducer or Driving System: equipment entries by hand or from the GUI, and a geometric baseline entry.
  • Rebuilding a Shipped Entry: rebuilding from hydrophone profiles and validating the result.
  • Contributing an Entry: what a pull request for a new entry contains.

At a glance

  • When you need it: Your device has no entry in config/equipment/ or config/calibration/.
  • Before you start: The device geometry (ring diameters, curvature, exit-plane distance, focal range); for a refined entry, hydrophone axial profiles.

How studies use the library is described in Transducer Library; fitting an entry to hydrophone profiles in Calibration.

items.title: Adding a Transducer or Driving System
New Driving System for an Existing Transducer
items.text:
1. Add a combo entry to the transducer's entry in config/equipment/ (model-<MODEL>/tran-<TRAN>_transducer.yaml), and describe a new driving system in config/equipment/ds/ds-<DS>_driver.yaml:

    combos:
  MY_NEW_DS:
    ds:
      serial: MY_NEW_DS
      name: My Driving System
      manufact: MyCompany
    # char_data_path: add when hydrophone data is available

  2. Generate a geometric baseline.

  3. Use it in study configs with combo.ds_serial: MY_NEW_DS.
  4. Refine it when hydrophone data is available.

items.title: New Transducer by Hand
items.text:
1. Create config/equipment/model-<MODEL>/tran-<MY_SERIAL>_transducer.yaml, copying an existing file as a template (a flat config/equipment/<MY_SERIAL>.yaml is read as well). A measured unit of a model already in the library needs only type, serial, model, name and its combos; it takes the geometry and steering range from the model entry. Required fields for a device model of an annular array:

    type: transducer
serial: MY_SERIAL
name: Human-readable name
manufact: Imasonic    # or: Sonic Concepts
min_foc: 30.0         # hardware steering range from the exit plane [mm]; a unit may omit it
max_foc: 90.0         # and use its model's
transducer:
  annular:
    elem_n: 10
    elem_id_mm: [0.0, ...]
    elem_od_mm: [21.0, ...]
    curv_radius_mm: 100.0
    dist_geom_ep_mm: 92.7
  freq_hz: 300000.0

  2. Run check_equipment_config(equip_path) to validate the geometry and its physical plausibility.

  3. Continue with the geometric baseline.

items.title: New Transducer from the GUI
items.text:
Click New… under the transducer list in calibration_gui. The form takes the type (annular or matrix), frequency, curvature radius, exit-plane-to-geometric-focus distance (dist_geom_ep_mm) and focal range, then the type-specific geometry:

  • Annular: ring inner and outer diameters and the number of physical channels, plus optionally one driving system with its profile CSV.
  • Matrix: steering (1D/3D), curved or flat, aperture diameter, element shape and size, and a define_here grid (rect rows × columns with spacing, fibonacci count and kerf, or fermat count). Coordinate-file layouts (extract_from_file) are not offered in the form.

Copy from fills the form from an existing transducer. A side view and a face view update as you type: rings coloured by channel, or matrix element footprints, with the exit plane, geometric focus and steering range. The message box reports the ring/channel count or the element count and median pitch, and flags overlapping rings or elements. On save the GUI writes the entry to its equipment folder (into its existing file, else model-<MODEL>/tran-<SERIAL>_transducer.yaml when the model folder exists, else <SERIAL>.yaml) (EquipPath, default config/equipment/) and selects the new transducer. For an annular transducer, the geometric prediction is shown right away. Serial-based study configs (transducer.serial) always read config/equipment/, so save there if the pipeline should resolve the new serial.

What the form checks and stores

On save the GUI:

  • rejects a serial that is not a valid identifier, unequal inner/outer diameter counts, a ring whose outer diameter does not exceed its inner diameter, a ring count that is not a multiple of the physical channel count (fit_transducer_model groups consecutive rings into channels), a curved matrix whose curvature radius is not larger than half the aperture, and a matrix grid with no element inside the aperture;
  • runs check_equipment_config on the entry and asks for confirmation if it reports issues.

The profile CSV path is stored relative to ProfileRoot when it lies under it, otherwise as an absolute path. For matrix entries, the top-level n_elem is the element count inside the aperture.

View geometry draws the selected transducer the same way. Matrix transducers are geometry only in the calibration GUI: the axial forward model behind prediction and fitting (axial_transfer_matrix, steering_path_lengths) is defined for annular arrays.

items.title: Geometric Baseline Entry
items.text:
For a transducer or driving system that is not in the shipped library and has no hydrophone data:

COMBOS_TO_RUN = {'MY_SERIAL_MY_DS_SERIAL'};              % a combo without char_data_path
LIBRARY_PATH  = '/project/my_study/transducer_library';  % omit to write config/calibration/
run(fullfile(prestus_root, 'functions', 'calibration', 'build_transducer_library.m'))

This writes an entry with an empty offset (pure geometric steering). Accuracy equals the geometric baseline in the shipped combos table. Add the device to config/equipment/ first (above).

items.title: Rebuilding a Shipped Entry
items.text:
Maintainers only. Set char_data_path in the transducer's equipment entry and run build_transducer_library. CHAR_DATA_ROOT defaults to local/profiles/ (see Input file formats), and LIBRARY_PATH to config/calibration/. A missing profile CSV is an error; it does not fall back silently to a geometry-only entry. Then check the entry:

validate_transducer_library(library_path, equip_path)   % must report no 'error'
What the build fits and records

Every measured depth becomes a refinement (PER_DEPTH_FIT_OPTIONS, as in Calibration), on a geometric global model with the measured drive per depth. meta.quality records:

  • the in-sample R² (median, min) and the geometric R²;
  • the held-out interpolation R²: each interior depth predicted from its two neighbours, without axial shift, as at run time.

Held-out interpolation shows how much of the refinement carries over between measured depths. On CTX-250-001 + TPO-203-035 it is 0.938, against 0.970 in-sample and 0.849 for geometric steering. Space the measured depths closely where you will stimulate.

items.title: Contributing an Entry
items.text:
Open a PR with:

  • the rebuilt YAML (with global_model.forward_model set)
  • validate_transducer_library passing with no errors
  • the meta.quality summary (in-sample, held-out interpolation and geometric R²)
  • characterisation conditions in the combo YAML notes field (water temperature, hydrophone model, tank geometry)

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
This page lists known problems by the message or symptom you see, each with its cause and fix.

On this page:

  • Installation and Setup: missing k-Wave, platform detection, config warnings, macOS file access and Nexus installation.
  • Segmentation (SimNIBS charm): charm errors and segmentations that are started twice or not redone.
  • Placement: PlanTUS, TUS_entry and positions that land in the wrong place.
  • Simulation: ISPPA targeting errors, cache mismatches, sampling warnings and running out of memory.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When a run stops with one of the messages below, or a result lands in the wrong place.
  • Before you start: The error identifier or warning text from the MATLAB console or the log/ folder.

Most entries link to the page that explains the behaviour. If you solve an issue that is not listed here, add it. If you find an error in the pipeline or have a suggestion, open an issue on GitHub.

items.title: Installation and Setup
items.text: Symptom Cause and fix makeBowl (or another k-Wave function) is not found k-Wave is not on the MATLAB path. Clone with submodules and add external/ (Installation). No HPC system detected (sbatch/qsub) platform: auto (the default) only detects SLURM or qsub. On a workstation set platform: matlab (HPC). Warning prestus:unknownConfigKey A key in your YAML is not a PRESTUS setting, often a typo; the warning suggests the closest known key (Configuring a study). Warning prestus:staleProjectDefault Your project copy of config_default.yaml predates settings added since; they take their toolbox default. Refresh it with prestus_config_upgrade(folder) (Configuring a study). macOS: files cannot be read when MATLAB is started from the Finder or Dock Add MATLAB.app under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access and restart MATLAB. MATLAB started from a terminal is not affected. Nexus: Library not loaded: …QtPrintSupport conda's pyqt mixed with pip's PyQt6-WebEngine; install Qt from pip only (Nexus).

items.title: Segmentation (SimNIBS charm)
items.text: Symptom Cause and fix ValueError: The qform and sform of do not match. Please run charm with the --forceqform option Set segmentation.use_qform: 1. undefined symbol errors from charm Empty, hpc.ld_library_path already gives SimNIBS tools the install's own libraries. Otherwise set it to the shared libraries SimNIBS needs (e.g. /opt/gcc/7.2.0/lib64; Installation). Two runs of the same subject (e.g. left and right transducer) both start a segmentation Neither finds a finished m2m_sub-XXX folder. Segment first (modules.segmentation_only: 1), then start the simulations. A segmentation is not redone after changing the input images Existing segmentations are reused unless io.overwrite_simnibs: 1 (independent of io.overwrite_files).

items.title: Placement
items.text: Symptom Cause and fix PlanTUS interactive mode runs headless No display was found (e.g. a cluster job or an SSH session without X forwarding); run it on a desktop or in a VNC session. PlanTUS places the last clicked vertex without a review dialog PyQt5 is missing in the SimNIBS Python; it ships with SimNIBS, so check placement.plantus.env_path. PlanTUS stops because intermediate files are missing wb_command (Connectome Workbench) is not found; install it in the SimNIBS environment or set placement.plantus.connectome_wb_path (Installation). TUS_entry: replacement has 1 row, data has 0 TUS_entry needs a solid head mask; check placement.tus_entry.scalp_mask (TUS_entry). MNI or RAS positions end up in the wrong place Manual ras/mni coordinates are converted in the placement stage, so modules.run_transducer_placement must be 1 (Placement). For MNI and Localite conventions see Coordinate systems.

items.title: Simulation
items.text: Symptom Cause and fix prestus:isppa:noBaseline or prestus:isppa:unsimulatedBaseline transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 needs a free-water baseline that is not available, e.g. modules.run_water_baseline: 0 with an uncalibrated transducer. Use auto, or set the target to [] to report the field at elem_p_amp (ISPPA targeting). Warning prestus:isppa:largeScale The target is more than 4× (or less than 0.25×) the simulated drive; check that this is still in the linear regime. Warning load_transducer_from_library:uncalibratedAmplitude The library drive at this depth was fitted analytically and not checked in k-Wave; see k-Wave drive calibration. prestus:cache:signatureMismatch A reused grid, medium or acoustic cache was built with other settings. Recompute (io.overwrite_files: always or force) or delete the cache files (Cache reuse checks). Changed source or medium settings have no effect on a re-run A grid, medium or acoustic cache was reused although its settings differ: io.cache_signature_check is warn (reuse with a warning) or off, or a chained-pipeline sub-job loaded a cache another stage wrote, which is not checked (Cache reuse checks). Keep io.cache_signature_check: error, use io.overwrite_files: force or delete the relevant cache/ files (Overwrite behaviour). Points-per-wavelength (PPW) warning The grid is too coarse for the frequency; reduce grid.resolution_mm (Spatial and temporal sampling). Out of memory in the thermal simulation Coarsen grid.thermal_resolution_mm, or use a GPU with more memory (Thermal, HPC). Out of memory in the acoustic simulation Use a coarser grid, a limited acoustic FOV, or the C++ binaries (Memory).

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification
items.text:
The acoustic and thermal properties of skull and brain are not precisely known for an individual subject, and published values vary across studies, so the simulated in-situ intensity and heating depend on which values are assumed. Uncertainty mode makes this dependence explicit: it runs the default medium and four variants built from the ITRUSST tissue property bounds and reports the range of each safety metric.

On this page:

  • Basic usage: switching uncertainty mode on.
  • Simulation variants: the five variants and why two pairs of bounds are needed.
  • Medium property ranges: the property values of each variant.
  • Workflow stages: the seven stages and the options that customise them.
  • Customising medium property ranges: study-specific variant files.
  • Output files: what each variant writes and what is cleaned up.
  • Uncertainty report contents: how the report presents the ranges.
  • Combining with multi-ISPPA or async modes: uncertainty as the outer mode.
  • Resuming a partial run: skipping completed stages.
  • HPC usage: job submission, dependencies and queues.
  • Pseudo-CT runs: how the bounds relate to a pseudo-CT skull.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When a safety assessment should state how much in-situ intensity and heating depend on the assumed tissue properties.
  • Before you start: A working study config; simulation.uncertainty: true and, on a cluster, a GPU budget for five runs.

Experimental feature

The uncertainty quantification workflow is under active development. The variant medium properties shipped with PRESTUS are the lower and upper bounds of the ITRUSST tissue property table. They are not formally validated bounds, and they do not capture all sources of simulation uncertainty. Each variant combines the bounds chosen one property at a time; parameter interactions can be non-linear, both amongst tissue properties and with subject-specific head anatomy such as skull thickness and morphology. Analysis choices such as the degree of image smoothing applied to the segmentation also affect intensity and thermal estimates. Treat the variants as scenarios that bracket a plausible range, not as guaranteed worst- or best-case predictions.

items.title: Basic Usage
items.text:
Set simulation.uncertainty = true (in the Nexus: the Uncertainty analysis switch on the Medium tab, Uncertainty sub-tab; the variant values and medium files are under Advanced below the bounds plot) and call the usual entry point:

prestus_path = '/path/to/PRESTUS';
addpath(fullfile(prestus_path, 'functions', 'helper'));
safe_addpath(fullfile(prestus_path, 'functions'));
safe_addpath(fullfile(prestus_path, 'external'));

parameters = load_parameters('config_study.yaml');
parameters.subject_id             = 1;
parameters.simulation.medium      = 'layered';
parameters.simulation.uncertainty = true;    % activates uncertainty mode
parameters.platform               = 'auto';  % 'matlab', 'slurm', or 'qsub'
parameters.path.sim               = '/absolute/path/to/sim_outputs';  % must be set

prestus_pipeline_start(parameters);

On a local MATLAB session (platform = 'matlab') the stages run one after another. On HPC (platform = 'slurm' or 'qsub') all jobs are submitted immediately with scheduler dependencies, and no MATLAB session is held open (HPC usage).

Uncertainty mode can be combined with sequential simulations; see Sequential: Combining with uncertainty mode.

items.title: Simulation Variants
items.text:
The five simulation variants are:

Variant Label Medium properties Runs heating Used for default Default PRESTUS default medium as modules.run_heating_sims Reference simulation temp_high Temp-H per property, the bound that maximises brain heating yes Upper end of thermal metrics temp_low Temp-L per property, the bound that minimises brain heating yes Lower end of thermal metrics trans_high Trans-H per acoustic property, the bound that maximises brain intensity no Upper end of acoustic metrics trans_low Trans-L per acoustic property, the bound that minimises brain intensity no Lower end of acoustic metrics

The bounds come from the ITRUSST one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis, which varied each tissue property between its lower and upper bound with all other properties at reference. Two pairs are needed because brain sound speed, density and attenuation and skull sound speed push heating and intensity in opposite directions: higher brain attenuation, for example, raises heating in the brain but lowers the intensity that reaches deeper targets. A single high/low pair would therefore bound neither metric. The Trans variants vary acoustic properties only and run without heating.

items.title: Medium Property Ranges
items.text:
The tables list the default medium (config/config_default.yaml) and the four variant files in config/uncertainty/. Attenuation and absorption coefficients are in dB/(cm·MHz^y); the variant values are the ITRUSST 500 kHz values converted with y = 1 (alpha_coeff = α_500 kHz / 0.5). "–" marks a property the variant file does not list: the Trans variants run no heating, so their thermal properties are not used.

Brain and skull property tables

Brain

Property Default Temp-H Temp-L Trans-H Trans-L Unit Sound speed 1546 1573 1520 1520 1573 m/s Density 1046 1040 1050 1050 1040 kg/m³ Attenuation coeff. 0.59 0.984 0.308 0.308 0.984 dB/(cm·MHz^y) Attenuation power 1.2 1 1 1 1 – Thermal conductivity 0.51 0.48 0.55 – – W/(m·K) Specific heat 3630 3525 3718 – – J/(kg·K) Perfusion 559 196 809 – – mL/min/kg Absorption fraction 1 1 0.29 – – –

Skull

The variant values apply to skull, skull_trabecular and skull_cortical alike. The Default column shows skull; the default values of the two sub-compartments are in Medium.

Property Default Temp-H Temp-L Trans-H Trans-L Unit Sound speed 2800 2871 2190 2190 2871 m/s Density 1850 1080 1991 1080 1991 kg/m³ Attenuation coeff. 13.3 8.04 23.4 8.04 23.4 dB/(cm·MHz^y) Attenuation power 1 1 1 1 1 – Thermal conductivity 0.32 0.30 0.36 – – W/(m·K) Specific heat 1793 826 2524 – – J/(kg·K) Perfusion 20 0 30 – – mL/min/kg Absorption fraction 0.28 coeff. 8.04 coeff. 2.1 – – –, dB/(cm·MHz^y)

Rationale. Temp-H combines low skull attenuation and density, which let more energy into the brain, with high brain attenuation and full brain absorption, which convert more of it to heat, and with the thermal bounds that raise temperature (low conductivity, specific heat and perfusion). Temp-L takes the opposite bound of each. Trans-H combines low skull impedance and attenuation with low brain attenuation, so more energy reaches the target; Trans-L takes the opposite bound of each. Skull density and attenuation take the same bound in Temp-H and Trans-H; brain sound speed, density and attenuation and skull sound speed take opposite bounds.

Multi-compartment skull models. With separate skull_cortical and skull_trabecular compartments, both get the single ITRUSST skull bound. To assign compartment-specific ranges, use your own variant files (see Customising medium property ranges).

items.title: Workflow Stages
items.text:
The uncertainty mode consists of seven stages, of which stages 2–6 can run in parallel:

Stage 1: Preprocessing & source setup  (serial; must complete before stages 2–6)
    ↓
Stage 2: Default simulation             ┐
Stage 3: Temp-H simulation              │  acoustic + thermal
Stage 4: Temp-L simulation              ├─ parallel jobs
Stage 5: Trans-H simulation             │  acoustic only
Stage 6: Trans-L simulation             ┘
    ↓
Stage 7: Uncertainty report generation  (serial; runs once all five output files are present)

Variants share the stage-1 head and grid caches; each maps its own medium, cached under its own affix. Only the properties defined in a variant file change; all other settings (transducer, grid, paths) are inherited from the base config. With pct.enabled: 1, stages 3–6 use a homogeneous skull layer (see Pseudo-CT runs).

What happens inside

prestus_pipeline_start detects simulation.uncertainty = true on HPC and redirects to uncertainty_pipeline before submitting a single job. On MATLAB, prestus_pipeline handles the redirect after path_log_setup has run. The per-variant parameter structs built internally have simulation.uncertainty cleared, so there is no recursion. uncertainty_pipeline builds one parameter struct per stage from the base parameters and dispatches them:

Stage Modules enabled io.output_affix Medium override 1 source setup only '' none 2 acoustic + thermal (as modules.run_heating_sims) <base> none (default) 3 acoustic + thermal <base>_desc-temphigh config_medium_temp_high.yaml 4 acoustic + thermal <base>_desc-templow config_medium_temp_low.yaml 5 acoustic only <base>_desc-transhigh config_medium_trans_high.yaml 6 acoustic only <base>_desc-translow config_medium_trans_low.yaml 7 uncertainty report '' none

<base> is the base config's io.output_affix (usually empty).

You can also call uncertainty_pipeline directly if you need to bypass prestus_pipeline:

uncertainty_pipeline(parameters, options);

items.title: Customising Pipeline Options
items.text:
The variants' medium files can be set in the config:

simulation:
  uncertainty: true
  uncertainty_temp_high: /path/to/my_medium_temp_high.yaml   # absolute path, or a file name in config/uncertainty/
  uncertainty_temp_low: my_medium_temp_low.yaml
  uncertainty_trans_high: ''                                 # '' = shipped file
  uncertainty_trans_low: ''

Empty (the default) uses the shipped config/uncertainty/config_medium_<variant>.yaml. Each file is merged onto the run's config, so tissues and properties it does not list keep their medium_properties values; the shipped files list brain and the three skull layers only. A file that sets absorption_coeff for a tissue clears the inherited absorption_fraction, and the other way round. The options.*_config arguments below take precedence.

Uncertainty-specific options can be passed as the second argument to prestus_pipeline:

% Output affixes (defaults: base affix, then _desc-temphigh, _desc-templow, ...):
options.affixes.default    = '';
options.affixes.temp_high  = '_desc-temphigh';
options.affixes.temp_low   = '_desc-templow';
options.affixes.trans_high = '_desc-transhigh';
options.affixes.trans_low  = '_desc-translow';

% Override the medium files with study-specific files:
options.temp_high_config  = '/path/to/my_medium_temp_high.yaml';
options.temp_low_config   = '/path/to/my_medium_temp_low.yaml';
options.trans_high_config = '/path/to/my_medium_trans_high.yaml';
options.trans_low_config  = '/path/to/my_medium_trans_low.yaml';

% HPC wall times:
options.stage1_timelimit  = '00:30:00';
options.sim_timelimit     = '04:00:00';
options.report_timelimit  = '00:30:00';

prestus_pipeline(parameters, options);

options.liberal_config, options.conservative_config and options.affixes.liberal / .conservative stop the run with uncertainty_pipeline:legacyVariant; use the options above instead.

items.title: Customising Medium Property Ranges
items.text:
The shipped variant files are in config/uncertainty/. To use study-specific ranges, copy and edit one of them:

# my_medium_temp_high.yaml: only override what you want to change
medium_properties:
  skull:
    alpha_coeff: 6.0
    absorption_coeff: 6.0

Pass it via the config (simulation.uncertainty_temp_high) or via options:

options.temp_high_config = '/path/to/my_medium_temp_high.yaml';
prestus_pipeline(parameters, options);

Only the properties present in the file are changed; all other settings are inherited from the base config. A Trans variant file needs no thermal properties, since the Trans variants run no heating.

items.title: Output Files
items.text:
Each simulation variant writes its outputs into the shared path.sim output folder (or a subject subfolder), identified by io.output_affix. The Trans variants write no thermal outputs (maxT, thermal_max, heating_res).

File pattern Description Kept when save_matrices is 0 or empty sub-NNN_layered<affix>.csv Acoustic and thermal metrics table yes sub-NNN_layered_report<affix>.html Per-variant simulation report yes sub-NNN_layered_intensity_<dim><affix>.png Intensity overlay image per slice dimension (x, y, z) yes sub-NNN_layered_maxT_<dim><affix>.png Max temperature overlay image per slice dimension (x, y, z) yes sub-NNN_layered_thermal_max<affix>.png Temperature vs. time plot yes sub-NNN_layered_parameters<affix>.mat Parameter struct for the variant yes sub-NNN_layered_heating_res<affix>.mat Heating simulation matrices (large) removed debug/sub-NNN_after_rotating_and_scaling.mat Intermediate head model (debug) removed debug/sub-NNN_layered_after_cropping_and_smoothing.mat Intermediate skull grid (debug) removed

Automatic cleanup

When parameters.io.save_matrices is 0 or empty (the default), the pipeline deletes the files marked removed above after the uncertainty report (stage 7) has been written (cleanup_uncertainty_intermediates, on both the MATLAB and HPC platforms). Cleanup only runs after stage 7 completes, so a failed run can be resumed beforehand.

The uncertainty report is written as sub-NNN_layered_desc-uncertainty_report<base>.html. The name ends with the default variant's affix, so runs with different base affixes keep separate reports. With a nested multi-ISPPA sweep or async run there is one report per sweep point, e.g. sub-NNN_layered_desc-uncertainty_report<base>_desc-isppa030.html (see below).

items.title: Uncertainty Report Contents
items.text:
The uncertainty report is a self-contained HTML file. Acoustic metrics (ISPPA, MI, pressure, focal metrics, half-maximum volume) are reported with the Trans range (Trans-L to Trans-H); thermal metrics (temperature rise, maximum temperature, CEM43) with the Temp range (Temp-L to Temp-H). Every table lists the values of all five variants; the Trans variants show N/A for thermal metrics.

  • Safety dashboard: colour-coded cards for all ITRUSST consensus safety metrics (MI, CEM43, temperature rise, absolute temperature). Each card shows the default value with the range of the relevant pair annotated. The bar spans a metric-specific minimum (37 °C for absolute temperatures, 0 elsewhere) to max(max_sim, limit); ticks mark the variant values. The card colour follows the highest value of the default and the pair.
  • Acoustic results: range table with the values of all variants and the Trans range for key acoustic metrics. Row colour follows the highest value of the default and the Trans pair.
  • Thermal results: range table with the values of all variants and the Temp range for thermal metrics (maxT, temperature rise, CEM43 per tissue); row colour follows the highest value of the default and the Temp pair. Side-by-side temperature-vs-time images (thermal_max) of the default and Temp variants. Per-layer and global timeseries plots show temperature and CEM43 over time with the Temp-L to Temp-H band shaded around the default trajectory.
  • Pseudo-CT skull vs. bounds: with pct.enabled: 1, histograms of the default run's mapped skull properties against the band of the bound variants' skull values (see Pseudo-CT runs).
  • Additional maps: side-by-side maximum temperature maps across the default and Temp variants.
  • Raw data tables: full CSV output tables for each variant.

items.title: Combining with Multi-ISPPA or Async Modes
items.text:
Uncertainty composes with the two other chained modes. When the base config is a multi-ISPPA sweep (a vector transducer.target_isppa_wcm2) or an async multi-transducer run (simulation.transducer_coupling: async), each of the five variants runs that pipeline with its own medium, and stage 7 writes one uncertainty report per sweep point. The Trans variants run no thermal jobs. Uncertainty is always the outer mode, on every platform.

Multi-ISPPA sweep Async transducers Stage 1 shared preprocessing, as above not run: each variant's async stage 0 builds its own grid and medium Stages 2–6 per variant: multi_isppa_pipeline (acoustic, one thermal job per target, summary) per variant: async_transducer_pipeline (stage 0, acoustic per transducer, combine and joint per sweep point) Variant outputs <variant affix>_desc-isppaNNN <variant affix>_desc-asyncJoint or _desc-asyncJointSjj Stage 7 one report per target one report per sweep point

On HPC, uncertainty_pipeline submits each variant's inner jobs itself. Job names carry the stage and variant (PRESTUS-u3-temp_high-mi2-thermal_isppa030_sub-001), the multi-ISPPA acoustic jobs wait for stage 1, and every report job waits for all the variants' jobs. Options for the inner pipeline (e.g. options.thermal_timelimit) pass through the options struct given to prestus_pipeline_start.

Not supported: sequential follow-up runs (options.sequential_configs) in nested mode, and a multi-ISPPA sweep with more than one coherent transducer (as without uncertainty). Both stop with an error before any job is submitted.

items.title: Resuming a Partial Run
items.text:
Re-run the same call. On HPC, a stage whose sentinel file exists is skipped and no scheduler dependency is created for it; only the missing stages are resubmitted. To rerun a stage, delete its sentinel file before resubmitting. With io.overwrite_files: 'always', stages 2–7 are always resubmitted (stage 1 still resumes from its cache); with 'force', stage 1 is resubmitted too. See Overwrite behaviour.

On the MATLAB platform there is no stage-level skip. Resumability relies on setting io.overwrite_files: 'never' in the base config (the shipped default is 'always'): each file write inside the pipeline is skipped if the file already exists, so a restarted run fast-forwards through completed steps file by file.

Sentinel files Stage Sentinel file Location 1, Preprocessing sub-NNN_<medium>_cropped_smoothed.mat <output_dir>/cache/ 2, Default sim sub-NNN_<medium><base>.csv <output_dir>/ 3, Temp-H sim sub-NNN_<medium><base>_desc-temphigh.csv <output_dir>/ 4, Temp-L sim sub-NNN_<medium><base>_desc-templow.csv <output_dir>/ 5, Trans-H sim sub-NNN_<medium><base>_desc-transhigh.csv <output_dir>/ 6, Trans-L sim sub-NNN_<medium><base>_desc-translow.csv <output_dir>/ 7, Report sub-NNN_<medium>_desc-uncertainty_report<base>.html <output_dir>/

In nested mode (above) the variants' inner pipelines apply their own per-stage checks, and each per-point report is skipped when its file exists.

items.title: HPC Usage
items.text:
When platform is 'slurm' or 'qsub', all seven jobs are submitted immediately using scheduler dependencies (--dependency=afterok for SLURM). Stages 2–6 depend on stage 1; stage 7 depends on all five simulation jobs. If stage 1 fails, all downstream jobs are cancelled (--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes). No MATLAB session is held open during execution.

Stages 1 and 7 (preprocessing and report) do not require a GPU and are submitted to the scheduler's default CPU queue. Stages 2–6 inherit the GPU resources from the base config. To override the queue for CPU stages use options.stage1_partition = 'gpu' and options.report_partition = 'gpu'.

Job names and dependencies

Job names are PRESTUS-u1-preproc_sub-XXX, PRESTUS-u<k>-sim-<variant>_sub-XXX for stages k = 2–6 (e.g. PRESTUS-u3-sim-temp_high_sub-001) and PRESTUS-u7-report_sub-XXX.

This requires that hpc_submit_job supports the parameters.hpc.depend_job_id (single) and parameters.hpc.depend_job_ids (array) fields; see doc_hpc.md.

items.title: Pseudo-CT Runs
items.text:
With pct.enabled: 1, only the default variant maps the skull from the pseudo-CT. The four bound variants use the same head geometry (preprocessing and grid caches) but give the skull layer the homogeneous values of their medium file. The brain and thermal bounds apply as in other runs. The skull_cortical and skull_trabecular layers are never mapped from the pseudo-CT.

The range then compares the pseudo-CT skull with homogeneous skulls at the ITRUSST bounds. It brackets the default only where the mapped skull properties lie within those bounds, and it does not express the uncertainty of the pseudo-CT transform itself. Mapped values can fall largely outside the bounds, so check them before interpreting the range:

  • The uncertainty report's Pseudo-CT Skull vs. Bounds section plots the default run's skull density, sound speed and attenuation (or a prediction, when they are not cached) against the band of the bound variants' skull values and states the share of voxels outside it.
  • Before simulating, pct_predict_skull_properties or Predict skull properties on the Nexus Pseudo-CT sub-tab predicts the modelled skull properties. The Nexus shows the default run's values instead when they exist.
parameters = load_parameters('config_study.yaml');
parameters.subject_id = 1;
stats = pct_predict_skull_properties(parameters);  % writes cache/sub-001_<medium>_pct_prediction.json
stats.properties.sound_speed                        % mapped skull sound speed: mean, percentiles, histogram
stats.bounds                                        % skull values of each bound variant

The prediction applies the configured pct.mapping_* to the skull voxels of the head-preprocessing cache when it exists (stats.source = 'grid', as modelled), else of pseudoCT.nii.gz and tissues_mask.nii.gz before cropping, resampling and smoothing ('native').

References

The variant bounds are the lower and upper values of the ITRUSST tissue property table (in preparation) and the property directions of its one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis. Sources cited in the table for the bounds include:

  • Aubry, J.-F., et al. ITRUSST consensus on biophysical safety for transcranial ultrasound stimulation. Brain Stimulation 18, 1896–1905 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brs.2025.10.007 (safety limits of the report)
  • Aubry, J.-F. et al. Benchmark problems for transcranial ultrasound simulation: Intercomparison of compressional wave models. J Acoust Soc Am 152, 1003–1019 (2022). https://doi.org/10.1121/10.0013426 (skull reference values).
  • Lyons, M. E., & Parker, K. J. Absorption and attenuation in soft tissues. II. Experimental results. IEEE Trans Ultrason Ferroelectr Freq Control 35, 511–521 (1988). https://doi.org/10.1109/58.4189 (lower brain attenuation and absorption).
  • White, P. J., Clement, G. T., & Hynynen, K. Longitudinal and shear mode ultrasound propagation in human skull bone. Ultrasound Med Biol 32, 1085–1096 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2006.03.015 (lower skull attenuation, upper skull absorption).
